paragraph_context: The chemical prelimithiation method is to employ lithium-based organic solvents with a strong reducing ability.[81,128-142] Common organic lithium solvents include $n$ -butyl lithium,[140] lithium-naphthalene (Li-Naph),[129,137-139] lithium-biphenyl (LiBiph),[131,133-136,142] Li-Biph derivatives,[128,132,141] and new organic compound of lithium have been developed.[130] In the early, Scott et al. demonstrated that the initial irreversible capacity of carbon black electrode can be almost eliminated by the chemical pretreatment with the $n$ -butyl lithium, which is ascribed to the formation of a stable SEI layer. Compared to $n$ -butyl lithium, the Li Naph, Li-Biph/tetrahydrofuran (THF), Li-butyl methyl ether (LiBME), and Li-dimethoxyethane (Li-DME) are stable in ambientair (Figure 8a).[137] These prelimithiation solutions have been reported in Si,[133,137,138] S,[137] P,[131,136] HC,[135] Sn,[134] and Al.[143] However, the high potential $(0.3 - 0.5\mathrm{V}$ vs $\mathrm{Li} / \mathrm{Li}^{+})$ of these organolithium compounds blocks lithium-ion to insert into anode materials such as graphite, Si, and $\mathrm{SiO}_x$ [130] Zhang et al. successfully applied a novel organolithium compound, Li-9,9-dimethyl $9H$ fluorene-tetrahydrofuran with low redox potential of $\approx 0.2$ V (vs $\mathrm{Li} / \mathrm{Li}^{+}$ ), to prelithiate the $\mathrm{SiO}_x$ anode (Figure 8b), which leads to a remarkable increase in the initial coulombic efficiency (ICE) from $61.1\%$ to $87.1\%$ for the assembled full cell (Figure 8c), as well as a high capacity retention of $80\%$ after 100 cycles at $0.5C.$ [130] In addition, Jang et al. introduced electron-donating methyl groups in the benzene ring to decrease the electron-affinity and reduction potential ( $\approx 0.2\mathrm{V}$ ) (Figure 8d-f).[132] Recently, Li-Biph/2-methyl tetrahydrofuran (2-Me-THF) solvent was reported to reduce the redox potential of Li-Biph to $0.08\mathrm{V}$ , which can prelithiate the graphite anode in a controllable way (Figure 8g).[128] At the same time Choi et al. pointed out that the weakly solvating solvents (Li-Biph/2-Me-THF solvent) can prevent the formation of free solvated ions and insertion into graphite (Figure 8h).[81] Ideally, an effective chemically prelithiation method could be achieved with well optimized reaction conditions. However, reaction conditions such as high potential and environmental requirement, further limit the application scope. Therefore, large-scale commercial production remains a challenge.

paragraph_context: Briefly speaking, the cathode prelithiation strategy is to add extra active lithium on cathode, which can diffuse into the anode during the initial charging process, thus compensating for the initial irreversible capacity loss of the anode. A comprehensive overview of cathode prelithiation strategies of LIBs are concluded in Table 3. Compared with the high-input and high-activity anode prelithiation strategy, the cathode prelithiation strategy is safer and can be effectively combined with the commercial lithium-ion battery manufacturing process, which is more convenient for large-scale applications. In general, there are two routes, one is to utilize high capacity prelithiation additives, the other one is to increase the content of active lithium in cathode materials (so-called over-lithiation).

paragraph_context: In general, cathode prelithiation additives ought to have sufficient lithium contribution capacity (Figure 10a). The corresponding delithiation potential platform should be lower than the charge cut-off potential of the traditional cathode. paragraph_context: Ternary lithium-rich compounds, such as $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CuO}_2$ (320-340 mAh g $^{-1}$ ),[153] $\mathrm{Li}_5\mathrm{FeO}_4$ (764 mAh g $^{-1}$ ),[41,84,160-165] $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{NiO}_2$ (340 mAh g $^{-1}$ ),[154-157] $\mathrm{Li}_6\mathrm{CoO}_4$ (318 mAh g $^{-1}$ ),[158,159] $\mathrm{LiVO}_3$ (318 mAh g $^{-1}$ ),[183,184] $\mathrm{Li}_8\mathrm{ZrO}_6$ (550 mAh g $^{-1}$ )[185] can also be used as prelithiation additive. However, lithium ions cannot be fully released, not to mention the poor stability in ambient air. In addition, the alkaline nature of side products when being exposed to air will result in poor stability of the cathode slurry.[186] To improve the air stability of the ternary cathode prelithiation additives, coating the surface with a good air stability material is a good choice. The active oxygen $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ from the NiO impurity phase on the surface of $\mathrm{LiNiO}_2$ , combined with $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ in air results in the generation of $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ and $\mathrm{LiOH}$ [187] leading to the rapid electrochemical performance degradation of the battery. In addition, Kim et al.[155] dissolved Al iso-propoxide in ethanol, and mixed with $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{NiO}_2$ followed by a drying process. The obtained $\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3@\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{NiO}_2$ exhibits a charge capacity of 420 mAh g $^{-1}$ (Figure 12a) and shows no capacity decrease even af ter the exposure to air (relative humidity was $40\%$ ) continuously for $7\mathrm{h}$ .When $4\mathrm{wt}\% \mathrm{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}@\mathrm{Li}_{2}\mathrm{NiO}_{2}$ was added to $\mathrm{LiCoO}_2$ ,the irreversible capacity of the $\mathrm{Li^{+}}$ cell was decreased (Figure 12b). But the specific capacities of $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{NiO}_2$ $\mathrm{Li_2CuO_2}$ $\mathrm{Li_6CoO_4}$ ,and $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CuO}_2$ are relatively low (under $400\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ ), so they may not be suitable for the novel high-capacity anodes as the cathode prelithiation additives. The theoretical capacity of $\mathrm{Li}_5\mathrm{FeO}_4$ (LFO) is $867\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ .In 2016, Su et al.[162] synthesized $\mathrm{Li}_5\mathrm{FeO}_4$ by a solid-state solution in an argon-filled glove box. The pure $\mathrm{Li}_5\mathrm{FeO}_4$ electrode in a half cell shows a charge capacity over $700\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $4.3\mathrm{V}$ and lithium could not insert reversely during the discharge in the initial cycle. They added $7 \%$ LFO in $\mathrm{LiCoO}_2$ cathode as the prelithiation reagent, and the reversible specific capacity of the $7 \%$ LFO@ $\mathrm{LiCoO}_2 / / \mathrm{HC}$ battery increases $14 \%$ than the raw electrode. Besides, the corresponding capacity retention improves more than $5 \%$ after 50 cycles. Moreover, the energy density of the $7 \%$ LFO@ $\mathrm{LiCoO}_2 / / \mathrm{HC}$ battery increases from $\approx 300$ to $\approx 400\mathrm{Wh}$ $\mathrm{kg^{-1}}$ (Figure 12c). However, owing to the extremely poor air stability and low electrical conductivity, it is hard for LFO to be incorporated in the practical productions. To improve the air stability of LFO, Li et al.[84] coated LFO with $\mathrm{Li}_6\mathrm{CoO}_4$ by a high temperature solid-state reaction (Figure 12d). The coated $\mathrm{Li}_6\mathrm{CoO}_4@\mathrm{LFO}$ exhibits enhanced air stability (almost no changes when exposed to air for $60\mathrm{min}$ ). In addition, $\mathrm{Li_6CoO_4@LFO}$ cathode delivers a high capacity of $736.6\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at the initial charge (Figure 12e,f). The NCM811//Graphite cell with $5\mathrm{wt}\%$ $\mathrm{Li_6CoO_4@LFO}$ cathode additive delivers an improved reversible specific capacity (increased by $38.5\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ ) (Figure 12g). Although the air stability was improved by coating $\mathrm{Li}_6\mathrm{CoO}_4$ , LFO still could not meet the practical application due to its low electrical conductivity, and thus Lee et al.[163] synthesized $\mathrm{Li}_5\mathrm{FeO}_4 / \mathrm{CNT}$ composites by a facile solid-state method. The $\mathrm{Li}_5\mathrm{FeO}_4 / \mathrm{CNT}$ composites show small particle size morphology (200-400 nm) and high elec trical conductivity properties (1.71 S cm $^{-1}$ ) (Figure 12h,i). However, a series of problems such as residual reaction products, poor air stability, and poor reaction kinetics, which severely hinder the practical application of ternary lithium-rich compounds as cathode prelithiation reagents. Future research should focus on stabilizing surface or introducing inert materials to improve the air stability and the corresponding compatibility with organic solvents of ternary lithium-rich compounds. Furthermore, materials with good electrical conductivity should be applied to improve the electrical conductivity of ternary lithium-rich compounds, and advanced in situ characterization methods should be explored to illuminate the instant side reactions between the residual reaction products from ternary lithium-rich compounds and the electrolyte.

paragraph_context: Binary lithium-rich compounds can provide more lithium ions than ternary lithium-rich compounds. The binary lithium-rich compounds typically include Li-N, Li-O, Li-S, and Li-P compounds. $\mathrm{Li}_3\mathrm{N}$ was regarded as one of the most promising cathodes prelithiation materials due to its high specific capacity of $2300\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ (based on the reaction formula: $2\mathrm{Li}_3\mathrm{N}\rightarrow 6\mathrm{Li}^+ +6\mathrm{e}^- +\mathrm{N}_2)$ .[120,166-169] Park et al.[166] firstly reported $\mathrm{Li}_3\mathrm{N}$ as a sacrificial source of lithium-ion the initial charge of $\mathrm{LiCoO_2}$ cathode. However, the high chemical activity and poor compatibility with NMP hinder the practical application of $\mathrm{Li}_3\mathrm{N}$ , which is worsened by its electrical insulating nature and the $\mathbf{N}_2$ release during cycling.[166,167] Follow-up investigators have made great efforts to solve problems.[167,169,188] As for Li-O compounds, although the high charging platform hinders their exertion. $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O}_2$ can be catalyzed by transition metals (Ni, Co, Mn) to offset the irreversible capacity loss of anodes.[170-172] Abouimrane et al.[170] verified that the activation degree of $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O}$ depends on the activation current density, the type of electrolyte salt, and the type of anode. The above-mentioned Li-N and Li-O compounds usually generate gases (such as $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{N}_2$ ) during charging. Although the gas can be released before the encapsulation of battery, the poor physical contact between cathode active materials after the gas escape should be considered. Moreover, the introduction of these prelithiation additives could increase the impedance and reduce the electrochemical performance of the battery by resulting in the electrolyte decomposition (Figure 13a).[170] Adding the prelithiation additives on cathode surface seems an effective method to minimize the deterioration of the cathode, but the low electronic and ionic conductivity production on the cathode surface after charging hinder the interfacial charge transfer. To further promotes the practical utilization of the above-mentioned prelithiation materials, surface coating could be an effective way to improve its air stability, electronic and ionic conductivity.

paragraph_context: $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{S}$ has a specific capacity of as high as $1166\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ [173] and a decomposition potential of $3.5\mathrm{V},$ [189] which indicates that $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{S}$ can be used as a cathode prelithiation additive. However, the inherent low electronic conductivity of sulfide requires a suitable electronic enhancer. label: 材料制备
paragraph_context: Recently, over-lithiated cathode materials were reported to improve the initial columbic efficiency, which indicates the overlithiated cathode can play a role in supplementing the undesired lithium loss. The over-lithiated cathode can be obtained by improving the stoichiometric ratio of lithium with chemical or electrochemical methods. Accurately, additional lithium can be intercalated into lithium vacancies of cathode materials by chem- ical or electrochemical methods. The additional lithium was released during the initial charging, while hardly intercalated into the cathode material during subsequent cycles due to kinetic constraints, which ensures the extra released active lithium supplemented the lithium loss during charging process in the initial cycle.

paragraph_context: Empty octahedral site of spinel-type $\mathrm{LiMn_2O_4}$ [199-201] and $\mathrm{LiNi_{0.5}Mn_{1.5}O_4}$ [87,202-208] can store additional lithium ions. label: 概述
paragraph_context: In the past few years, prelithiation strategies have been widely studied to put forward the commercialization of high-specific-capacity anode materials for high energy density LIBs. Regrettably, there are still no mature prelithiation strategies which can fully tackle the initial capacity loss issues. In this paper, we reviewed the research progress of anode prelithiation strategy and cathode prelithiation strategy ever reported, and systematically summarized and evaluated the challenges and advantages of anode prelithiation strategy and cathode prelithiation strategies including the controllability, cost-effectiveness, prelithiation capacity, safety and stability, industrial compatibility, as shown in Figure 17.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Research efforts have focused on increasing the energy density by the anode and cathode prelithiation technologies, but little attention has been paid to the negative impacts and challenges, including the prelithiation residuals, the chemical and air stability, the electrochemical stability, safety problems, etc.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The anode prelithiation strategy is more suitable for anode materials that requires high-capacity lithium supplementation. Lithium foil prelithiation and SLMPP are more suitable for fast and efficient prelithiation process. There exist some issues in controlling the rate, uniformity, and degree of lithium foil prelithiation. Incipient over-lithiation often occurs due to the use of thick lithium foil without means of adjustment. Thermal runaway must therefore be investigated and monitored. The storage of lithium foil and removal of excess lithium foil will increase the production cost of lithium foil prelithiation and hinder its future large-scale commercialization. In the future, it is necessary to adopt more precise technological means to control the thickness of lithium foil. SLMPP and lithium alloy powders prelithiation have the advantage of uniformity and controlled degree of prelithiation. However, their high chemical activity results in the incompatibility with common solvents and can lead to serious safety hazards. Therefore, effective structural design and modification strategies are required to further improve their stability.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The chemical prelithiation method at the anode can control the prelithiation level by optimizing the reaction conditions (such as concentration and reaction time) of the prelithiation reagents. However, the deep prelithiation of anode materials places strict requirements on the prelithiation reagents (sufficiently low redox potential). And inert organic residuals may affect the formation and chemical stability of SEI. This limits the range of applications. In the future, the aim is to develop organic compounds that are more compatible, easier to clean, less expensive, and easier to be synthesized.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The electrochemical prelimithiation method on the anode can precisely control the degree of prelimithiation and adjust the formation and composition of the SEI by introducing external circuits and appropriate electrolyte additives (such as FEC). However, the scale of practical applications is challenging due to complex circuit assembly, and extremely high inert conditions.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In occasions where safety and process compatibility are more emphasized and the demand for lithium replenishment capacity is not high, cathode prelithiation strategies are usually more appropriate. The cathode prelithiation materials will result in the release of gases, inert residuals, solutes in the electrolyte, severe volume changes, and substantial structural changes, culminating in impedance rise, which may affect the rate capability, the cycling stability, and reduce energy density of LIBs. There is a lack of in-depth understanding of these problems. Therefore, their effect on the cathode needs to be further explored in the future work (including electron and ion dynamics transport of the cathode prelithiation in LIBs). So far, most of the literature reports have only evaluated the electrochemical properties of prelithiated cathode materials in coin-type half cells, it is urgent to evaluate them in commercial-level-capacity LIBs (including the long cycle stability and high-rate performance). The industry is focusing on the cost-effectiveness, scalability, safety, product stability, controllability, and prelithiation capability and efficiency of the cathode prelithiation. Therefore, it is imperative to develop cathode prelithiation additives with air-stable (stabilizing surface passivation or introducing inert materials), safe and simple preparation method, higher lithium storage capacity (more than $400\mathrm{mAh}$ $\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ ), less residue and scalable (e.g., roll-to-roll production process and spraying process).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: At present, the industrialization of prelithiation is still at an experimental stage. Battery manufacturers have to put invest into new equipment and process procedures, and strictly control en vironmental conditions. The challenges faced by battery suppliers are: (1) Strict humidity and temperature control: the cathode prelithiation strategy and the anode prelithiation strategy processes are very sensitive to moisture and oxygen, which requires extremely low water and oxygen levels from the beginning of prelithiation to the end of battery sealing; (2) Battery management system (BMS) upgrade: the anode prelithiation strategy and the cathode prelithiation strategy can change the battery voltage, and extent the cycle life of the battery, which is a challenge to accurately assess the state of health and state of charge of each battery cell. Therefore, a large database of prelithiated batteries using different methods needs to be established to evaluate different states of charge and health; (3) Thermal runaway monitoring: the anode prelithiation strategy and the cathode prelithiation strategy can increase the possibility of local over-lithiated and even generate lithium dendrites, which will lead to short circuit inside the battery. The prelithiation process involves a large transfer of lithium ions, which is a heat dissipation process. This will have a certain degree of impact on batteries, electrodes, and electrode materials. Therefore, it is necessary to add a cooling device and a thermal runaway management system to the prelithiation process.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: At present, there are few studies on electrolyte prelithiation. Generally, stabilizers are added during the electrochemical prelithiation process to promote the formation of CEI and SEI. High-voltage, high-stability electrolytes need to be developed to match the prelithiation process or to contain high concentration lithium salt alone for electrolyte prelithiation.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Up to now, the mechanism of evolution and the principle of action of the additional lithium sources in full cells is not clear. Research and development staff need to further investigate the structural changes, dynamic properties, and morphological evolution of the additional lithium sources using in situ X-ray, electron, neutron, optical and scanning probes.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In summary, anode and cathode prelithiation strategies are crucial for the development of next-generation LIBs with high-capacity anodes. We review the issues related to anode prelithiation strategy and cathode prelithiation and propose future improvement directions. In the future, in-depth mechanism analyzing methods should be developed for clarifying the mechanism of prelithiation and its impact on the performance of full batteries, so as to promote the large-scale development of prelithiation technologies. Furthermore, this review can also provide a reference for the Na-ion, K-ion, lithium-free battery systems.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Electrospun is a unique technique for the fabrication of multiscale structured nanofibers (MSNFs), which can be used as functional units for improving the performance of lithium-based batteries. This review systematically examines how MSNFs, including core-shell, hollow porous, multichannel, wire-in-tube, tube-in-tube, and hierarchical nanofibers, effectively improve battery performance as components in lithium-based batteries. The application of aforementioned MSNFs and their chemical modification contributes to the development of lithium-based batteries with high energy density and enhanced safety when used as electrodes, separators, and electrolytes. Specifically, MSNFs are used to derive electrodes and electrolytes that improve electron/ion transfer rates, increase the utilization ratio of active materials, suppress dendrite growth, and mitigate volume expansion, enabling fast and stable electrochemical reactions at the electrodes. Additionally, MSNFs-derived separators, which feature more ion transport channels, exceptional mechanical properties, and the capability to inhibit thermal runaway, are also discussed. Finally, the challenges and prospective pathways for electrospun technology in the application of lithium-based batteries are reviewed.

label: 理化性质
paragraph_context: As the energy density of conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) approaches its theoretical limits, alternative negative electrode materials are being explored, such as transition metal negatives with stable structures and the "holy grail" lithium metal Key Lab for Special Functional Materials of Ministry of Education Collaborative Innovation Center of Nano Functional Materials and with a low electrochemical potential $(-3.04\mathrm{V}$ vs standard hydrogen electrode), high specific capacity $(3860\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1})$ and low density $(0.59\mathrm{gcm})$ [1-3] which promises to increase the energy density of batteries. In addition, lithium metal shows potential for use in next generation lithium-sulfur batteries[4] (LSBs) and lithium-oxygen batteries[5] (LOBs) for high energy storage applications. However, challenges such as uncontrolled lithium dendrite growth and volume expansion during cycling[6,7] necessitate the introduction of effective lithium carriers. Traditional lithium-based batteries electrodes suffer from limited surface area and porosity, restricting the loading of active materials and thereby impacting battery energy and power densities. Moreover, poor interface stability between the electrolyte and electrode leads to uneven electrolyte infiltration and formation of an unstable solid electrolyte interface (SEI), affecting battery cycle and safety performance. Similarly, conventional separator materials face limitations in ion transfer rates and mechanical properties, constraining charge/discharge rates, safety, and cycle durability of batteries.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Electrospun is a simple and versatile technique to produce nanofibers compared to other methods such as self-assembly,[8] templating,[9] and phase separation.[10] It can fabricate fibers with diameters ranging from micrometers to nanometers and lengths from centimeters to meters, bridging the micro and macro worlds. By adjusting process parameters, electrospun facilitates the design of one-dimensional (1D) nanofibers into MSNFs. Their nanostructure endows MSNFs with unique features, including an abundance of active sites and defects, intricate secondary structures, and remarkable flexibility. These characteristics, combined with high porosity, uniform ionic flux, substantial internal space, and mechanical strength, as well as the ability to integrate functional groups, render MSNFs suitable for various applications in lithium-based batteries, such as self-supporting framework electrodes, separators, gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs), and polymer solid electrolytes (PSEs), as depicted in Figure 1, holding the promise as lithium-based battery materials for better performance.[11-13] Electrospun enables the simple, economical, and efficient preparation of various 1D nanofibers with high length-to-diameter ratios, large specific surface areas, controllable In this review, we highlight the versatile roles of electrospun MSNFs as battery component for lithium-based batteries, with a focus on the relationship between the structure of MSNFs and battery performance. Different from the previous reviews those concentrated on the introduction of the preparation and morphology of electrospun nanofibers, as well as their application in solid-state batteries or various metal-based batteries, in this paper, we delineate the relationship between MSNFs structure/materials and functionality, and the pivotal role of electrospun MSNFs in enhancing energy and power densities, cycle life, and the safety of lithium-based batteries is discussed.

label: 材料制备
paragraph_context: MSNFs prepared by electrospun are formed based on the uniaxial stretching of viscoelastic solutions. The preparation apparatus is similar to the original electrospun setup, and the basic principles remain the same. As schematically illustrated in Figure 3a, the electrospun device is typically consist of a syringe containing the precursor solution, a syringe pump controlling the flow rate, various specialized spinneret needles, fiber collectors, and a DC high-voltage power supply. Under high voltage, the surface of the precursor solution droplet becomes charged, generating electrostatic forces. When the electrostatic forces counterbalance the surface tension, the droplet at the needle tip forms a conical shape known as a "Taylor cone." As the voltage is further increased and the electrostatic force exceeds the surface tension, a straight jet is emitted from the tip of the Taylor cone. After ejection, solvent evaporation and charge dissipation render the jet unstable, leading to jet thinning and the formation of numerous fine jets. The whipping jet, continuously extended by electrostatic repulsion, moves toward the collector, where further solvent evaporation and solidification occur. The curved and unstable jet undergoes multiple stretches, forming continuous nanofibers on the collector.[17,18] Due to the complexity of quantifying the diameter and orientation of nanofibers, MSNFs can be prepared through the design of spinnerets and collectors[19] and by altering precursor components. The presence of these special structures imparts unique properties to the nanofibers, significantly improving their performance in lithium-based batteries.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The morphology, structure, and performance of electrospun nanofibers primarily depend on three factors: precursor solution characteristics, process parameters (e.g., voltage, flow rate, needle-collector distance), environmental conditions (e.g., temperature, humidity), and post-treatment methods (e.g., calcination, hot pressing, soaking).[20,21] This paper focuses mainly on solution electrospun.

DC voltage $(10 - 20\mathrm{kV})$ ensures continuous fibers, while high AC voltage $(1 - 10\mathrm{kV})$ may cause bead formation but can produce longer fibers. For instance, modifying the working distance alters the electric field strength (Equation (2)) and the distribution of electric flux lines, thereby influencing the fiber morphology. Optimal feed rates are essential; high rates cause bead formation, while lower rates produce finer fibers. Common collectors like metal foils and rotating drums help create aligned, flexible nanofibers.[25] $$ E = V / H \tag {2} $$ Ambient humidity significantly impacts electrospinning. High humidity leads to water condensation on fiber surfaces, forming pores and weakening mechanical properties, resulting in bead structures.[26] It also causes incomplete solvent volatilization, leading to irregular fiber shapes.[27] Maintaining humidity below a critical threshold is essential. Elevated temperature reduces viscosity and fiber diameter but excessive heat can cause thermal degradation. Introducing vertical airflow helps counter electrostatic forces and enhances fiber deposition.[28] Spinnerets are essential in the manufacture of MSNFs via electrospun, the design of spinning needles significantly influences the structure and morphology of electrospun MSNFs. Single-channel needles typically produce simple, uniform fibers, while coaxial needles enable the formation of core-shell structures, enhancing functional integration by allowing different materials to be combined within a single fiber. Tri-channel and triple-coaxial needles further advance this complexity, facilitating the creation of fibers with multiple layers or channels. Following calcination, these can form grape-like, wire-in tube, tube-in-tube, bamboo-like and multichannel nanofibers (Figure 3b), which can be tailored for specific functions such as enhanced ion transport, mechanical stability, or controlled porosity. These advanced needle designs allow for greater control over fiber architecture, enabling the development of fibers with customized properties for specific applications, though they also introduce challenges in terms of fabrication consistency and scalability.

paragraph_context: As the heating rate increases during the carbonization stage, the temperature gradient remains sufficient to form an additional dense shell, resulting in the formation of tube-in-tube nanostructures. These structures exhibit distinct transmission efficiencies and catalytic sites across different layers, making them ideal as electrode support materials for lithium-based batteries. The unique tubular 1D structure enhances the chemical and physical properties, significantly improving lithium storage capacity and overall electrochemical performance.[55,56] The tube-in-tube design provides multiple protective layers around the active material. label: 概述
paragraph_context: Hierarchical designs combine the advantages of both microscale and nanoscale structures, working synergistically to enhance the performance of high-energy-density lithium-based batteries. By integrating features across these scales, such designs improve ion and electron transport, provide ample active sites for reactions, and ensure structural stability during cycling. Li et al.[39] developed hierarchical nanofibers that, after thermal treatment, formed grape-like graded carbon hollow fibers. When applied as positive electrodes in lithium-sulfur batteries (LSBs), these fibers create nanoscale reaction chambers and a conductive network, enabling high sulfur capacity and excellent cyclic stability. The titanium monoxide layer within the fibers helps prevent polysulfide dissolution, further enhancing the electrode's performance.

paragraph_context: MSNFs can significantly enhance the battery performance through integrating structural engineering, interfacial engineering, and chemical modification techniques. Figure 5 vividly illustrates the distinct differences between common host materials and MSNFs when used as positive electrode, negative electrode, and separator in lithium-based batteries. As the positive electrode host, MSNFs enable higher active material loading, increased active sites, and effectively mitigate volume expansion during the charging and discharging process.[57] The MSNFs-based negative electrode enhances ion flow, enabling high-rate lithium batteries, while their uniform ion flow and well-distributed nucleation sites prevent dendrite growth.[58] Additionally, as functional separators, MSNFs offer enhanced porosity for faster ion transport[59] and can incorporate flame-retardant materials to prevent thermal runaway, thereby improving battery safety.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Based on their compositional characteristics, MSNFs are categorized into carbonized, non-carbonized, and composite nanofibers. Figure 3d further details the inherent advantages and exceptional performance of MSNFs in battery applications. Through improvements in energy density, charge/discharge rates, lifespan, and scalability, nanofiber-based lithium battery technology makes a significant contribution to meet the growing demand for energy storage solutions. This technology is especially critical for achieving high-performance batteries in key areas such as renewable energy, electric vehicles, and portable electronics. This section will systematically detail the applications of MSNFs in positive electrodes, negative electrodes, separators, gel electrolytes, and solid-state electrolytes.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The challenges faced by unconventional lithium-based negative electrodes, including issues like lithium dendrite formation, expansion of volume, and reduced coulombic efficiency (CE), have been addressed through various approaches. Researchers have focused on adjusting electrolyte composition to form a stable SEI,[60] developing artificial SEI layers,[61] using solid state electrolytes (SSEs),[62] and constructing advanced negative electrode host.[63] However, altering electrolyte composition or creating artificial SEI has proven ineffective in halting lithium dendrite growth.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In contrast, MSNFs, which constructed through the rational coordination of the chemical composition and spatial nanostructure, as negative electrode host have emerged as a promising solution. This section will explore MSNFs used in LIBs negative electrodes, including conversion-type, intercalation-type, alloy-type, and conversion-alloy-type MSNFs host with high theoretical capacities and excellent stability. These materials offer new possibilities for enhancing battery energy density and cycle stability through various energy storage mechanisms. Additionally, for LMBs negative electrodes, we will discuss a range of innovative MSNFs host designs, such as standard carbonized MSNFs, heteroatom-doped MSNFs, lithium-affinity seed-embedded MSNFs, composite-enhanced MSNFs, and heterostructure interface-driven MSNFs. Although MSNFs have shown significant improvements in electrochemical performance as LIB negative electrodes, the challenges remain. paragraph_context: The positive electrode of high energy density lithium-based batteries face challenges such as cycling stability, safety. To address these issues, an excellent positive electrode material must possess high conductivity and a stable structure. MSNFs, when used as positive electrodes host, offer the potential to overcome these challenges by enhancing the transport rates of electrons and ions and increasing the utilization of active materials, thereby improving battery performance.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: Over the years, extensive research on insertion-type lithium transition metal oxide positive electrode materials has steadily increased the energy density of batteries.[104] However, the energy density of these positive electrodes is nearing its limit. As a result, researchers have designed positive electrode materials with multiscale structures and explored multi-electron redox materials, such as elemental sulfur, which offer excellent electrochemical reversibility and high theoretical energy density.[105] MSNFs as a host for sulfur provides high specific surface area,[106] conductivity, and porosity, which help increase the loading of sulfur catalytic materials and electrochemically active substances. This structure also mitigates the volume expansion of sulfur positive electrodes, thereby enhancing the energy density and cycling stability of the battery.[107] Moreover, CNFs effectively prevent the dissolution and migration of sulfur materials, suppressing the "shuttle effect" of polysulfides and improving the electrochemical performance of LSBs.[108] The large specific surface area of MSNFs increases active sites, the small diameter shortens ion transport paths, and the high-efficiency 1D electron transport along the longitudinal direction offers the potential to achieve high-energy-density, high-capacity, and long-cycle lithium-based batteries.

paragraph_context: MSNFs significantly enhance the performance of LSBs through several mechanisms. Their porous and hollow structures capture lithium polysulfides (LiPSs), suppressing the shuttle effect and improving cycle stability. The high surface area and active sites of MSNFs boost sulfur redox reactions, while catalytic materials like TiN or Co accelerate the conversion of LiPSs, enhancing overall electrochemical kinetics. Additionally, their hollow structures mitigate volume expansion, reducing mechanical stress and extending cycle life. Doped with conductive materials, MSNFs form continuous conductive networks that improve electron and ion transport, enhancing rate performance. Their hierarchical structures allow high sulfur loading while maintaining structural integrity, increasing capacity and cycling stability.

paragraph_context: Titanium-Based MSNFs Host: The excellent catalytic capabilities of titanium-based heterostructures facilitate the adsorption, diffusion, and redox conversion of LiPSs. By compositing TiO or TiN into carboned MSNFs to positive electrode host via electrospun, the large surface area and strong chemical interactions between these polar bonds and LiPSs[125] can promote the rapid conversion between sulfur and LiPSs,[126] thereby suppressing the shuttle effect.[127] TiN not only effectively stabilizes polysulfides through the polar Ti-S and N-S bonds but also enhances redox reactions due to its outstanding catalytic properties. Huang et al.[128] successfully synthesized a carbon/titanium nitride (TiN/C) composite nanofiber with a biomimetic root-like structure using a single-needle electrospun technique combined with high-temperature ammonia calcination. This material serves as a self-supporting framework for high sulfur-loading positive electrodes. The TiN/C matrix features a 3D porous interconnected structure that mimics the morphology of plant root systems, providing efficient channels for the transport of polysulfides, electrons, and electrolytes. Just as plant roots absorb water and oxygen from the soil and efficiently deliver these nutrients throughout the plant via a complex network system, the TiN/C matrix facilitates the transport and conversion of key species in electrochemical reactions through its unique structural advantages (Figure 13a). Even with a sulfur loading of $10.5\mathrm{mgcm}^{-2}$ , the battery delivers a high capacity of $790\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ (Figure 13b). Zhang et al.[129] proposed a "three-region" strategy for fabricating integrated positive electrodes for LSBs. The middle region (TN-CNFs) consists of CNFs loaded with TiN nanocrystals, providing polar adsorption sites to catalyze redox processes and flexible highways for ion and electron transport (Figure 13c). It offers a high gravimetric energy density at a sulfur loading of $10.7\mathrm{mgcm}^{-2}$ (Figure 13d).

While MSNFs have improved sulfur-based electrodes in LSBs, the challenges remain. Long-term stability is affected by material degradation over extended cycling, leading to capacity loss. High sulfur loading poses difficulties in maintaining uniform distribution and avoiding agglomeration without compromising conductivity. Additionally, at high current densities, suppressing the polysulfide shuttle effect becomes more challenging. Furthermore, stronger chemical binding and advanced heterostructures are needed to trap LiPSs and mitigate the shuttle effect under high-rate conditions. The resulting GPEs, with its rich porosity and 3D hierarchical nanostructure, was easily wetted and absorbed by the electrolyte, achieving a high ionic conductivity of $9.44\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{Scm}^{-1}$ and a $\mathrm{Li^{+}}$ transference number of 0.66. Sun et al.[197] added $\mathrm{Li}_{1.3}\mathrm{Al}_{0.3}\mathrm{Ti}_{1.7}(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (LATP), known for its high ionic conductivity and stability in air, to PVDF-HFP. The synergistic effect between the 3D network fibers and the in situ formed gel led to a significant enhancement in ionic conductivity, reaching up to $3.394~\mathrm{mS~cm^{-1}}$ . Zhang et al.[198] prepared a GPE matrix using electrospun and soaking methods with PVDF-HFP as the main component, which exhibited high ionic conductivity $(1.27\times 10^{3}\mathrm{S~cm}^{-1})$ and excellent affinity for liquid electrolytes.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In a nutshell, GPEs show great promise for lithium-based batteries, offering high ionic conductivity, mechanical stability, and strong interfacial affinity. Electrospun nanofiber membranes, such as PEO and PVDF-based composites, enhance $\mathrm{Li^{+}}$ transport, suppress lithium dendrite growth, and improve electrolyte absorption. Recent advancements incorporate inorganic fillers like LLZTO and LATP, further boosting conductivity and structural integrity. However, achieving long-term stability, optimizing filler dispersion, and improving dendrite suppression remain challenges. Future GPE development should focus on enhancing safety and mechanical properties while ensuring compatibility with advanced lithium-based battery systems.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Currently, electrospun MSNFs, with diverse morphologies, structures, and chemical compositions, offer significant advantages across various components of lithium-based batteries, including positive electrodes, negative electrodes, separators, SSEs, and GPEs. The integration of MSNFs into lithium-based batteries offers promising improvements in both performance and safety. In the application in positive electrode, MSNFs not only enhance energy density and cycling stability by providing a high specific surface area and excellent conductivity but also increase active material loading and offer additional catalytic sites. In the application in negative electrode, MSNFs effectively buffer volume changes, maintaining electrode integrity during cycling by accommodating lithium expansion and contraction. Their high surface area and abundant active sites enhance lithium storage capacity and promote uniform lithium deposition. The interconnected structure enables rapid ion transport, improving charge/discharge rates and electron conductivity, while also suppressing dendrite growth through uniform ion flux regulation and the incorporation of lithiophilic materials. As separators, MSNFs exhibit high porosity and mechanical strength, improving ionic transport and thermal stability while enhancing battery safety. In SSEs, MSNFs improve ionic conductivity and electrochemical stability by incorporating high ionic conductivity fillers and ceramic nanofibers into polymer nanofibers. Finally, in GPEs, MSNFs address issues such as electrolyte leakage, swelling, and mechanical stability, thereby improving overall battery performance.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: MSNFs enable higher energy density, allowing more energy storage in smaller, lighter battery units, directly supporting growing energy demands in electric vehicles, portable electronics, and large-scale renewable energy storage systems. Enhanced charge/discharge rates support fast-charging infrastructure and high-power applications, addressing the needs of sectors like electric vehicles and grid-scale energy storage. Additionally, MSNFs-based batteries demonstrate extended cycle life and improved stability, reducing the need for frequent replacement. This longevity contributes to more sustainable and efficient energy storage solutions, minimizing environmental and resource impact. With recent advancements in scalable production techniques like high-throughput electrospun[199] and roll-to-roll processes,[200] nanofiber-based lithium batteries are poised to meet large-scale energy demands, making nanofiber technology a viable solution for widespread deployment in global energy storage systems.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: However, the surface of MSNFs electrode frameworks is not sufficiently smooth, which may hinder the formation of stable SEI and CEI during lithium-based batteries cycling. Moreover, previous research has not integrated the design of the electrode framework with the design of the electrode-electrolyte interface. A synergistic approach to both could potentially enhance the safety and stability of battery operation. Additionally, future applications of MSNFs in SSEs and GPEs could unlock significant advancements in battery technology. Unlike current composites of ordinary fibers, true MSNFs could enhance ionic conductivity through hierarchical pore structures, improve mechanical integrity with varied stiffness, and increase electrochemical stability by incorporating materials at different scales. Additionally, they could offer tailored interfacial properties, customizable architectures optimized for specific battery functions. Different layers or regions of the fiber structure are optimized for different functions, such as ion transport, mechanical support, and thermal management. Collectively, MSNFs have propelled the advancement of lithium-based batteries technology characterized by high energy density, enhanced safety, and long cycling endurance.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Despite the notable advantages of MSNFs in lithium-based batteries, several key challenges remain.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: I) The electrospun process for MSNFs has not yet achieved industrial-scale production efficiently, and the limitations in geometric freedom and scaffold morphology control in electrospun hinder the precise tailoring of nanofiber structures for specific applications.  II) MSNFs may reduce the packing density and volumetric energy density of electrodes, and the typical thickness of the lithium layer deposited onto the MSNFs framework often exceeds $50\mu \mathrm{m}$ , leading to excess lithium.  III) In the preparation of full cells with MSNFs-based electrodes in the laboratory, it is typically necessary to first deposit lithium metal onto the MSNFs host before assembling it with the positive electrode. Since molten lithium does not adequately wet the MSNFs structure and may even damage it, electrochemical deposition is commonly employed. However, this process must be conducted in an inert environment, and the cell must be disassembled before combining it with the positive electrode, rendering the procedure both complex and labor-intensive. Moreover, in practical applications such as the production of pouch or cylindrical cells, the electrochemical deposition of bulk lithium metal must be performed under low-oxygen and low-humidity conditions, which imposes stringent demands on engineering technology.  IV) Extensive specific surface area and large volume of the MSNFs will cause significant side reactions between lithium and the electrolyte, and the lithiumphobic surface of carbon-based materials can hinder the initial nucleation of lithium.[201]  V) Current electrospun technology struggles to produce nanofibers with diameters below $50~\mathrm{nm}$ consistently, and the evaporation of solvents can result in the emission of toxic gases, raising environmental concerns.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: To address the challenges associated with electrospun MSNFs in lithium-based batteries applications, future efforts will focus on several key areas.

Additionally, by controlling the deposition to achieve a thinner lithium layer, the practical application of these MSNFs-based electrodes can be significantly enhanced.  III) By controlling the deposition to achieve a thinner lithium layer, the practical application of these MSNFs-based electrodes can be significantly enhanced. label: 概述
paragraph_context: Keywords: lithium-ion battery | silicon-based anode | solid electrolyte interphase | thermal runaway | thermal safety Silicon-based anodes offer high capacity for next-generation lithium-ion batteries but face potential thermal safety concerns due to insufficient understanding of thermal runaway mechanisms. This review systematically analyzes thermal runaway mechanisms and mitigation strategies in silicon anode-based lithium-ion batteries. Discussions are conducted based on three materials categories of nano-silicon, micro-silicon, and silicon-carbon composite materials, highlighting their advantages and challenges. Thermal runaway features involved in reaction of SEI, reaction of $\mathrm{Si / Li}_x\mathrm{Si}$ , and chemical crosstalk are clearly revealed. Key mitigation strategies are summarized including interface modifications and electrolyte optimizations. The review provides a foundation for developing safe and high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), serving as the dominant power source for portable electronics, electric vehicles, and grid-scale energy storage systems, face ever-increasing demands for higher energy density—a key requirement to prolong their single-cycle operational duration to expand their application scenarios across diverse fields. Among the candidate anode materials, silicon (Si) has exceptionally high theoretical specific capacity (based on the $\mathrm{Li}_{15}\mathrm{Si}_{4}$ phase, $\sim 3579\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ ), promising for breaking the energy density ceiling imposed by conventional graphite anodes (theoretical capacity $\sim 372\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ [1-8]. However, Si-based materials undergo substantial volumetric expansion during lithiation and delithiation processes, which induces critical challenges. This includes particle pulverization, loss of electrical contact within the electrode matrix, and continuous rupture/reformation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) [9-12]. These issues collectively lead to severe structural degradation, which in turn leads to rapid capacity decay—a problem that has hindered the widespread commercial application of Si-based anodes.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Significant progress has been made in mitigating the cycling instability of Si-based anodes in the past 20 years [13]. Early research (primarily throughout the 2000s) focuses on nanostructural design (e.g., nanoparticles, nanowires), which alleviated particle fracturing during cycling by reducing stress accumulation during (de)lithiation and shortening ion diffusion pathways, thereby significantly enhancing rate capability [14-18]. These efforts demonstrate the fundamental feasibility of Si as an anode material. The subsequent decade witnesses the emergence of composite design strategies, particularly silicon-carbon (Si-C) architectures. The carbon matrix not only improves electrical conductivity but also provides a buffering framework to accommodate volume changes, thereby enhancing cyclic stability [19-21]. Concurrently, substantial progress is made in surface engineering techniques, such as the construction of artificial SEI layers and functional coatings, which improve interfacial stability and reduce irreversible lithium consumption and improved initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) loss [4, 22-24]. Furthermore, the adoption of advanced binders (e.g., self-healing polymers, conductive binders) significantly enhance the mechanical properties and structural integrity of electrodes, outperforming conventional polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based binders [25-27].

label: 概述
paragraph_context: These collective advances, coupled with the optimization of tailored electrolyte additives that facilitate the formation of a more stable electrode-electrolyte interphase, have collectively accelerated the commercialization of Si-based anodes [28-31]. Currently, silicon-oxygen-carbon composites, as representative materials, are being initially deployed in high-end consumer electronics and high-energy-density power batteries. Nevertheless, systematic investigations into the thermal runaway mechanisms specific to Si-based LIB systems remain insufficient.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Thermal runaway represents the most severe safety hazard for LIBs, characterized by an uncontrollable, violent exothermic chain reaction. This process is often accompanied by fire, explosion, and the release of toxic gases, posing grave risks to property and personal safety [32-34]. The inherent large volume changes, complex interfacial chemistry, and potentially higher reactivity of Si-based material may introduce distinct thermal failure pathways and potentially exacerbated thermal hazards compared to conventional graphite anodes [35, 36]. This knowledge gap highlights the critical need to better understand thermal runaway mechanisms in Si-based LIBs. Additionally, the current lack of a comprehensive grasp of their thermal safety profile has sparked widespread industry concerns about the safety risk of their large-scale application.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Consequently, a systematic elucidation of thermal runaway mechanisms in Si-based LIBs is paramount for accurately evaluating their safety risks, guiding the rational design of intrinsically safer Si-based batteries, and facilitating their more secure and reliable application. This review aims to systematically elaborate on the thermal runaway mechanisms of Si-based LIBs and corresponding mitigation strategies.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Specifically, it first clarifies the thermal safety challenges inherent to different Si-based anode types, then dissects the core thermal runaway mechanisms by focusing on high-temperature interactions among key components in Si-based systems. Building on this mechanistic understanding, the review further summarizes state-of-the-art technical pathways for enhancing thermal safety, including interface modification and electrolyte optimization. Finally, it prospects future research directions. By integrating mechanistic insights, practical solutions, and forward-looking perspectives, this review fills the void of systematic thermal runaway research in Si-based LIBs, providing essential theoretical support and scientific references for advancing next-generation LIBs with both high energy density and superior safety — addressing a long-standing need for actionable guidance in industrial and academic communities.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Currently, commercially applied Si-based anodes are mainly categorized into three types (Figure 1a,b): nano-silicon, micro-silicon (typically represented by silicon oxide and porous silicon), and silicon-carbon composite materials, each with unique advantages and pending challenges [37-39].

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: Nano-silicon materials (particle size $< 150~\mathrm{nm}$ ) can effectively alleviate mechanical stress during lithiation/delithiation through the nanoscale effect [40-42], thus exhibiting excellent rate capability and high reversible capacity. However, their large specific surface area leads to increased surface energy, which exacerbates side reactions with electrolytes, resulting in low ICE and poor cycling stability [43, 44]. Additionally, their low tap density limits industrialization. Current preparation methods include ball milling (low-cost but with inferior performance) and Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) (better product consistency but higher cost) [45]. Future research should focus on developing low-cost preparation processes and reducing side reactions via interface modifications to improve cycle stability.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Typical representatives of micro-silicon are silicon oxide and porous silicon [15, 22, 46, 47]. Among them, pre-lithiated silicon-oxygen composites use micro-sized $\mathrm{SiO}_x$ ( $0 < x < 2$ ) as the matrix, and pre-lithiation treatment compensates for irreversible lithium loss during the first cycle [48-50]. Their advantages lie in the fact that oxygen atoms can partially buffer volume expansion, while pre-lithiation significantly improves ICE, enabling practical applications in power batteries. Nevertheless, the materials still suffer from poor conductivity, unresolved volume expansion, and difficulties in precisely controlling oxygen content and pre-lithiation uniformity [51]. Future efforts need to further optimize preparation processes and develop new auxiliary materials to enhance performance consistency and reduce costs.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: Silicon-carbon composite materials can alleviate the volume expansion of Si by means of the carbon phase and enhance the conductivity of Si-based materials. CVD silicon-carbon composites have emerged in recent years. It is fabricated by depositing silicon on porous carbon substrates via chemical vapor deposition, combine the dual advantages of carbon matrix for buffering volume changes and constructing 3D conductive networks, thus demonstrating optimal cycling stability and high ICE [52-54]. However, they face challenges such as insufficient rate capability, high cost, and poor consistency of porous carbon precursors, complex processes, and safety risks of silane gas. Future research should focus on optimizing CVD process parameters and developing new low-cost carbon precursors to promote industrialization.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Future development will show differentiated trends: nano-silicon needs to enhance stability; pre-lithiated silicon-oxygen composites require further optimization of the cost-performance ratio; CVD silicon-carbon composites need process simplification and cost reduction. The final material selection will depend on the comprehensive requirements of specific application scenarios for performance, cost, and process.

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: The fundamental cause of thermal runaway in batteries lies in a sequence of exothermic chemical reactions occurring within the cell, leading to progressive heat accumulation that ultimately triggers an irreversible chain reaction. When the battery temperature rises continuously, the reaction chain inducing battery thermal runaway can be summarized as the following sequence (Figure 2a): SEI decomposition, anode-binder reaction, anodesilicon reaction, anode-electrolyte reaction, heat release process caused by internal short circuit, cathode-electrolyte reaction, and finally ends with electrolyte decomposition reaction [55]. Although the cathode-electrolyte reaction and electrolyte decomposition reaction exhibit higher enthalpy change values and heat release rates compared with the anode-centric series of reactions, the initial trigger of thermal runaway is still dominated by anode-related reactions. Accelerating Rate Calorimetry (ARC) provides an essential adiabatic testing environment (Figure 2b,c) for precisely investigating this process, enabling the effective capture of three core characteristic temperatures $\mathrm{(T_1}$ : onset temperature signifying the beginning of significant self-heating; $\mathrm{T}_2$ : trigger temperature marking the onset of uncontrollable temperature rise; $\mathrm{T}_3$ : maximum temperature) and one critical rate indicator (maximum temperature rise rate, dT/dt) during thermal runaway [56, 57]. These parameters serve as the cornerstone for quantitatively evaluating battery thermal safety. Consequently, the primary objectives for enhancing thermal safety are to elevate the values of $\mathrm{T}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{T}_2$ while suppressing the peak of $\mathrm{T}_3$ [58, 59]. Specifically for Si-based anodes, they are not only the key factor dominating $\mathrm{T}_{1}$ (corresponding to the decomposition process of the SEI) but also exert a significant influence on $\mathrm{T}_2$ (related to the reaction of Si/Li $_x$ Si and chemical crosstalk). In addition to ARC, Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) is also a commonly used and effective method for studying the thermal behavior of Si-based anodes; by monitoring the endothermic and exothermic characteristics of Si-based anodes during thermal runaway, it can provide support for further optimizing their thermal safety performance. For Si-based anodes, their influence on battery thermal runaway mainly stems from the following three aspects: Reaction of SEI: With [60, 61] increasing temperature, SEI on the electrode surface undergoes decomposition, and the decomposi tion products further react with the electrolyte. This process is accompanied by significant exothermic effects and generates a large amount of gas, resulting in the destruction of the structural integrity of the SEI.

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: Reaction of $\mathrm{Si} / \mathrm{Li}_x\mathrm{Si}$ : The destruction [62] of the SEI film structure exposes the highly reactive surfaces of $\mathrm{Si} / \mathrm{Li}_x\mathrm{Si}$ directly to the electrolyte environment, triggering intense interfacial side reaction. This process not only intensifies the exothermic intensity but also generates more gas, promoting a rapid rise in the temperature of the battery system.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Therefore, a thorough understanding of the thermal runaway mechanism in Si-based anodes necessitates a detailed examination of these three core aspects: reaction of SEI, reaction of $\mathrm{Si} / \mathrm{Li}_x\mathrm{Si}$ , and chemical crosstalk. The following sections will elaborate on each of these key processes.

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: The thermal decomposition of SEI marks the initiation of self-heating reactions in LIBs. Thus, enhancing the thermal stability of the SEI is crucial for suppressing battery thermal runaway. However, compared with the SEI formed on graphite anodes, the SEI on Si-based anodes exhibits lower stability at elevated temperatures [64]. This phenomenon is mainly attributed to the higher work function of the oxide layer on the surface of Si-based anodes, which significantly hinders the electron transfer process and FIGURE 2 | (a) Energy release diagram during thermal runaway for the cell with Si-C composite anodes. (Figure 3a). In contrast, the high electrical conductivity and low surface work function of graphite facilitate the decomposition of EC into inorganic components such as $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ . This fundamental distinction directly governs the thermal stability thresholds of the two types of SEI.

label: 结构表征
paragraph_context: Si-based SEI, dominated by organic phases, exhibits not only electrolyte solubility but also compromised thermal stability. The representative component LEDC undergoes a well-defined three-stage thermal degradation in Figure 3b,c [60]: decomposition at $50^{\circ}\mathrm{C} - 300^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ releases $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4$ , leaving $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ and lithium propionate $(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CO}_2\mathrm{Li})$ as solid residues; lithium propionate further decomposes to 3-pentanone and $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ between $300^{\circ}\mathrm{C}-600^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ; above $600^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , under the influence of carbon thermal reduction, $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ ultimately decomposes to $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O}$ . In situ analysis by Wang et al. [65] confirmed that organic SEI components decompose at room temperature, liberating flammable gases $(\mathrm{H}_2,\mathrm{CO},\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4)$ . Upon heating beyond $50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , decomposition kinetics accelerate markedly, evidenced by a carbon content decrease from $32\%$ to $25\%$ alongside rising oxygen, fluorine, and lithium concentrations — indicating partial conversion of organics to inorganic phases (e.g., $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O}$ , LiF), though unstable organic matrices remain predominant. Above $100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , extensive cleavage of $\mathrm{C = O}$ and $\mathrm{C - O}$ bonds releases escalating concentrations of $\mathrm{CH_4}$ and $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_6$ , while SEI thickness contracts from 14.8 to $8.1\mathrm{nm}$ at $200^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , severely compromising mechanical integrity (Figure 3d,e).

label: 理化性质
paragraph_context: It is noteworthy that although common inorganic components in the SEI (such as $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ , LiF, and $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O}$ ) are generally regarded as key contributors to the thermal stability of the SEI, their stability is, to some extent, dependent on the electrolyte composition. For instance, while pure $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ decomposes only at high temperatures ( $>800^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ), in electrolyte systems containing $\mathrm{LiPF}_6$ , $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ can react with $\mathrm{LiPF}_6$ at temperatures below $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , yielding products such as LiF, $\mathrm{CO}_2$ , and $\mathrm{LiPO}_2\mathrm{F}_2$ (Figure 3f) [66]. Thermal analysis studies indicate that the heat released from this reaction even exceeds the decomposition heat of common organic constituents in the SEI, such as lithium alkyl carbonates and lithium alkenyl carbonates [61]. Therefore, in the context of using $\mathrm{LiPF}_6$ as the electrolyte salt, the impact of $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ on the thermal safety of batteries needs to be re-evaluated.

In addition, the impact of $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ , a common inorganic component in SEI, on the thermal safety performance of batteries in $\mathrm{LiPF}_6$ based electrolytes should be reevaluated.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: With respect to Si-based materials, their lithium content and dimensional characteristics are two critical factors governing thermal safety. DSC of Si at varying lithiation degrees (Figure 4a,b) reveals three exothermic peaks at $100^{\circ}\mathrm{C} - 200^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Zone A), $250^{\circ}\mathrm{C} - 350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Zone B), and $350^{\circ}\mathrm{C} - 500^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Zone C) [62]. Total heat generation increases with lithium content: Peak C intensifies and shifts to lower temperatures, while the exothermic peak near $140^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ grows progressively. From this perspective, the reaction between $\mathrm{Li}_x\mathrm{Si}$ and electrolytes at high temperature mainly caused by the reaction between lithium in $\mathrm{Li}_x\mathrm{Si}$ and the electrolyte. However, ARC tests on $\mathrm{LiNi}_{0.8}\mathrm{Co}_{0.1}\mathrm{Mn}_{0.1}\mathrm{O}_2$ (NMC811)/Si@C batteries [69] show no significant state of charge (SOC)-dependent variation in thermal runaway onset temper atures $\mathrm{T}_{1}$ ( $\sim 60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ) and $\mathrm{T}_{2}$ ( $\sim 150^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ). This may be due to the wrinkling of the diaphragm at high temperatures.

label: 理化性质
paragraph_context: For fully lithiated Si electrodes with different particle sizes (Figure 4c), the $140^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ exothermic peak strengthens with reduced particle size (due to thicker SEI on smaller particles), whereas the primary exothermic peak diminishes and shifts to lower temperatures [62]. Collectively, smaller Si particles provide increased reactive interfaces, enabling more lithium to participate in electrolyte reaction at reduced temperatures and elevating low-temperature heat release [70].

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: Beyond lithium content and dimensional characteristics, the thermal stability of Si in electrolyte systems also requires further improvement. The dangling bonds on the Si surface significantly affect its interfacial reaction behavior with the electrolyte: [71] when the surface dangling bonds are dominated by $-\mathrm{H}$ , the gaseous products generated from the reaction between Si and the electrolyte are mainly composed of CO; whereas when the surface dangling bonds are dominated by $-\mathrm{OH}$ , the gaseous products from the reaction are mainly $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ . During the reaction between the electrolyte and Si, $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ is a key factor promoting gas generation; at the same time, under high-temperature conditions, Si is also prone to chemical reaction with $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ to form $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{SiF}_6$ (Figure 4d), and this process directly leads to the capacity fading of Si-based anodes [67, 72]. Therefore, for the application scenario of developing high-safety Si-based anodes, $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ may be not an ideal electrolyte component choice.

paragraph_context: Although interface modification has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in improving the electrochemical cycling performance of Si-based material, systematic studies on its mechanism of action in the thermal runaway process of Si-based material remain relatively scarce. The mechanisms by which interface modification enhances the overall thermal safety of Si-based batteries can be mainly summarized into the following three points: i. Using the dynamic regulation function of interface modification substances on the SEI, the composition and microstructure of SEI are optimized, thus effectively increasing the thermal decomposition temperature of SEI and enhancing its high-temperature stability. ii. By virtue of the excellent chemical stability or specific reaction characteristics of interface modification substances under high-temperature environments, the effective isolation between the electrolyte and Si-based active materials is realized. This significantly suppresses exothermic reactions between them at elevated temperatures, thereby reducing the risk of thermal runaway. iii. By reducing chemical crosstalk between the cathode and anode through interface modification materials, the initiation and accumulation of interfacial side reactions are suppressed.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The optimization of electrolytes is crucial for enhancing the thermal safety of Si-based batteries, as they constitute a primary heat source in the chain reaction of thermal runaway. Therefore, targeted electrolyte design to intervene in this process has become a key research focus. However, a central challenge in this endeavor lies in the inherent trade-off between achieving thermal stability and maintaining electrochemical performance. Strategies that enhance safety parameters—such as elevating characteristic temperatures $(\mathrm{T}_1,\mathrm{T}_2)$ or reducing the peak temperature $(\mathrm{T}_3)$ —often inadvertently impair key performance metrics. This compromise may manifest as reduced ionic conductivity, increased interfacial resistance, lower Coulombic efficiency, or deteriorated rate capability. Consequently, the forefront of electrolyte research is not merely focused on maximizing safety, but on intelligently mitigating the trade-off through innovative design [96, 97].

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: The main technical pathways for advanced electrolytes to navigate these challenges can be categorized into the following four aspects: i. Enhancing interfacial thermal stability: By optimizing electrolyte components, an inorganic-rich (e.g., LiF) and thermally stable SEI/CEI is promoted to increase its decomposition temperature, thereby delaying the onset of thermal runaway.  ii. Constructing intrinsically flame-retardant systems: Developing non-flammable electrolyte solvents (e.g., fluorinated solvents, ionic liquids) or incorporating efficient flame retardants to fundamentally eliminate the combustibility of the electrolyte matrix.  iii. Suppressing chemical crosstalk: Utilizing functional additives or novel salts to effectively scavenge or neutralize reductive gases (e.g., $\mathrm{H}_2$ , $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4$ ) generated at the anode, thereby blocking their migration to the cathode and mitigating the associated exothermic chain reactions.  iv. Introducing active thermal safety mechanisms: Designing smart electrolytes (e.g., thermally responsive polymerizing electrolytes) that can rapidly solidify or form an insulating barrier upon reaching a critical temperature, thus physically terminating ion transport and chemical crosstalk to arrest thermal runaway propagation.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The following subsections will systematically review the progress made in areas such as solvent engineering, functional additives, solid-state electrolytes, high-concentration electrolytes, and thermally responsive electrolytes, based on these core design principles.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In Si-based battery systems, solvent engineering serves as a crucial means to balance thermal stability and interfacial compatibility. Its core lies in achieving precise regulation of the properties of SEI and the thermal safety performance of batteries by optimizing solvent compositions and additive types. Among them, the rational selection of fluorinated carbonates [98, 102] and the innovative application of high-flash-point solvents [103-105] are two important research directions.

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: Fluorinated carbonates, with their unique chemical structures, exhibit a significant role in regulating the interface of Si-based anodes. Fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), as the most commonly used additive, can preferentially undergo reduction reaction on the Si surface, forming an inorganic SEI dominated by LiF. This LiF-rich interfacial layer can not only effectively inhibit the volume expansion of Si particles but also significantly improve the ICE of the battery. However, the application of FEC has obvious high-temperature limitations: [106-108] at temperatures above $55^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , FEC tends to undergo side reaction with $\mathrm{LiPF}_6$ to generate HF, which continuously corrodes the interface of the Si-based anode, destroys the integrity of the SEI, and seriously endangers the thermal safety of the battery.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: To overcome the high-temperature drawbacks of FEC, researchers have proposed a replacement strategy using difluoroethylene carbonate (DFEC) [98, 102]. In high-temperature environments, DFEC can significantly reduce the amount of HF generated compared to FEC. Specific experimental data show that when DFEC is used as the electrolyte additive for Si-based batteries instead of FEC, the maximum temperature of the battery in the needle penetration test is only $116.9^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , which is much lower than $581.6^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ of the FEC system, and no combustion occurs; meanwhile, the heat release of the DFEC system (1832 J) is also significantly lower than that of the FEC system (11030 J) (Figure 7a-c). The above results further confirm that DFEC can greatly improve the thermal stability and safety performance of the battery on the basis of ensuring the quality of the film formed on the interface of the Si-based anode [98]. Nevertheless, the introduction of highly fluorinated solvents, while beneficial for thermal stability and flame retardancy, often comes at the cost of increased viscosity and reduced ionic conductivity, highlighting a typical trade-off that requires careful formulation balancing.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: The application of high-flash-point solvents provides another effective way to enhance the thermal safety of batteries. Such solvents, with their high boiling points and low volatility, can fundamentally reduce the flammability risk of batteries. However, their film-forming performance on the anode is usually poor, and they often need to be used in conjunction with film-forming additives [109-111]. Chen et al. [99]. Designed a flame-retardant sulfone-based electrolyte STF, which constructs a thinner, more uniform CEI with more inorganic components at high temperatures, compared to the commercial electrolyte $\mathrm{ED}(1\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\mathrm{LiPF}_6$ in EC/DMC, 1:1 in volume). This CEI has excellent thermal stability and mechanical strength, which can effectively protect the structural integrity of the cathode material and improve the electrochemical performance of the battery at high temperatures (Figure 7d,e). In addition, sulfone-based electrolytes have good thermal stability and flame retardancy, and can effectively reduce the decomposition of $\mathrm{LiPF}_6$ at high temperatures to generate HF, thereby lowering the risk of thermal runaway and improving the safety performance of the battery [112].

paragraph_context: Nitrile solvents have shown unique application prospects in battery safety due to their high polarity, strong coordination ability, excellent oxidation resistance, and good high-temperature stability [113, 114]. They adjusted the ion-dipole interaction between $\mathrm{Li^{+}}$ and SN by introducing FEC with weak solvating ability. In the ST-F electrolyte (SN/LiTFSI/FEC = 15:1:0.75 by mol), the unique $\mathrm{Li^{+}}$ solvation structure rich in FEC and anions selectively decomposes on the Si monoxide anode, thereby forming a stable LiF-rich SEI. This SEI enhances the stability of the solid-liquid interface and electrochemical performance, and effectively protects the anode from performance degradation caused by volume expansion and continuous decomposition of the electrolyte.

paragraph_context: Functional additives mainly include three categories: lithium salts, ionic liquids, and flame retardants. In commercial applications, $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ is a commonly used lithium salt, but it has poor thermal stability (with a decomposition temperature of approximately $80^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ) [116]. It tends to release corrosive gases such as HF at elevated temperatures, exacerbating interfacial side reaction, thus failing to meet the requirements in terms of high-temperature performance and thermal safety. Based on this, researchers have developed various lithium salts with high-temperature stability, such as lithium tetrafluoroborate ( $\mathrm{LiBF_4}$ ), lithium bisoxalatoborate (LiBOB), Lithium difluorooxalatoborate (LiDFOB), LiFSI, and LiTFSI. Their decomposition temperatures all exceed $200^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , much higher than that of $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ . However, each of these lithium salts has certain drawbacks: for instance, $\mathrm{LiBF_4}$ exhibits low ionic conductivity at room temperature; LiBOB has high viscosity and the formed SEI has large impedance; LiDFOB has high preparation cost; LiFSI and LiTFSI tend to corrode Al foil under high-voltage conditions [116].
