paragraph_context: Polyanionic compounds, as the name implies, are a series of compounds consisting of a series of tetrahedral anionic units with a general formula of $(\mathrm{XO}_4)^{\mathrm{n - }}$ or $(\mathrm{X_mO_{3m + 1}})^{\mathrm{n - }}$ and polyhedral $\mathrm{MO_x}$ where X represents P, Mo, Si, W, or other elements, and M represents transition metal elements.[39] The strong X-O covalent bond provides a stable 3D framework structure for polyanionic compounds, which ensures the rapid transmission of metal ions in the framework, resulting in excellent cycling stability. On account of the high degree of valence electron localization of transition metal ions, the elements with larger electronegativity will increase the redox potential of the material through the induction effect. As a promising cathode material, polyanionic compounds are widely used in secondary batteries, especially sodium-ion and potassium-ion batteries. According to the group composition of the compound, polyanionic compounds are roughly divided into phosphate, other single polyanion (sulfate/silicate/molybdate, etc.), and mixed polyanion systems, among which phosphate system is the most widely used.[40] Among all phosphate polyanionic compounds, olivine and NASICON-type compounds are the most common ones. The most typical olivine-type compounds include $\mathrm{LiMPO_4}$ and $\mathrm{NaMPO_4}$ ( $\mathrm{M} = \mathrm{Fe}$ or $\mathrm{Mn}$ ). $\mathrm{LiFePO_4}$ has become the most commercialized cathode material for lithium-ion batteries since it was discovered by Goodenough in 1997.[41] However, each unit of $\mathrm{LiFePO_4}$ allows one metal ion to insert or extract at most, therefore they have no multi-electron transfer conditions. NASICON-type compounds with an open 3D framework show high ionic conductivity. In NASICON-type compounds, the orthorhombic $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{M}_2(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ ( $\mathrm{M} = \mathrm{V}$ , Ti) exhibits good rate performance and cycle life. Taking $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{V}_2(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (NVP) as an example, the phosphorus-oxygen tetrahedron and the vanadium-oxygen octahedron are connected at the same vertex, forming a crystal structure with two types of sodium sites. paragraph_context: Dual-ion batteries (DIBs), with high energy density, high power density, and low cost, are a new type of energy storage system. Different from the traditional rocking-chair battery, the anions in the solution also play a part in the intercalation reaction (Figure 5). The dual-ion intercalation reaction indicates that the cations and anions in the system are stored in the anode and cathode materials respectively.[52] When more than 0.5-mole ions are intercalated or deintercalated to each side on average, the material is regarded as a multi-electron material in the dual-ion intercalation reaction. Note that the battery reactions involving different cations (for example, both $\mathrm{Li^{+}}$ and $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ ) are generally not classified as dual-ion reactions, which is named as "hybrid-ion reactions" in most related publications. The materials for dual-ion intercalation should possess an exceptional ability to contain ions. The cathode materials typically possess characteristics such as outstanding structural stability, wide interlayer spacing, and high resistance to working voltage, enabling them to accommodate anions with large radii and high electronegativity (e.g., $\mathrm{PF_6}^-$ , $\mathrm{TFSI}^-$ , $\mathrm{FSI}^-$ , $\mathrm{ClO_4}^-$ , $\mathrm{DFOB}^-$ , as shown in Figure 6b) without causing any structural damage. Currently, cost-effective and stable inorganic carbon materials such as expanded graphite, along with environmentally friendly and structurally controllable organic polymer materials, as well as layered metal oxides and metal organic frameworks (MOFs), can serve as excellent materials for dual-ion batteries.

paragraph_context: The use of rechargeable inorganic carbon materials, such as graphite, has been extensively employed within the realm of electrochemistry. Layered graphite consists of multiple layers of graphene stacked through the Van der Waals force and serves as the most prevalent inorganic carbon electrode in DIBs. It can serve as both the cathode and anode, exhibiting efficient and reversible intercalation/deintercalation of cations and anions.

paragraph_context: The intercalation reaction of DIBs can be illustrated, taking graphite as an example: $\mathrm{xA^{-} + }$ Graphite $\rightleftharpoons$ Graphite(A)x+xe-(at cathode side); $1 / 6\mathrm{Li^{+}} + 1 / 6\mathrm{e^{-}} + \mathrm{C}\rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Li}_{1 / 6}\mathrm{C}$ (at anode side)[53] Graphite exhibits a high anionic intercalation potential (typically $>4.5\mathrm{V}$ versus $\mathrm{Li} / \mathrm{Li}^{+}$ ) when is used as cathode in a DIB, thereby resulting in high energy density.[54] The discharge voltage and capacity of graphite cathodes are intricately linked to their inherent properties and the size and nature of the anions within the system. Anions usually intercalate the graphite interlayers by a staging mechanism. Research indicates that greater degrees of graphitization and crystallinity will enhance anionic storage capabilities, for instance, highly crystalline natural graphite surpasses amorphous graphite. However, despite extensive research, graphite materials still face numerous challenges.[55] On the one hand, the narrow layer spacing of the graphite cathode limits its ability to fully accommodate anions' intercalation. When large-sized anions intercalated into the graphite layers, volume changes occur significantly with a $50\%$ expansion rate.[56] It leads to easy detachment of the graphite sheet, thereby impacting the battery's cycling life. On the other hand, the electrode's magnification performance and specific capacity will be compromised due to the low diffusion kinetic rate of anions.

paragraph_context: The organic dual-ion materials in the DIBs, possess several advantages including environmental friendliness, facile recycling, exceptional flexibility, high operating voltage, abundant and diverse raw materials availability, and a designable structure. The common organic materials in DIBs can be categorized into n-type, p-type, and bipolar electrode materials based on their electron transfer mechanism and charge state. The n-type electrode undergoes reduction to an anion during discharge and subsequently combines with cations in the system, which is reversed during charge. Similarly, the p-type electrodes lose electrons in a neutral state while charging, resulting in the formation of positively charged cations that combine with anions present in the system. Bipolar organic materials possess both these characteristics, and act as either cathode or anode as required.

In this section, we briefly introduce the classification and research progress of dual-ion intercalation materials, including inorganic carbon materials, organic dual-ion materials, layered metal oxides, metal-organic frameworks, etc. DIBs present new opportunities for the development of environmentally friendly, cost-effective, highly safe, and high-specific-energy battery systems. However, the dual-ion intercalation system possesses certain inherent drawbacks such as a low Coulombic efficiency of the initial cycle and a high irreversible capacity. Due to the sluggish kinetics of anions' diffusion and intercalation, there is a pressing need to enhance the rate performance of DIB cathodes. Currently, research on dual-ion intercalation systems is still at the initial stage, with many mechanisms remaining elusive. To surmount these limitations and challenges, material engineering, electrode engineering, and system engineering are indispensable to develop electrodes with better electrochemical properties to replace the existing materials. Additionally, it is possible to develop systems such as all-organic DIBs with high energy density, which possess distinct advantages in terms of environmental sustainability and cost.

paragraph_context: The structure of organic carbonyl compounds typically exhibits excellent symmetry, with the ability to transfer two or more electrons simultaneously. Carbonyl compounds are classified as n-type organic materials. The carbonyl group gains electrons and is reduced during discharge, leading to the formation of aryl carboxylates or enolates through combination with cations $(\mathrm{Li}^{+}, \mathrm{Na}^{+}, \mathrm{K}^{+})$ in the system. The process is reversed during charging. The reported electroactive carbonyl compounds primarily consist of small molecule compounds and polymers, in which the small molecule compounds can be broadly categorized into quinones, carboxylic acid compounds, imide compounds, and anhydride compounds based on their functional groups.[69] Quinone compounds, such as benzoquinone and anthraquinone, with a relatively simple structure, low molecular mass, and high theoretical capacity, can exhibit multiple electron transfer reactions.[68] Quinones exhibit higher redox potential than carboxylic acids and imides. During discharge, two carbonyl groups gain electrons sequentially and combine with alkali metal ions to form anionic alkali metal salts. The category of small molecule quinones encompasses multicarbonyl quinones, substituted quinones, hybrid aromatic quinones, and other compounds. Small molecule quinones commonly include poly(2,6-anthraquinonyl sulfide) (PAQS), poly(benzoquinonyl sulfide) (PBQS), poly(2,5-dihydroxy-1,4-benzoquinonyl sulfide) (PDBS), poly(1,4-anthraquinone) (P14AQ), salt-disodium rhodizonate $\mathrm{(Na_2C_6O_6)}$ , 1,5-dihydroxyanthraquinone (1,5-DHAQ), poly(anthraquinonyl imide) (PAQI), 2,7-bis(lithiooxycarbonyl)pyrene-4,5,9,10-tetraone (LCPYT), tetrahydroxybenzoquinone (THBQ), calix[4]quinone $\left(\mathrm{C}_{4} \mathrm{Q}\right)$ , tetrachloro-1,4-benzoquinone $\left(\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{Cl}_{4} \mathrm{O}_{2}\right)$ , poly(2,5-dihydroxy-p-benzoquinonyl sulfide) $\left(\mathrm{Li}_{2} \mathrm{PDHBQS}\right)$ , and others.[70] These quinones show exceptional characteristics in terms of capacity, discharge voltage, and reaction reversibility as highly promising cathode materials.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: In aromatic carboxyl compounds, carboxyl is attached to both sides of the aromatic ring, usually in para-position. The inserting potential of metal ions in such compounds is typically low so they are suitable for anodes in alkali metal ion systems in consideration of both safety and energy density.[71] Common aromatic organic carboxylic acids include terephthalate $(\mathrm{C_8H_4O_4R_2}$ , R is alkali metal), $4,4^{\prime}$ -biphenyldicarboxylate $(\mathrm{C_{14}H_8O_4R_2})$ , $4,4^{\prime}$ -stilbene-dicarboxylate $(\mathrm{C_{16}H_{10}O_4R_2})$ , and others.[72] Interestingly, non-aromatic carboxylic acids can also serve as anode materials. Ma and his co-workers reported 1,4-cyclohexane dicarboxylic acid $(\mathrm{C_8H_{12}O_4}$ , CHDA) with a non-conjugated ring structure as an anode for sodium-ion batteries. They conducted first-principles calculations to analyze its energy distribution, and explored its reaction mechanism, expanding the range of organic anode materials. The calculations indicate that hydrogen-transfer-mediated orbital transforms from antibonding $\pi^{*}$ to bonding $\sigma$ drive the stabilization of electrons, thus activating the sodiation of carboxylic acid groups. CHDA exhibits a reversible capacity of $284\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at a current density of $0.1\mathrm{A g^{-1}}$ with a $100\%$ capacity retention rate after 100 cycles.[73] Anhydride compounds show relatively high specific capacity among organic materials. In aromatic anhydrides, anhydride connected with the aromatic system can disperse the electrons through delocalization. 3,4,9,10-perylene tetracarboxylic dianhydride (PTCDA), which is the most typical anhydride, has been extensively used as a cathode for advanced batteries in numerous studies.[74] Structurally, it consists of a large condensed aromatic ring and conjugated carbonyl groups. Typical anhydride materials include pyromellitic dianhydride (PMDA), 1,4,5,8-naphthalene tetracarboxylic dianhydride (NTCDA), etc.[75] The redox potential of anhydride can be improved by expanding the conjugated system of aromatic rings and introducing electron-withdrawing substituent groups.[76] The structure of imide compounds is quite similar to that of anhydride compounds (such as PTCDI/PTCDA). Compared with other compounds, imide compounds possess the advantages of larger $\pi$ conjugated systems and more electroactive groups.[77] During discharge, the carbon in the carbonyl groups gains electrons to form carbon-oxygen anions and combines with metal ions subsequently. It is worth noting that during the charge-discharge process, usually only one of the two carbonyl groups in the imide group is reactive, and the reduction potential of the other carbonyl group is much lower, therefore irreversible. Traditional imide compounds such as o-phenylenediamine (PMI), naphthalene diimide (NDI), and perylene diimide (PDI) have poor performances as cathodes. However, with the evolution of materials, the specific capacities of imide materials such as $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{PMI}$ , $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{NDI}$ , and hexyl-NDI-F have been greatly improved.[78] Unfortunately, carbonyl organic compounds have obvious defects in common, including but not limited to high solubility in organic electrolytes, low discharge voltage, low conductivity, and so on.[79] The introduction of polar functional groups (-COONa, -SO₃Na, etc.) into carbonyl compounds can effectively reduce the solubility of organic materials. For example, Wang et al. obtained Na₂BNDI cathode containing sodium carboxylate group by condensation of 1,4,5,8-naphthalene tetracarboxylic acid dianhydride (NTCDA) and 2-aminoethanoic acid in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) solvent (Figure 9a).[80] The dissolution behaviors of Na₂BNDI and NTCDA in different solvents were observed by UV–vis spectroscopy. It was found that no obvious absorption peak was observed in several solvents soaked in Na₂BNDI, while NTCDA was different, showing that the salted Na₂BNDI is more difficult to dissolve. At the same time, Na₂BNDI as the cathode of SIB shows a capacity retention rate of 57.3% after 70000 cycles at a rate of 10C. Nevertheless, these groups are often not reactive so the increased molecular mass significantly diminishes the specific capacity of such materials. Therefore, optimizing and adjusting the molecular structure is an ideal modification method that avoids compromising specific capacity. Taking quinone compounds as an example, the preparation of multi-quinone polymers through polycondensation is a common and low-cost effective method to inhibit the dissolution of small molecule quinones. The theoretical specific capacity of these quinone polymers depends on the composition of the monomer. In the study of Luo et al., a variety of anthraquinone-based polymer cathodes were synthesized through different connection ways using benzene with low molecular mass as the crosslinking agent of anthraquinone.[81] It is found that the connection mode can significantly affect the porosity and band structure of the material, resulting in charge storage capacity. Of the three products synthesized, the 1,2,4,5-tetra linkage pattern endows the polymer PBAQ-3 (Figure 9b) with a high specific surface area, a low LOMO level, and a narrow band gap, which enables excellent capacity and rate performance. The results show that a high-crosslinked structure can reduce the solubility of quinone materials. As the cathode of sodium-ion battery, it provides a specific capacity of $200\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ with a capacity retention of $83.1\%$ after 40000 cycles at a current density of $3\mathrm{Ag}^{-1}$ . Gu et al. designed and prepared a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with different imine conjugated units through molecular engineering strategy.[82] The size of the conjugated unit can affect the molecular orbital energy of the active unit, thereby improving the electrochemical performance of COFs. What's more, phosphorous has the same alloying ability with Na and K, generating $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{K}_3\mathrm{P}$ , demonstrating the same theoretical capacity as lithium-ion batteries when referring to sodium- and potassium-ion batteries.[125] Low-cost, fully commercialized, and highly sta ble red phosphorous (RP), which is believed amorphous, could be exploited as a cheap anode material.[126] A high-quality 1D RP nanofiber product was fabricated on a large scale through a bottom-up approach using $\mathrm{Sn}_{24}\mathrm{P}_{19.3}\mathrm{I}_8$ ternary complex as a catalyst, and its composite with graphite was further investigated as an anode to perform eminent performance of $1048.4\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ at $4.0\mathrm{A g}^{-1}$ after 1300 cycles, which provides an applicable range of P-based anode material for LIBs.[127] Despite that, the "breaking-off effect" of $\approx 200\%$ volume variation and poor electronic conductivity seriously block its commercial application, accompanied by the "shuttle effect" of intermediate products (polyphosphides), which would cause fast capacity declination.[128] Black P (BP), easily synthesized by RP, shares a graphene-like layered structure with high electronic conductivity of $\approx 3\times 10^{2}\mathrm{S m}^{-1}$ and low $\mathrm{Li^{+}}$ diffusion barrier of $0.08\mathrm{eV}$ (zigzag edges), and has been developed rapidly in recent years.[129] Jin and his coworkers reported a BP-graphite (BP-G) composite with a covalently bonded interface, thus avoiding its edge reconstruction and enabling high $\mathrm{Li^{+}}$ diffusion kinetics (Figure 15f).[130] What's more, a thin polyaniline (PANI) gel coating layer was achieved to prevent the continued (re-) formation and buildup of less-conductive lithium fluorides and carbonates in the SEI layer. The designed BP-G/PANI anode shares ultrahigh cyclability of more than 2000 cycles at $2.6\mathrm{A g}^{-1}$ (1 C), with its capacity remaining steady and stable ( $>910\mathrm{mAh g}^{-1}$ ).

This prevents the formation of by-products from parasitic reactions and enhances the reaction kinetics of carbon catalysts in lithium-oxygen batteries. Theoretical calculations suggest that the doped P atoms will form graphitic P-N sites before replacing the N atoms in the pyrrole-N position, rather than forming graphitic P-C sites. Therefore, sawdust-derived P-doped catalysts exhibit a specific capacity of $\approx 20000\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at 200 and $500\mathrm{mA g^{-1}}$ , and long-term cycle stability of 220 and 160 cycles. Nevertheless, exploring low-cost electrocatalysts without noble metal composites to enhance the co-catalytic activity of ORR and OER, and keeping the catalytic activity, still remains a continuous challenge in the research community.[148] Still, the direct acquisition of oxygen from ambient air would take a long way to go.[149] Changing organic systems into an aqueous or solid-state one is also a feasible path to stabilize the oxygen electrode.[150] Researchers are also inducing solar energy to enhance the kinetics of the $\mathrm{O}_2$ electrode, or changing the reaction system into a closed one, which restricts the reversible $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O} / \mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O}_2$ conversion into an encapsulated battery environment, to prevent decomposition and volatilization of the organic electrolyte.[151] Different from $\mathrm{O}_2$ in oxygen-based batteries, which dominantly generates peroxides, in sulfur-based secondary batteries, the main product is sulfides, meaning that per S atom could carry two electrons.[152] High-temperature sodium-sulfur (Na-S) batteries were invented as early as 1967 by the Ford Company, which was deemed to be an available energy storage device and developed for decades.[153] Unlike the high-temperature Na-S system, in which the molten sodium is packed in beta alumina tubes, lithium-sulfur (Li-S) battery is designed directly like a lithium-ion battery (or lithium metal battery), with sulfur-carbon composite cathode, lithium anode, separator, and organic electrolyte (usually ether-based).[154] The two-electron redox reaction and polysulfides (LiPSs) diffuse to the anode and produce $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{S}$ on the surface of lithium, causing high polarization, sluggish kinetics, and active material consumption.[156] paragraph_context: One imperative problem in Li-S batteries is that large amounts of conductive carbon with low density in insulating sulfur cathodes (electronic conductivity $5 \times 10^{-28} \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~m}^{-1}$ ) inescapably lead to reduced volumetric capacity.[156a] To overcome this difficulty, except for enhancing the loading of sulfur,[159] the co-family elements of sulfur, selenium ( $1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~m}^{-1}$ ), and tellurium ( $2 \times 10^{2} \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~m}^{-1}$ ), are developed as cathode materials.[160] Although their theoretical gravimetric capacity is not that high (675 and $420 \mathrm{mAh} \mathrm{g}^{-1}$ for Se and Te, respectively), their high densities enable ultrahigh theoretical volumetric capacity ( $3268 \mathrm{mAh} \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ for Se and $2621 \mathrm{mAh} \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ for Te).[161] However, the intermediates (polyselenides and polytellurides) keep shuttling through the separator, which would still be an urgent problem.[162] A multifunctional Janus separator was created by applying hierarchical N-doped carbon nanocages (hNCNC) and AlN nanowires to different sides of a commercial polypropylene (PP) separator to address the challenges of Li-Se battery.[163] At ambient temperature, Li-Se batteries with the modified separator demonstrate an ultrahigh rate capacity ( $331 \mathrm{mAh} \mathrm{g}^{-1}$ ) and maintain a high capability of $408 \mathrm{mAh} \mathrm{g}^{-1}$ at 3C after 500 cycles, with an extreme environment capability at $-30$ to $60^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ , indicating a wider application. The exceptional pergenerateance arises from the "bucket effect" of suppressed lithium polyselenides shuttling through chemisorption and electrocatalysis of hNCNC on the cathode side, while suppressed Li-dendrite growth through thermally conductive AlN network on the anode side. Elucidated by the synergistic effect, this Janus separator presents a universal approach for developing advanced batteries with S/Se/Te cathodes.

paragraph_context: Elements in the VIIA family $(\mathrm{Cl}_2, \mathrm{Br}_2, \mathrm{I}_2)$ , which have high abundance in the oceans, have been applied as cathodes for centuries.[164] In 1884, the airship La France, measuring $52\mathrm{m}$ in length, embarked on its maiden voyage near Paris with a $435\mathrm{-kgZn - Cl_2}$ battery, which served as a power supply throughout the entire journey, covering a distance of $\approx 8\mathrm{km}$ .[165] In their cathode redox reactions, halogen $\mathrm{X}_2$ $(\mathrm{X} = \mathrm{Cl}, \mathrm{Br}$ or I) generates two electrons and generates $2\mathrm{X}^{-}$ , theoretically possessing 756, 335, and $211\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ of the capacity, respectively.[166] $\mathrm{F}_2$ has not been a potential object of study since its high reduction potential $(>2.88\mathrm{V}$ vs S.H.E.), which exceeds the potential window of most electrolytes.[167] Noteworthy, the transition of other types of the different oxidation states of halogens have been discovered, for example, $\mathrm{I}^{-} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{I}^{+}$ , or $\mathrm{I}^{-} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{IO}_{3}^{-}$ .[167a,168] The main drawback of halogen cathodes is the crosstalk effect of polyhalides, in particular, the $\mathrm{X}_2$ species tend to combine an $\mathrm{X}^{-}$ ion and generate soluble $\mathrm{X}_3^{-}$ , which would accelerate this process, causing high polarization and self-discharge issues.[169] In addition, the $\mathrm{X}_2$ with high oxidability may corrode the entire system.[167a] Separately, the chlorine, bromine, and iodine cathode have different drawbacks. $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ cathode, as a gas electrode, needs a porous adsorbent that has the ability to catalyze the three-phase reaction.[170] What's more, excessive chloride would block the porous tunnels of the gas, resulting in poor kinetics. The sluggish kinetics further lead to parasitic side reactions, which deteriorate the reversibility.[171] As for $\mathrm{Br}_2$ , its low vapor pressure makes it easy to evaporate, causing possible toxicity.[172] Solid state $\mathrm{I}_2$ , with better tunability and stability than $\mathrm{Cl}_2 / \mathrm{Br}_2$ , still faces the problem of poor conductivity.[173] Researchers have developed various solutions to alleviate the problems, for example, physical/chemical restrictions, separator modification, and anode protective layers.[174] In a lithium-iodine case, highly thermally stable organic salts with iodine content of up to $80\%$ were developed to serve as ideal cathode materials (Figure 15e).[173] The stabilization of iodine within compounds such as methylamine hydroiodide (MAI) or tetrabutylammonium triiodide $(\mathrm{TBAI}_3)$ was achieved through effective chemical bonding with organic groups, eliminating the need for porous or layered hosts while maintaining its redox activity. Both experimental and theoretical evidence confirm the robust interaction between organic groups and iodine/polyiodides, enhancing its thermodynamic stability and addressing the crosstalk problem to improve cathode capacity and mitigate anode corrosion. In typical scenarios, $\mathrm{Li - I}_2$ batteries demonstrate a notable enhancement, with an increase of $217~\mathrm{mAh}~\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ (based on $\mathrm{I}_2$ , equivalent to $166.1~\mathrm{mAh}~\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ based on the whole MAI cathode) after 10 000 cycles at 5 C. Furthermore, the 50C rate capacity exhibits a $78.1\%$ percentage compared to a 0.5C low rate, which paves the way for the development of high-performance cathode materials for halogen cathodes and metal-halogen batteries.

paragraph_context: Conversion-alloying type metal chalcogenides (sulfides, selenides, and tellurides) share a similar mechanism to metal oxides, consisting of a replacement reaction forming alkali metal chalcogenide and simple substance M, followed by an alloying reaction in which M generates electrons and generate alloy with alkali metal ions.[119] Generally, these materials are mechanically stable in comparison with metal oxides, which might be carefully balanced with the decreased theoretical capacity.[70a,191] Except for the general problem of volume change and pulverization, the "shuttle effect" of polysulfides/polyselenides/polytellurides may take place, resulting in severe fading of the electrochemical performance.[70a,192] In recent years, various kinds of conversion-alloying type metal chalcogenides have been discovered, for example, $\mathrm{GeS}_2$ , SnS, $\mathrm{SnS}_2$ , SnSSe, $\mathrm{SnSe}_2$ , $\mathrm{Sb}_2\mathrm{S}_3$ , $\mathrm{Bi}_2\mathrm{S}_3$ , $\mathrm{Sb}_2\mathrm{Se}_3$ , $\mathrm{Bi}_2\mathrm{Se}_3$ , etc., in which $\mathrm{Sb} / \mathrm{Bi}$ sulfides/selenides are received more and more attention on account of the excellent compatibility of $\mathrm{Sb} / \mathrm{Bi}$ with sodium or potassium.[193] The rational surface engineering of $\mathrm{Sb}_2\mathrm{S}_3$ with PVDF-derived carbon was achieved through thermal interfacial reactions, resulting in the formation of a dual carbon layer with the development of tightly bonded Sb-C chemical bonds, which promotes $\mathrm{Li^{+}} / \mathrm{Na^{+}}$ ion transferring and alleviates the phase separation of antimony and sulfide (Figure 18c).[193o] Through "voltage-cutting" methods, the crucial factor of capacity promotion about phase transitions was further determined. When employed as lithium-ion battery anodes, the capacity remains approximately $813\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1.0\mathrm{A}$ $\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ , and even $674\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at an ultrahigh current density of $5.0\mathrm{A g^{-1}}$ . The sodium ion storage capacity remained up to 366 $\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $3.0\mathrm{A g^{-1}}$ , demonstrating significant insights into interfacial evolutions toward conversion-alloying systems. In another case of SnSSe, Ji's group presented a groundbreaking approach to achieve a quantum-dot-level distribution of reaction intermediates $(\mathrm{Sn}^0$ and $\mathrm{Na}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{M})$ within metal chalcogenides, particularly targeting the layered SnSSe material (Figure 18b).[193e] In this innovative work, the anionic selenium atoms in SnSSe were strategically replaced with S atoms, leading to the formation of SnSSe crystals with a uniform dispersion and an abundance of crystal defects. Additionally, the SnSSe nanosheets were dispersed onto reduced graphene oxide, utilizing the confinement effect to create a 2D van der Waals heterostructure (SnSSe/C). This combination of induced defects and the unique layered heterostructure promotes rapid nucleation, fostering the formation of quantum-dot-level dispersed $\mathrm{Sn}^0 /\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S} / \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{Se}$ intermediates during the conversion reaction. Concurrently, the in situ generation of numerous $\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S} / \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{Se}$ grain boundaries effectively inhibits $\mathrm{Sn}^0$ agglomeration and facilitates rapid $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ diffusion across the $\mathrm{Sn}^0 /\mathrm{Na}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{M}$ solid-state interphases, resulting in exceptional cycling stability, evidenced by a mere $0.002\%$ capacity decay per cycle over 15000 cycles, and remarkable rate performance, achieving $310.5\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $20\mathrm{A g^{-1}}$ . Furthermore, a comprehensive analysis combining in situ/ex situ experimental techniques and DFT calculations provides insights into the stabilization mechanism of the intermediates and the rapid $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ transport kinetics, significantly advancing the understanding of the sodium ion storage process in metal chalcogenides and offers valuable guidance for the design and fabrication of conversion-alloying materials.

As a substitute for alloying materials, conversion-alloying materials have been investigated for decades. Due to the buffer effect of the resilient conversion product which could tolerate volume expansion, the conversion-alloying materials generally show decreased stress/strain (in other words, smaller volume change and more unlikely to form microcracks) than alloying materials.[198] Another advantage is that the conversion-alloying materials enable lower voltage than conversion on account of the alloying reaction, which would create advantageous conditions for the application of anode. Nevertheless, the as-introduced conversion reaction leads to phase separation that ultimately decreases the reaction kinetics.[193c] What's more, one thing that should be noted is that diverse and complex voltage plateaus might be a negative condition to the commercialization scenarios, like electric vehicles or large-scale energy storage devices, which emphasize flat and stable plateaus.[199] Various kinds of modification strategies have been operated, i.e., structural engineering, buffering matrix, defect engineering, and so on. Most of the advanced strategies cannot do without carbon materials, like graphene, carbon nanotubes, and carbon nanofibers, which may take on the role of either relieving stress or building up an electron conductive network. Composite materials or heterostructures might be another possible measure to increase the electron flow (Figure 18d).[200] However, this would lead to a more complicated mechanism to be revealed. Furthermore, the role of conversion products (especially insulative $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{O} / \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{O} / \mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{O}$ ) has not been fully discovered, which should have been (theoretically) harmful to the reaction kinetics, but seemingly not.[110d] Besides, the possible synergistic effect between the electrolyte and conversion-alloying materials still remains indefinite.[201] A series of multi-electron reactions and their relative materials have been highlighted in previous sections of this brief review. Owing to their different potentials versus related alkali metals, they are investigated as either cathodes (most single-ion intercalation materials, $\mathrm{MF}_{\mathrm{x}}$ conversion materials, and alloying materials in VI- & VII- families) or anodes (most conversion materials, conversion-alloying materials, and alloying materials in IV& V- families). Potential-tunable organic materials have been applied as both cathode and anode materials. By combining multi-electron cathode materials with the suited multi-electron anode materials, high-energy-density battery systems could be achieved, for example, Li-rich Mn-based cathode || Si anode in Li-ion batteries, or PBA cathode || $\mathrm{MoS}_2$ anode in Na-ion batteries.[6] Determined by diverse requirements for battery performances in various fields, the future applications of different battery systems have been categorized. For instance, high gravimetric energy density for power batteries, cost-effectiveness and ultrahigh safety for massive energy storage systems, and high flexibility highly desired for wearable smart consumer electronics, putting forward a higher expectation for the future development of high-energy-density batteries.[202] As we demonstrate in this brief overview, massive solutions have been proposed to overcome the existing problems of different battery chemistries and embrace the various applications of batteries in future smart cities.[203] Carbon materials, characterized by their low cost, wide availability, good conductivity, and excellent structural performance, have been frequently utilized as conductive agents and structural buffers. Elemental engineering, usually the introduction of heteroatomic chemistry, alters the local electronic and chemical environment, leading to improved properties. Bulk engineering, mediated by delicate design of nanomaterials or heterostructures, provides feasible electronic tunnels and improves the kinetics. Interfacial engineering, namely, the induced defects or coating layer, regulates the interfacial diffusion and enhances the electrochemical performance.

paragraph_context: The increased demand for energy has prompted users to seek alternative energy storage devices. Post-Li-ion battery chemistries have been considered potential contenders for the development of next-generation battery technologies. The high specific capacity $(\approx 1675\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1})$ and high natural abundance $(\approx 953~\mathrm{ppm})$ of sulfur provide opportunities to meet the rigorous requirements of the market's demands, such as high energy density and low cost. When combined with a high capacity metal anode (e.g., $\mathrm{Na}\approx 1165\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , $\mathrm{Mg}\approx 2205\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , and Al $\approx 2980\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ ), it leads to high energy density that can outperform the existing battery technologies, including high-energy Li-ion batteries. Despite the unique attributes of the sulfur-based battery system, it remains in infancy owing to the complex reaction chemistry of sulfur cathode, and the level of complexity increases with an increase in valency of metal ions. This review summarizes the unique aspects of a sulfur cathode essential to stabilizing sulfur cathode-based high-energy rechargeable batteries. Furthermore, deeper insight into the electrochemical performance of various metal-sulfur-based systems has been provided. This review may pave the path for the researchers to accelerate the development of sulfur cathode for post-Li-ion batteries.

paragraph_context: Increased demand for high-energy storage technologies has resulted in a substantial rise in high-energy rechargeable batteries.[1-4] Among various rechargeable battery chemistries, the Li-ion system currently dominates the consumer market. It is part of stationary storage due to its appreciably high energy density and long cycle life.[5-9] However, their viability has been severely impacted by the high cost of cathode materials and limited energy density that inherently limits its applications in large-scale grid storage applications and long-range electric mobility applications.[10,11] There has been a quest for a high-energy cathode with substantial storage capacity. In pursuit of the prerequisites above, realizing an alternate solution toward feasible battery chemistry is imperative to leapfrog the existing Li-ion chemistries.[12-14] Post-Li-ion battery technologies, for instance, metal-sulfur batteries, represent one of the most promising chemistries for high-energy rechargeable batteries.[15,16] Lithium-sulfur (Li/S) battery chemistry was initially investigated in the 1960s.[17] Lithium metal anode with a high theoretical capacity of $3860\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , when coupled with the sulfur cathode, brings out a high theoretical specific energy of about $2500\mathrm{Whkg}^{-1}$ .[18-21] These merits are further strengthened by its low-temperature operation and low cost of the electrode material \((\\) 0.02\mathrm{g}^{-1})^{[22,23]}\) Sulfur with relatively low redox potential is ideally configured with different metals to achieve state-of-the-art cascaded sulfur-based battery technologies.[24] As schematically illustrated in Figure 1, a metal-sulfur battery comprising a sulfur cathode, a metal anode, and a separator soaked in the liquid electrolyte. The mechanistic aspect of metal-sulfur chemistries shares a similar fundamental understanding. The complexity and viability of a metal-sulfur battery strongly depend on the nature of the metal anode. Though the nature of the charge/discharge products strongly depends on the metal anode used, the reversibility and stability of the sulfur cathode can be tuned by altering the physical structure of cathode materials (see Figure 1).[25,26] This review explicitly gives a holistic overview of various cathodes used in metal-sulfur batteries (metal—Na, Mg, and Al). Notably, we aim to unveil the unique aspects of sulfur chemistry dictating the electrochemical reversibility of various metal anodes.

paragraph_context: In contrast to the alkali metal-based battery system, the $\mathrm{Mg / S}$ battery system's studies have focused on conductive layered materials as the host for a sulfur cathode. Due to high voltage hysteresis during the cycling process, the $\mathrm{Mg / S}$ battery often suffers from poor efficiency. Layered host composites can minimize the electrostatic force between $\mathrm{Mg}^{2 + }$ ions and polysulfides; however, it enlarges the reaction overpotential. The polysulfides formed are well confined within the layered matrix and thus, resulting in enhanced cycling performance of the battery. As most layered sulfides are poor electronic conductors, the cycling performance of $\mathrm{Mg / S}$ batteries is limited to a few tens of cycles.

paragraph_context: Abstract: Due to the natural abundance of iodine, cost-effective, and sustainability, metal-iodine batteries are competitive for the next-generation energy storage systems with high energy density, and large power density. However, the inherent properties of iodine such as electronic insulation and shuttle behavior of soluble iodine species affect negatively rate performance, cyclability, and self-discharge behavior of metal-iodine batteries, while the dendrite growth and metal corrosion on the anode side brings potential safety hazards and inferior durability. These problems of metal-iodine system still exist and need to be solved urgently. Herein, we summarize the research progress of metal-iodine batteries in the past decades. Firstly, the classification, design strategy and reaction mechanism of iodine electrode are briefly outlined. Secondly, the current development and protection strategy of conventional metal anodes in metal-iodine batteries are highlighted, and some potential anode materials and their design strategies are proposed. Thirdly, the key electrochemical parameters of state-of-art metal-iodine batteries are compared and analyzed to solve critical issues for realizing next-generation iodine-based energy storage systems. Therefore, the aim of this review is to promote the development of metal-iodine batteries and provide guidelines for their design.

paragraph_context: Since the utilization of fossil fuels brings their scarcity and the emissions of pollutants and greenhouse gases, the transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy, such as solar energy, wind energy, tidal energy, and geothermal energy, is necessary.[1-3] As the equipment for energy conversion and storage, rechargeable battery systems can store energy that comes from renewable forms into chemical energy and wait for fueling our modern lifestyles demand. For this reason, rechargeable batteries already play an important role to us and have powered a diverse range of applications, e.g. portable electronics, electric vehicles, and grid-scale storage.[4-10] Many practical rechargeable batteries have been proposed and fabricated by far, such as lead acid, nickel-cadmium, nickel-metal hydride, and lithium-ion batteries. In these practical batteries, lithium-ion batteries become the primary choice for storage devices owing to its long-span life, eco-friendliness, and memoryless effect. Unfortunately, the insufficient energy density of lithium-ion batteries makes electric vehicles difficult to achieve the same driving mileage as fuel vehicles. Hence, the exploitation of next generation batteries with high energy density is essential.

paragraph_context: Iodine is eco-friendly and abundant in nature $(50 - 60\mu \mathrm{g}$ iodine $\mathrm{L_{ocean}})$ . Its conversion chemistry is fast and reversible when iodine is adopted as cathode in metal-iodine $(\mathrm{M - I_2})$ batteries.[11,12] In theory, the specific capacities of iodine are 211 and $422\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ based on the traditional two-electron transfer reaction and the new-reported four-electron transfer reaction, respectively.[13-17] Therefore, iodine becomes a competitive candidate material for next-generation energy storage batteries. As early as the 1970s, primary lithium-iodine batteries were employed to drive cardiac pacemakers because of long shelf life, high reliability, and outstanding hermetic seal.[18] Then, numerous efforts have been devoted to the development of $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries, and many rechargeable batteries subsequently have been proposed and im proved, e.g. $\mathrm{Li - I_2}$ ,[19-21] $\mathrm{Na - I_2}$ ,[22,23] $\mathrm{K - I_2}$ ,[24,25] $\mathrm{Mg - I_2}$ ,[26] $\mathrm{Al - I_2}$ ,[27,28] $\mathrm{Fe - I_2}$ ,[29] and $\mathrm{Zn - I_2}$ batteries.[30-33] Meanwhile, various in situ/ex situ characterization techniques, electrochemical test methods, and density functional theory calculation reveal in depth the redox mechanism of iodine electrode.[24,34-37] Considering that the inherent insulation nature of iodine and the shuttling of soluble iodine species have a negative influence on the reaction kinetics, self-discharge behavior, and cycle performance of $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries, various functional conductive porous materials (e.g. carbonaceous materials, metal organic framework materials) are used to improve conductivity and anchor iodine species,[35,36,38-41] and some interesting methods are also come up that a blocking interlayer is introduced between separator and cathode to restrict the shuttling behavior.[42,43] Additionally, for the enhancement of energy density of batteries, replacing neutral anolyte with alkaline electrolyte is a way in $\mathrm{Zn - I_2}$ batteries to reduce the anode reaction potential,[44] and the operating voltage of battery shows a decent boost. Besides, when the halogen ions are added into the electrolyte, $\mathrm{I}_2$ can be oxidized to its oxidation state $(\mathrm{I}^{+})$ during charging, which can also lead to the increase of the potential and capacity of iodine electrode.[13,45] In short, researches on the optimization and improvement of $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries are still ongoing as iodine-based energy storage systems is a hot research direction, and a timely review and summary of $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries is necessary for development of next-generation energy storage systems. Latest reviews have focused on the compilation of advances in the design strategies for iodine cathode that provides the opportunity to collectively overview the recent research progress of reported metal anode in $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries and their demonstrated solutions. Therefore, we in this review briefly summarize the classification of iodine cathode with their corresponding reaction mechanisms at first, and then highlight the current development of metal anode in $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries. Various strategies towards solving the problems of metal anode and the improvement of $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries are reviewed and classified into four types, which are electrolyte optimization, anode coating, conductive scaffold design, and alleviating the electrolysis of water (for low-reactivity metal anodes). label: 材料制备
paragraph_context: Since iodine is volatile with poor thermal stability, the loss of active iodine on the electrode during preparation is unavoidable, and when used directly as the electrode in battery, it inevitably causes severely deteriorated electrochemical performance. To address these issues, the common method is to prepare a composite electrode by loading and fixing iodine species into the porous matrix material with inherent physical adsorption effect.[24,25,35,36,38-41,46-57] As shown in Figure 1a, iodine species are encapsulated in the holes of the matrix based on electrostatic interactions. The main matrix materials can be divided into carbonaceous materials[24,25,35,36,38,40,41,49-57] and non-carbonaceous material.[39,48] Carbonaceous materials include conductive carbon black,[53] CMK-3,[25] three-dimensional (3D) biofoam,[38] carbon cloth,[24] graphene,[36] and so on.[49] Noncarbonaceous materials include $\beta$ -cyclodextrin,[48] metalorganic framework materials (MOFs),[39] and Prussian blue analogues (PBAs).[58] The methods of uploading iodine species into the matrix include melt-diffusion method,[39,55,56] thermal treatment method,[38,40,53] inside encapsulation method based on solution-adsorption process,[24,25,35,36,41,49,57] solution-dropping method,[51,54] solution-crystallization method,[48] and in situ chemical deposition route.[52] Haoxiang Yu is currently a lecturer at Ningbo University and member of Chinese Chemical Society. He received his Ph.D degree from Harbin Institute of Technology. He has published more than 100 peer-reviewed papers about advanced materials for rechargeable batteries. His current research is focused on the molecular engineering of high-energy-density electrode materials for aqueous batteries.

paragraph_context: For carbonaceous substrate, it makes up for the poor electrical conductivity of active iodine and endows electrode capacitive characteristic, which is beneficial for high-rate performance of battery. However, pristine carbon substrate is non-polar and has a weak attraction to iodine species. To optimize the adsorption of carbon-based matrix, heteroatom doping[36,50,51,54] and additive (or polar functional groups) wrapping strategies[41,59] are implemented. Furthermore, the pore size (macropores/mesopores/micropores), porosity, and graphitization degree of carbonaceous matrix have an influence on the adsorption of iodine species. Therefore, reasonable design and construction of carbonaceous matrix is essential for the enhancement of the battery electrochemical performances. As for $\beta$ -cyclodextrin, the inherent abundant hydroxyl functional groups greatly improve the thermal stability of iodine in electrode because of additional chemical interaction.[48] The dense metal center of MOFs also enables strong polar chemical adsorption ability toward iodine species.[39] For PBAs host, strong chemical interaction between the iodine and functional organic ligands improves the ability to confine iodine in pores.[58] In conclusion, these porous substrates not only anchor iodine species, but also alleviate the change of electrode volume during cycling, contributing to durable cyclability.

paragraph_context: Besides using host material to physically restrain iodine species, combining electroactive iodine with no-electroactive iodophor to form an iodine-containing complex as active electrode material can inhibit the dissolution and diffusion of iodine in electrolyte effectively. According to previous reports, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), MXene, $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_3\mathrm{I}$ and $\mathrm{C_{16}H_{36}NI_3}$ have frequently been adopted as iodophor to prepare chemical complex iodine electrode.[13,60-65] Specifically, in the PVP-I compound, triiodide is adhered to PVP chain via H-I and $\pi$ I chemical bonds (Figure 1b), which significantly reduces the vapor pressure of iodine and improves the thermal stability of iodine. In $\mathrm{Ti}_{3}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{I}_{2}$ I as termination is attached to $\mathrm{Ti}_{3}\mathrm{C}_{2}$ which endows $\mathrm{Ti}_{3}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{I}_{2}$ with natural electrochemical activity.[13] $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_3\mathrm{I}$ and $\mathrm{C_{16}H_{36}NI_3}$ belong to the stable organic iodized salts, which are the most widely used phase transfer catalysts. In these compounds, iodine is effectively stabilized by chemical bonding with organic groups.[64,65] As for the preparation process, elemental iodine and PVP are added to methanol solvent to dissolve and mix homogeneously, and then the solvent is removed in a vacuum environment to prepare PVP-I inclusion. $\mathrm{Ti}_3\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{I}_2$ MXene is prepared by employing $\mathrm{Ti}_{3}\mathrm{AlC}_{2}$ precursor and $\mathrm{CuI}_2$ etchant according to the following equation: $$ T i _ {3} A I C _ {2} + 5 C u I \rightarrow T i _ {3} C _ {2} I _ {2} + 5 C u + A I I _ {3} \uparrow \tag {2} $$ For $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_3\mathrm{I}$ and $\mathrm{C_{16}H_{36}NI_3}$ , these reagents are frequently purchased without further treatment. The detailed information about these four materials is listed in Table 1. Typically, $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_3\mathrm{I}$ reported in recent years shows the highest iodine content in these four materials, so that the theoretical capacity can reach up to $168.6\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ (based on the formula weight of $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_3\mathrm{I}$ ). For $\mathrm{C_{16}H_{36}NI_3}$ and $\mathrm{Ti}_{3}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{I}_{2}$ , the high formula weight of these two materials leads to the relatively low theoretical capacity. By contrast, Meng et al. in their study stated that the iodine content of commercial PVP-I compound is $13\%$ according to ion chromatography measurement.[61] This is possibly due to the high degree of polymerization for PVP. Besides, the potential of $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_3\mathrm{I}$ in organic electrolyte is $2.91\mathrm{Vvs.Li^{+}/Li}$ , being higher than those of $\mathrm{C_{16}H_{36}NI_3}$ and commercial PVP-I compound, suggesting its potential for practical application. When applied in aqueous batteries, $\mathrm{Ti}_{3}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{I}_{2}$ can achieve an excellent electrochemical performance while few studies have focused on these materials ( $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_3\mathrm{I}$ , $\mathrm{C_{16}H_{36}NI_3}$ , and commercial PVP-I compound). paragraph_context: Understanding the reaction mechanism of iodine electrode during charging and discharging is beneficial to optimizing and improving the electrochemical performance of battery in essence, so that in situ and ex situ characterizations, including Raman spectra,[28,35,40] Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy,[56] ultraviolet-visible spectrum,[37] X-ray diffraction analysis,[76] X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy,[56,61] and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy[13] are implemented. According to the reported literatures, two types of charge transfer processes occur on the iodine electrode, which are two-electron transfer reaction with a theoretic capacity of $211\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ (Figure 2a and b) and four-electron transfer reaction with a theoretic capacity of $422\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ (Figure 2c and d).

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: The most common reaction mechanism for $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries is the two-electron conversion chemistry. Theoretically, when element iodine is reduced to iodide, only one plateau should be observed in the potential curves as shown in Figure 2a and b, because equilibrium exists between iodine and iodide. But due to the presence of polyiodide (triiodide mainly), more than one pair of redox peaks are usually found in the Figure 2. Theoretical charge-discharge curve (a) and cyclic voltammetry (CV) curve (b) of iodine electrode with two-electron conversion chemistry. Theoretical charge-discharge curve (c) and CV curve (d) of iodine electrode with four-electron conversion chemistry. (e-h) Schematic diagram of reaction mechanism for iodine electrode. practical CV curves according to the previous studies.[24,29,35,36,61] In the case of $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ systems (alkali metaliodine batteries mainly) using organic electrolytes, element iodine is frequently selected as electrode and its redox behavior is related to the $\mathrm{I}_2 / \mathrm{I}_3^-$ and $\mathrm{I}_3^- / \mathrm{I}^-$ couples (Figure 2e-g). Specifically, the signal of $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ gradually increases during discharging, while it gradually decays until it disappears during charging.[36,40,56,60] Besides, the products on the electrode obtained after fully charged and discharged are $\mathrm{I}_2$ and $\mathrm{I}^-$ , respectively.[23,24] Consequently, $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ can be considered as an intermediate upon this reaction process. The corresponding reactions about $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ can be written as Equation 3 and 4, and the whole reaction can be given by Equation 5.[35,36,61] $$ 3 I _ {2} + 2 e ^ {-} \leftrightarrow 2 I _ {3} ^ {-} \tag {3} $$ $$ I _ {3} ^ {-} + 2 e ^ {-} \leftrightarrow 3 I ^ {-} \tag {4} $$ $$ I _ {2} + 2 e ^ {-} \leftrightarrow 2 I ^ {-} \tag {5} $$ Although these two reactions of Equation 3 and 4 occur during the electrochemical process, Equation 4 has a major contribution to the specific capacity of iodine. As shown in previous reports, two pairs of redox peaks appear in the CV curves, which are attributed to the $\mathrm{I}_2 / \mathrm{I}_3^-$ and $\mathrm{I}_3^- / \mathrm{I}^-$ couples. The $\mathrm{I}_3^- / \mathrm{I}^-$ redox peaks are well-defined whereas the $\mathrm{I}_2 / \mathrm{I}_3^-$ redox peaks are weak,[71,73] so it seems only an obvious discharge plateau can be found in the potential curves of iodine electrode. Unfortunately, $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ tends to be dissolved in organic electrolyte rather than adsorbed in the matrix materials,[11] leading to the capacity fading and inferior durability.

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: Iodine electrode in aqueous electrolyte is operated under a similar mechanism as it in organic electrolytes. But in contrast to organic electrolytes, the intermediate $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ tends to be adsorbed in the matrix materials rather than dissolved in the aqueous electrolyte,[11] and the potential difference between Equation 3 and 4 is almost negligible, which makes it difficult to detect the signal of $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ based on the Raman spectroscopy. Therefore, the reaction about iodine electrode in aqueous system $(\mathrm{Zn - I_2}$ and $\mathrm{Fe - I_2}$ batteries) can be simplified as Equation 5, and the reaction mechanism can be deemed as a one-step conversion of $\mathrm{I}_2 / \mathrm{I}^-$ (Figure 2f).[29,37] Some researchers ever used DFT calculations to explain this mechanism.[37] Active iodine species are stored in the pores of the matrix materials, thereby the electrochemical reaction is confined within the pores. Since the geometric size of $\mathrm{Zn(I_3)_2}$ is larger than the diameter of the pores, it is difficult to exist in the pores whereas the latter can accommodate $\mathrm{I}_2$ and $\mathrm{ZnI_2}$ . Accordingly, the batteries can only undergo a conversion reaction of $\mathrm{I}_2 / \mathrm{I}^-$ without the formation of $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ . This explanation implies that the reaction mechanism of iodine electrode is affected by the pore size of the matrix materials, which requires further verification by subsequent works. In addition, Equation 5 can also be considered as the reaction mechanism of $\mathrm{Li - I_2}$ batteries using solid electrolyte.[76-79] For the batteries using aqueous redox-active catholyte, $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ is oxidized to $\mathrm{I}_2$ after being charged, and then the remaining $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ in catholyte spontaneously react with $\mathrm{I}_2$ to form $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ (Figure 2g). The corresponding reaction can be written as Equation 1 and 5 and the whole reaction is Equation 4.[69,75] Given the electron transfer process of Equation 1 occurs in catholyte and the inert current collector can hardly receive the signal, the behavior of Equation 1 cannot appear in CV curves or potential profile. Therefore, only a pair of plateaus and redox peaks representing the transformation chemistry of $\mathrm{I}_2 / \mathrm{I}^-$ appear in the charge-discharge curves and CV curves for this redox electrode, respectively.

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: When a battery selects PVP-I compound as cathode, the initial iodine species in PVP-I compound should be $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ ,[28] as Meng et al. demonstrated that the PVP-I electrode undergoes a reversible conversion chemistry of $\mathrm{I}_3^- / \mathrm{I}^-$ during cycling.[61,62] Therefore, its reaction mechanism can be considered as Equation 4. Additionally, they found the signal of $\mathrm{I}_5^-$ after overcharge,[61,62] which is attributed to the further oxidation of $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ to $\mathrm{I}_5^-$ as well as the robust chemical interaction between iodine species and PVP to ensure the stable existence of $\mathrm{I}_5^-$ .[63] It is well known that the violent shuttle behavior of $\mathrm{I}_5^-$ is destructive to the cycling performance of battery. Consequently, voltage window needs to be adjusted reasonably as battery adopts PVP-I electrode.

paragraph_context: As mentioned above, the potentials of $\mathrm{I}_2 / \mathrm{I}^-$ and $\mathrm{I}_3^- / \mathrm{I}^-$ in aqueous electrolyte are close (Equation 4 and 5), so that it is difficult for electrochemical analysis to distinguish them. Furthermore, the conversion between $\mathrm{I}_2$ and $\mathrm{I}_3^-$ is rapid and reversible, and its capacity contribution can be negligible. Therefore, the usual two-electron transfer reaction mechanism in aqueous electrolyte possesses flat charge-discharge plateaus and a pair of prominent redox peaks (Figure 2a and b).

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: In addition to the acceptance of electrons to form $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ during the traditional two-electron transfer reaction, element iodine can also donate electrons to form $\mathrm{I}^{+}$ (Figure 2h), achieving higher capacity and higher voltage plateau.[13,45] The conversion reaction from $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ to $\mathrm{I}^{+}$ with donating electrons is called four-electron conversion chemistry, because such a process is made up of two two-electron transfer reactions. These two reactions are Equation 5 and 6. $$ 2 I X + 2 e ^ {-} \leftrightarrow I _ {2 (s)} + 2 X ^ {-} \quad X = (F, C l) \tag {6} $$ Therefore, in practice, the charge-discharge profile shows two well-defined plateaus while the CV curve displays two pairs of sharp redox peaks (Figure 2c and d). For the redox couple of $\mathrm{I}^{+} / \mathrm{I}_{2}$ (Equation 6), when electrolyte contains some electronegative ions such as $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ and $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ , this redox couple can be activated. Since the electronegative ions can bond with $\mathrm{I}^{+}$ , the $\mathrm{I}^{+}$ -containing products are stable and electrochemically reversible, leading to the excellent cycling performance of iodine electrode. Typically, Zou et al.[45] reported that during the charge process, $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ is directly converted to $\mathrm{I}_{2}$ , and then further oxidized to $\mathrm{I}^{+}$ . The latter and $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ which is from aqueous electrolyte combine to form a ICl interhalogen, so that $\mathrm{I}^{+}$ can stably exist in the electrolyte.

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: Besides, it is worth noting that $\mathrm{I}_2$ can be oxidized to generate $\mathrm{IO}_3^-$ without the presence of electronegative ions when overcharged to a high potential (Equation 7).[80] Such a reaction is irreversible, and the $\mathrm{IO}_3^-$ ions are easily dissolved into electrolyte, leading to the loss of active material on the electrode and subsequently the serious capacity decay of batteries. $$ 2 I O _ {3} ^ {-} + 1 2 H ^ {+} + 1 0 e ^ {-} \leftrightarrow I _ {2} + 6 H _ {2} O \tag {7} $$ If one is able to activate the redox couple of $\mathrm{IO}_3^- / \mathrm{I}_2$ and $\mathrm{IO}_3^-$ ions can be adsorbed on the electrode without diffusing into the electrolyte, the capacity and energy density of iodine electrode can be significantly enhanced.

paragraph_context: Alkali metals (lithium, sodium, potassium), alkali-earth metals (magnesium), aluminum, transition metals (zinc, iron, and copper) have been reported as anode materials to pair with iodine active electrode. These batteries perform excellent electrochemical performances. For instance, $\mathrm{Li - I_2}$ battery exhibits capacity degradation of $0.002\%$ per cycle during 2000 cycles[54] and remains $113\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $100\mathrm{C}$ .[81] $\mathrm{Na - I_2}$ battery shows a discharge capacity of $208\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ and $95.5\%$ capacity retention after 3200 cycles.[39] $\mathrm{K - I_2}$ battery[24] delivers an energy density of $75\mathrm{WhKg^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{Mg - I_2}$ battery[56] delivers an energy density of $400\mathrm{WhKg^{-1}}$ .

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: $\mathrm{Al - I_2}$ battery yields high discharge capacity of $205\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ with $98.4\%$ of Coulombic efficiency.[63] $\mathrm{Zn - I_2}$ battery[37] delivers an ultrahigh energy density of $400\mathrm{WhKg^{-1}}$ and an ultra-durable cyclic capability of 10000 cycles with $80\%$ capacity retention.[82] $\mathrm{Fe - I_2}$ battery[29] shows a reversible capacity of $190\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $5000\mathrm{mAg^{-1}}$ . $\mathrm{Cu - I_2}$ battery possesses an open circuit voltage of $0.61\mathrm{V}$ and a long cycle performance of 4000 cycles.[72] Nevertheless, the corrosion and dendrite growth of the metal anode in rechargeable iodine batteries is still inevitable. The corrosion of electrode will cause rapid decay of capacity and deterioration of cycling performance. Meanwhile, along with the corrosion, the formation of an uneven solid electrolyte interface (SEI) layer is able to result in inhomogeneous metal deposition, and ultimately causing metal dendrite. In addition, these dendrites are easily broken and detached from the anode, leading to inefficiency and irreversibility of battery. Therefore, plenty of efforts have been put into solving the problems of metal anode, and many effective optimization strategies have been proposed and demonstrated.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: One of the widest strategies for the electrochemical performance improvement of anode in $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries is the optimization of electrolyte, and three approaches (Figure 3a) are frequently adopted, which are the introduction of additive into electrolyte, changing condensed matter state of electrolyte, and composition improvement of electrolyte. For introduction of additive into electrolyte, some researchers added lithium nitrate $(\mathrm{LiNO}_3)$ additive into the electrolyte of $\mathrm{Li - I_2}$ batteries to promote the spontaneous formation of a conductive passivation layer on the surface of lithium (Figure 3b).[35,49,54,61] The protective layer prevents anode from being directly exposed to electrolyte, and the undesirable side reactions can hardly occur, improving the electrochemical performance significantly (Figure 3c).[83] Aside from addition of $\mathrm{LiNO}_3$ , polysulfide additive can achieve the goal of lithium metal anode protection because of the formation of solid $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{S}$ film.[84] The formed $\mathrm{Li}_2\mathrm{S}$ reacts with polyiodide, yielding iodide and polysulfide, which further alleviates the attack of polyiodide. Since the complexation between ethanol and zinc ions can reduce the exchange current density of zinc, Li et al. achieved dendrite suppression process by adding ethanol additive to electrolyte.[85] Besides, changing condensed matter state of electrolyte can strongly inhibit dendrites growth and electrode corrosion (Figure 3d).[41,68,76-79,86] Typically, when the state of electrolyte in $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries changes from liquid to (quasi-)solid, the charge flow in the electrolyte is frequently dominated by the migration of cations. The electric fields from anion mobility are reduced, resulting in stable metal electrodeposition. Meanwhile, (quasi-)solid electrolyte is able to facilitate a relatively homogeneous cation flux, blocking dendrite growth.[41,86] Furthermore, due to the low solubility and slow diffusion of intermediate (polyiodide) in (quasi-)solid elec Figure 3. For instance, pentaerythritol-tetraacrylate-based gel polymer electrolyte (Figure 3e) facilitates uniform lithium plating and plays a restraining effect of dendrite formation because of the superior lithium-ion transference number.[41,86] It is noted that lithium-ion transference number is a crucial parameter for electrolytes because a high lithium-ion transference number contributes to reduced polarization and improved rate performance of batteries. In addition to pentaerythritol-tetraacrylate-based gel polymer electrolyte, several materials of which previous literatures reported have been the ingredients of (quasi-)solid electrolyte, e.g. poly(ethylene oxide),[68] NaSICON-type $\mathrm{Li}_{1 + x + }$ $^{3z}\mathrm{Al}_x(\mathrm{Ti},\mathrm{Ge})_{2 - x}\mathrm{Si}_{3z}\mathrm{P}_{3 - z}\mathrm{O}_{12},$ [66,68] the perovskite structured $(\mathrm{La,Li})\mathrm{TiO}_3,[68]$ and $\mathrm{LiI(C_3H_5NO)_2}$ [76-79] However, the poor conductivity of (quasi-)solid electrolyte is an urgent problem to be solved. Additionally, composition optimization of electrolyte is a practical method for the protection of anode. Li et al.[87] reported the substitution of $\mathrm{Zn(CF_3SO_3)_2}$ electrolyte for $\mathrm{ZnSO_4}$ electrolyte to inhibit zinc electrode corrosion and improved the electrochemical performance of $\mathrm{Zn - I_2}$ battery. $\mathrm{Zn(CF_3SO_3)_2}$ $\mathbf{I}_2$ and $\mathrm{ZnI_2}$ are able to spontaneously form a dense SEI film on the surface of zinc anode, avoiding the invasion of iodine species and solving the anxiety of dendrite growth. For the metal aluminum anode, a passive oxide layer is always formed on the surface during cycling, which severely limits anodic electroplating ability and easily induces the random growth of dendrites. Zhang et al.[63] accordingly selected ionic liquids as electrolytes to avoid the formation of passivation oxide layer on aluminum anode and achieved excellent cycling stability of $\mathrm{Al / I_2}$ batteries.[63] Meanwhile, the ionic liquids electrolytes (Figure 3f) own better electrical conductivity at higher temperatures, which is beneficial to the electrochemical performance of battery under high temperature conditions.[28] In addition, ultrahigh-concentration electrolyte (solvent-in-salt) and deep-eutectic-solvent electrolyte (Figure 3g) can also solve the problem of metal dendrite growth.[61,88] Typically, solvent-in-salt electrolyte usually shows the features of ultrahigh salt concentration and high viscosity. A classic Chazalviel model[61,89] states that metal dendrites form on the electrode where less anions exist. In ultrahigh concentration electrolyte, condition for dendrite growth hardly occurs since a mass of anions is near metal anode, leading to the uniformity of lithium deposition and dissolution. Meanwhile, high viscosity of ultrahigh concentration electrolyte can result in its high pressure and the limitation of anion convection near deposition area, suppressing the dendrite growth. For deep-eutectic-solvent electrolyte,[88] its high viscosity can protect metal anode against the formation of dendrites as mentioned above. Therefore, the use of two aforementioned electrolytes has a positive effect on the electrochemical performance of $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ batteries.

paragraph_context: In addition to electrolyte optimization, anode coating is also a good strategy to enhance the electrochemical performance of rechargeable iodine batteries (Figure 4a). Specifically, the side reactions occurring on the surface of metal anode in $\mathrm{M - I_2}$ battery come mainly from the presence of soluble polyiodide in electrolyte and the inhomogeneous metal deposition as mentioned above. To suppress these reactions, researchers frequently design a smooth dense layer on anode for blocking the soluble polyiodide in electrolyte from anode,[55,73] so that corrosion of metal anode can hardly take place. Meanwhile, the smooth dense layer can facilitate uniform metal deposition because the cations can distribute evenly on the surface of anode, resulting in the inhibition of dendrite growth. Eventually, the electrochemical performance of rechargeable iodine batteries is improved. For instance, Tian et al. reported the in situ generation of dense NaI passivation layer on Na electrode surface (Figure 4b).[55] Due to the isolation of Na electrode from electrolyte and the lower diffusion energy barrier of NaI $(0.02\mathrm{eV})$ , the dense NaI passivation layer not only inhibits the deterioration of anode, but also promotes the uniform deposition of sodium. Consequently, the battery is endowed with remarkable discharge capacity of $210\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ and ultralong cycle life of 2200 cycles without dendrite growth. paragraph_context: Besides, conductive scaffold design is an another feasible way to regulate the deposition/striping process of metal (Figure 4e).[90-94] Dendrite growth frequently occurs at high current density. When materials with 3D host are used, the applied areal current density can be reduced due to their large surface area. The possibility for dendrite growth decreases. Meanwhile, plenty of nucleation sites for metal plating exist on the surface of conductive scaffold materials. They can induce uniform Li nucleation/growth. Hence, uncontrolled growth of metal dendrites has been suppressed by using this strategy.[90-94] For example, Zhang et al. selected copper metal as a deposition substrate for zinc iodine batteries since copper has a superior electric conductivity than zinc. The selected copper substrate was treated with polyiodide to form porous copper nanoclusters (Figure 4f), which provided lots of nucleation sites for zinc, resulting in ultralow-overpotential, uniform Zn deposition, and superior reversibility.[91] Similarly, Lu et al. selected 3D sulfur and nitrogen enriched graphene foam host to fix zinc metal. The composite can reduce the energy barrier for zinc electroplating and stripping, contributing to the suppression of uncontrollable zinc deposition.[92] In addition, carbon cloth as flexible conductive scaffold is also used in $\mathrm{M - I}_2$ batteries. Li et al. fixed molten lithium into nitrogen-phosphorus co-doped carbon cloth to prepare a self-standing composite anode (Figure 4g).[93] The heteroatom doping is beneficial to the uniform deposition of lithium onto the anode because of enhanced lithiophilicity. The 3D structure of carbon cloth reduces the local charge density, suppressing the growth of lithium dendrite and decreasing the electrode polarization. Hence, the $\mathrm{Li - I}_2$ battery delivered $99\%$ capacity retention after 4000 cycles. To further inhibit dendrite growth, Yu et al. infused a eutectic Li-Na alloy, rather than molten lithium, into a carbon cloth.[94] Owing to the good electric conductivity of carbon cloth and the alloying reaction between Li and Na, uniform deposition occurs on the composite anode with restrained volume expansion and suppressed dendrite formation.

paragraph_context: For high-reactivity metals such as lithium, sodium, potassium, magnesium, and aluminum, they are able to spontaneously react with water since their reduction potential is lower than the hydrogen evolution potential of water. Consequently, the electrolytes used in these $\mathrm{M - I}_2$ batteries are non-aqueous electrolytes.[24,28,34,36,38,39,48,49,52,54,56,57,95] As for low-reactivity metals like zinc and iron, they are quasi-stable in neutral or weakly alkaline aqueous electrolytes. Meanwhile, aqueous electrolyte possesses several advantages, e.g. high ionic conductivity, environmental friendly, low cost, and safety.[96] Nevertheless, when scientists adopt aqueous solution as electrolyte, the electrolysis of water must be considered in rechargeable iodine batteries (Figure 5a), especially $\mathrm{Zn - I_2}$ batteries, because the reduction potential of zinc is very close to the hydrogen evolution potential of water. Actually, the electrolysis of water easily occurs in aqueous $\mathrm{Zn - I_2}$ batteries when overcharged. Accompanying the water decomposition, insulated $\mathrm{ZnO}$ or $\mathrm{Zn(OH)}_2$ would deposit on the surface of zinc electrode and $\mathrm{IO}_3^-$ would form on the cathode side, which significantly slows down the reaction activity of anode and wastes the electroactive iodine species of cathode.[80] To suppress the electrolysis of water, Wang et al.[80] added poly(2-vinylpyridine) with smart pH-responsive nature to the traditional $\mathrm{ZnSO_4}$ electrolyte. When the battery is overcharged, the pH value of electrolyte increases, poly(2-vinylpyridine) would change from an initial hydrophilic sol state to a new hydrophobic gel state due to the deprotonation of its internal quaternary pyridine (Figure 5b). paragraph_context: As known to all, the key to alleviate the electrolysis of water is to reduce reaction activity of water in aqueous electrolyte. Generally, water molecule exists in common $\mathrm{ZnSO_4}$ electrolyte in three forms, namely free state water, solvent separated ion pair (SSIP, $[\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6\cdot \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}]$ ), and contact ion pair (CIP, $[\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_5\cdot \mathrm{OSO}_3^{2-}]$ ) (Figure 5c).[97] SSIP mode easily releases water molecule, revealing its reactivity as free state water. In contrast, CIP mode only releases minority of free water, limiting water reactivity. Based on the aforementioned fact, Yang et al. converted the solvation sheath on the surface of Zn completely into CIP mode by coating a functional MOF membrane (Zn-BTC) on zinc anode, effectively inhibiting the electrolysis of water during charging (Figure 5d).[97] Furthermore, the coating film facilitates rapid transport of ion and uniform deposition of zinc. Therefore, the battery produced a discharge capacity of $201\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ with Coulombic efficiency of $99\%$ and a long cycle performance of 6000 cycles with $84.6\%$ capacity retention. Sonigara et al. integrated an amphiphilic block copolymer (F77, $\mathrm{PEO}_{53}-\mathrm{PPO}_{34}-\mathrm{PEO}_{53}$ ) with liquid electrolyte to form solid gel electrolyte (Figure 5e).[98] Specifically, $\mathrm{ZnSO_4}$ combines with F77 to form gel anolyte electrolyte (IC1). Water molecular is trapped in the cross-linked network of F77 micelle without contacting the electrode and subsequently loses reactivity, but zinc ion can diffuse in F77 micelle. Consequently, the hydrogen evolution reaction can be avoided during cycling. Moreover, the gel electrolyte circumvents the corrosion of zinc electrode by the shuttle iodine species. In addition to limiting the reactivity of water, reducing the hydrogen evolution potential is a feasible strategy. Substituting traditional $\mathrm{ZnSO_4}$ with KOH can reduce the hydrogen evolution potential below the reduction potential of zinc, which eliminates water electrolysis.[44] More importantly, the work widens the voltage window, resulting in a high energy density of $330.5\mathrm{WhL}^{-1}$ .
