paragraph_context: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) have attracted extensive attention for large-scale electric energy storage due to the abundance and low cost of sodium resources [158]. As shown in Figure 8a, the early studies of SIBs can be traced back to the 1980s, almost the same age with lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, with the large-scale commercial application of LIBs around 1990s, the research of SIBs was put on hold for a long time. Although some cathode and anode materials for SIBs were also reported from 2000 to 2010, the development of SIBs was slow. Until 2011, Komaba et al. [159] reported the performance of $\mathrm { N a N i _ { 0 . 5 } M n _ { 0 . 5 } O _ { 2 } \mathrm { - H C } }$ full cell for the first time, and the research of SIBs has entered a boom period. For instance, Guo et al. [160,161] prepared a zero strain, highquality Prussian blue cathode material, and subsequently presented a concept of active facets by multiple-layer oriented stacking nanosheets. Hu et al. [162] reported a P2- $\mathrm { N a } _ { 2 / 3 } \mathrm { C u } _ { 1 / 3 } \mathrm { M n } _ { 2 / 3 } \mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$ cathode material, and firstly discovered the electrochemical activity of $\mathrm { C u } ^ { 2 + } / \mathrm { C u } ^ { 3 + }$ redox pairs in layered oxides. Furthermore, HINA BATTERY produced the world’s first SIB electric vehicle in 2017. And Chou’s group successfully built the SIBs production line based on Prussian blue in 2019. In addition, CATL has vigorously developed SIB research, and released the first-generation SIBs in 2021. As expected, the number of papers published per year has shown a rapid growth from 2010 to 2022 (Figure 8b). As an important component, cathode materials largely determine the electrochemical performance of SIBs. Among various cathode materials, sodium layered transition-metal oxides $( \mathrm { N a } _ { x } \mathrm { T M O } _ { 2 } )$ seem very promising candidates for future SIB applications owing to their great variety of compositions, ease of scalable preparation and high reversible specific capacity Sodium-based layered transition-metal oxides, with a general formula of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ $( \mathbf { M } = \mathbf { \mathrm { C o } }$ , Ni, Mn, Cr, Fe, and Cu, etc.), consist of $\mathrm { M O } _ { 6 }$ octahedral transition metal layers and $\mathrm { N a O } _ { 6 }$ sodium layers [163]. This structure provides a 2D transport channel for ${ \mathrm { N a } } ^ { + }$ insertion/deinsertion. Typically, the ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ are divided by Delmas into two polymorphs: P type (P: prismatic) and O type (O: octahedral) in accordance with the coordination environment of ${ \mathrm { N a } } ^ { + }$ . Generally, ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ mainly include P2, P3, O2 and O3 type, where the 2 or 3 means the number of transition metal layers in a single cell unit. Among them, P2- and O3-type ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes have attracted more attention. P2-type cathodes have a wider $\mathrm { N a } ^ { + }$ transport channel and a lower ${ \mathrm { N a } } ^ { + }$ migration barrier, showing faster diffusion kinetics. O3-type cathodes have higher initial capacity due to the higher ${ \mathrm { N a } } ^ { + }$ content. However, the commercial development of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes is still hindered by three major challenges: (1) sluggish kinetics, (2) low energy density, (3) air instability. Various approaches were proposed to solve the problems mentioned above. This roadmap review summarizes the current optimization strategies from macro- to micro-perspective with different dimensions: microstructure design, local chemistry regulation and structural unit construction (Figure 9).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The sluggish kinetics of SIBs is due to the relatively larger $\mathrm { N a } ^ { + }$ radius compared with ${ \mathrm { L i } } ^ { + }$ and limits the cycle stability and rate performance in most cathode materials [164]. The microstructure design is the universal method to improve performance for $\mathrm { N a } _ { x } \mathrm { T M O } _ { 2 }$ cathodes. The different structures including 1D nanowires [165], 2D nanosheets [166,167], 3D microspheres [168], and exposed active facets [161] are designed to improve the electrochemical performance of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes. Reasonable structure design (such as core–shell structure, micro-/nano-structure) can effectively improve the cycling stability to alleviate the volume expansion of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ materials during the charging/discharging process.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Besides, the local chemistry regulation can be further used to improve the performance of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes based on modulating intrinsic electron/ion properties by chemical element substitution [169]. Therefore, it can modulate the physical and chemical properties to accelerate the phase transformation and suppress lattice strain [170,171]. Furthermore, anionic redox induced by regulating the local chemical environment has been regarded as an effective method to provide additional reversible capacity [38,172].

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In addition, structural unit construction can improve the intrinsic chemical properties of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes by ad- justing the interionic interactions [173,174]. For example, the formation of super-structural units can improve the air stability and structural stability of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes due to inhibiting the valence change of anions and the release of lattice oxygen [38,175]. Furthermore, reasonably integrating different kinds of superstructure units can also obtain high- performance ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes. Therefore, these effective strategies enable ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes with enhanced cycling stability and rate capability. It is the research trend of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes in the future to combine various improvement methods and integrate their respective advantages.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In summary, the structural stability and electrochemical performance of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes can be enhanced by designing and optimizing the microstructure, local chemical, and structure unit from macro- to micro-dimensions. (1) A reasonable microstructure design can effectively improve the sluggish transport kinetics of $\mathrm { N a } ^ { + }$ . (2) The local chemistry regulation can enhance the energy density of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes. (3) The air stability of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes can be improved by reasonably regulating the structural unit. In addition, gradient structure and coating structure design inducing reverse electric field also can modulate the electron/ ion structure of ${ \mathrm { N a } } _ { x } { \mathrm { T M O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes. These strategies presented in the review will provide some inspiration for the design and development of next-generation high energydensity cathodes for SIBs.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) have gained significant attention over the last decade as a new technology capable of complementing the existing lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) for some specific applications such as low-range electric vehicles and future stationary energy storage [176–178]. The interest seen in PIBs lies in the abundant resources of K (i.e., $1 . 5 \ \mathrm { w t . \% }$ in the Earth’s crust) and a relatively high energy density. It is widely acknowledged that the fully optimized graphite||Prussian blue PIBs at the pouch-cell level can deliver a gravimetric energy density over $2 0 0 \mathrm { W h } \mathrm { k g } ^ { - 1 }$ , 2–3 times greater than conventional lead–acid batteries and is comparable with the prevalent LIBs [179]. PIBs become increasingly attractive to meet the requirements of grid-scale energy-storage applications when considering the following merits, including (1) a similar standard redox potential $( - 2 . 9 2 \mathrm { V }$ vs. standard hydrogen electrode) compared with that of its Li counterpart $( - 3 . 0 4 \mathrm { V } )$ ; (2) $\mathrm { K } ^ { + }$ has the smallest Stokes’ radius $( 3 . 6 \mathrm { \AA } )$ compared with ${ \mathrm { L i } } ^ { + }$ (4.8 Å) and ${ \mathrm { N a } } ^ { + }$ $( 4 . 6 \mathrm { \AA } )$ in conventional electrolytes, affording faster ion mobility and ion conductivity; (3) aluminium foil can be used as an anode current collector in PIBs instead of the copper foil found in LIBs; and (4) the cost of PIBs can be further decreased, considering the salt in the electrolyte presents lower cost than that of LIBs [180–183]. Although PIBs hold the promise to compete with the established LIBs, PIB systems are still in the infancy stage and facing several challenges that need to be tackled before considering their practical deployment. For instance, it is still challenging for cathode materials to work at a high voltage and most of the reported electrolytes will be continuously decomposed owing to the fragile electrode/electrolyte interface, while most of the anode materials are plagued by the low Coulombic efficiency (Figure 10). To make the PIBs commercially competitive, in this roadmap, we will focus on critical challenges discovered by the research effort to date and offer possible solutions for further development in this battery system.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: PIBs share a similar rocking-chair principle to the LIBs, where $\mathrm { K } ^ { + }$ ions shuttle between the anode and the cathode through a non-aqueous electrolyte. Like LIBs, the performance of PIBs significantly depends on the nature of key components, including cathodes, electrolytes, and anodes.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: (1) Cathode. As the core factor that dominantly dictates the overall performance of the PIBs, whether the PIBs technology can achieve new breakthroughs lies in the development of cathode materials with high working-voltage windows. Nevertheless, it is challenging for the discovered cathode candidates to readily work at a high voltage above $4 . 2 \mathrm { V }$ in PIBs. Additionally, in order to achieve higher battery capacity and cycling stability, the cathode materials should be intentionally designed with ample channels for the diffusion of charge carriers, suitable crystal structure, and high redox potential. To date, several types of materials have been attempted including Prussian blue and its analogues (PBAs), layered metal oxides, polyanionic compounds, and organic crystals, in which the main strategy is to connect transition metals with chemical species such as –O–, –P(S)–O(F)– and –CN– to build up compounds with suitable interlayer spacing, large tunnel and frame structure to allow the insertion of $\mathrm { K } ^ { + }$ ions.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: (2) Electrolyte. The electrolyte not only acts as a medium for ionic diffusion between electrodes but also dictates the properties of the solid-electrode interface (SEI) layer, which influences electrochemical performance such as cycle stability. In the past five years, various functional electrolytes were developed for PIBs. Traditional carbonate-based electrolytes have been ruled out due to the formation of unstable SEI layers at high voltage on the cathode and low voltage on the anode surface. Ether electrolytes have excellent ionic conductivity with low viscosity, and can form a stable SEI layer. However, the key challenges for ether-based electrolytes lie in the low boiling points and poor oxidation stability, as well as the co-intercalation of $\mathrm { K } ^ { + }$ ions and ether molecules into the graphite anode (the most promising anode in PIBs). In order to fulfill the requirements for both cathodes and anodes, electrolyte engineering should be mainly focused on the manipulation of $\mathrm { K } ^ { + }$ ion conductivity, viscosity, chemical/ electrochemical/thermal stability, and the ability to form a stable SEI layer [182]. Moreover, the solvation structure of electrolytes and the interaction between the cation and solvent/anion in the electrolyte should be fully understood at atomic/molecular level, especially how they interact with the electrode surfaces. In this case, advanced computational and experimental tools, including operando characterization techniques can be used to quantitatively describe the characteristics and properties of electrolytes and SEI formation and evolution. The electrolyte development will be the key to unlocking high-safety and fast-charging PIBs in the future.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: (3) Anode. The anode electrode is not typically the bottleneck for capacity or cell potential. Owing to the high reactivity leading to safety issues, using K metal is practically not suitable, other than acting as the reference/counter electrode in half-cell configurations. In this case, various anodes have been synthesized and tested for PIBs, including intercalation-based materials (hard carbon, graphite, ${ \mathrm { N b } } _ { 2 } { \mathrm { O } } _ { 5 }$ , etc.), conversion-based materials (oxides, sulfides, selenides, etc.), and alloying-type anodes (phosphorus, antimony, bismuth, etc.). However, because of the large $\mathrm { K } ^ { + }$ radius (1.38 Å), significant volume variation and strain of active materials (such as ${ \sim } 4 0 7 \%$ for Sb) can be observed during the potassiation/depotassiation. Therefore, both conversionbased and alloying-based materials with high theoretical capacity exhibit rapid capacity fading and poor rate performance. Possible solutions include the introduction of nanostructure and carbon scaffold to enhance charge carrier diffusion and endure the stress, but these strategies would scarify the whole volumetric energy density [177,178].

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: Considering the high theoretical capacity of $2 7 9 \mathrm { m A h g } ^ { - 1 }$ according to the graphite intercalation compound of ${ \mathrm { K C } } _ { 8 }$ , carbon materials have shown great potential in PIBs. However, the formation of $\mathrm { K C } _ { 8 }$ affords a dramatic volume expansion of $6 1 \%$ , which is much larger than that of $\mathrm { L i C } _ { 6 }$ (about $1 0 \%$ ), the dominant challenge of the graphite anode is its poor cycle stability. One strategy is to improve the structural disorder. Hard- (with disordered and non-expandable framework) and soft-carbons (higher conductivity and better aligned graphitic domains) have been developed, where hard carbon has the best cycle life but the soft carbon structure benefits high-rate behavior. A hard–soft composite would integrate the advantages of both carbons, and the capacity can be further modified by the introduction of defects/heteroatoms. However, another challenge that affects its further deployment is the low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE). Reducing the specific area, defects and surface functional groups can increase ICE significantly but will result in low capacity. How to balance between ICE and capacity is challenging [185]. In addition, the preparation of carbon anodes with high tap density is needed to improve the volumetric energy density.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: PIBs have been proved to be promising with the features of cost effective that can meet the requirements of energy storage for niche market. The aforementioned challenges led to disappointment, but new findings about the prospects of PIBs have broadened today’s ambitions, and existing obstacles can be overcome through advanced strategies in the future. It should be emphasized that outstanding performance reported for battery materials and cells in the literature is often reported under specific conditions that are not aligned with practical applications. Aiming to bridge the gap between academic research and industry, we advocate that academic research turn to improve performances under industrial requirements and metrics, such as lean electrolyte, high loading of active material, and excellent CE. Because the development of PIBs follows LIB’ track, the physio- and electro-chemical features of electrodes and electrolytes can be directly engineered from the successful experience of LIBs. This is a good indication considering the fact that it will be economically beneficial for the industries. Therefore, there will be plenty of opportunities to develop PIBs with high energy density and low cost, and PIBs will have a bright future as next-generation batteries for grid scale energy storage.

label: 理化性质
paragraph_context: Today’s electrochemical energy storage technology has evolved into a variety of rechargeable battery systems. Recently, the resource shortage of raw material in widely used lithium-ion batteries has attracted widespread attentions. The requirements to meet resourcefulness, sustainability, safety and high energy density have motivated the rapid development of various novel batteries [186]. Among “beyond Liion” batteries, rechargeable magnesium-ion batteries (RMBs) have many unique advantages [187]. (1) High theoretical volumetric energy density (Figure 11a). Magnesium (Mg) metal has a low reduction potential (−2.37 V versus S. H.E), and its volume capacity $( 3 , 8 3 3 \mathrm { m A h } \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 3 } )$ is 1.8 times higher than that of lithium $( 2 , 0 4 6 \mathrm { m A h } \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 3 } )$ ). (2) Rich reserves and easy extraction (Figure 11b). Mg is the eighth most abundant element in the earth’s crust and is also present in large quantities in seawater. (3) Less susceptible to dendrite growth and higher safety. Compared with lithium, Mg metal is less reactive and less prone to dendrite formation during reversible plating/stripping process, reducing the occurrence of internal short circuits. Also, Mg is environmentally friendly, and most Mg-containing compounds are non-toxic [188]. These advantages provide a solid foundation for the potential application of RMBs, which are expected to partially replace the application scenarios of lithium batteries.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In 2000, Aurbach et al. [189] reported the first prototype system of RMBs. In spite of the fact that RMBs have been developed for more than two decades and have yielded many substantial breakthroughs, there are still many existing challenges that hinder their commercial applications. RMBs are generally composed of three key components: $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ - conducting electrolytes, $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ -storage cathodes, Mg metal or alternative anodes. It is well known that the intrinsic properties of these key materials and the corresponding interfacial components jointly determine the practical performance of RMBs. According to our decade’s R&D knowledge of RMBs, we provide a brief review and prospect of relevant key scientific issues in RMBs.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In terms of $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ -conducting electrolytes, chlorine-containing electrolytes have played a very important role in the development of RMBs, despite the accompanying corrosion problems that are inevitable. Recently, there is a growing interest in highly performing single salt electrolytes with non-corrosive characteristic, such as boron-center (or aluminium-center) Mg salts and carborane-based Mg salts [190–192], which usually display higher ionic conductivity and superior compatibility with metallic battery components. However, the currently commonly used solvents are still only some ether solvents, such as tetrahydrofuran, 1,2-dimethoxyethane, diglyme and tetraglyme. We note that solvent choices and solvation effects in Mg electrolytes have received less attention. From the widely studied lithium batteries, it is known that metal-ion solvation structure determines important electrolyte properties, such as ionic conductivity, transference number, and electrochemical window of both solvent and anion [193]. More importantly, different solvation shells also directly affect the corre- sponding interfacial chemistry such as the formation of solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and charge-transport through electrolyte/electrode interfaces. To date, there have been sporadic reports declaring that the $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ coordination structure has significant effects on the electrochemical behavior of a variety of Mg cathodes [194,195]. These important factors that have been overlooked in the past provide a valuable metric to understand and assist further progress in designing suitable anions and solvents for $\mathrm { M g }$ batteries. We call for future solvent designs for Mg electrolytes and the utilized Mg salt types (and concentrations) must be more concentrated for their vital effects on $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ coordination environment. In addition to the typical liquid electrolytes, solid electrolytes are also very promising candidates by virtue of their high safety features, mainly including polymer electrolytes, inorganic solid electrolytes and MOF-based electrolytes. Nevertheless, their drawbacks of low ionic conductivity and poor electrode/electrolyte compatibility need further optimization and modification. The transport of multivalent ions in solid-phase materials has always been a thorny problem plaguing the scientific community, and it is also a very attractive research topic.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Regarding $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ -storage cathodes, the intercalation-type Chevrel phase $\mathrm { M o } _ { 6 } \mathrm { S } _ { 8 }$ is still the most stable benchmark cathode for evaluating other RMB components. Although various intercalation-type cathode structures have been designed and proposed in RMBs, the practical performance is very limited, arising from the strong polarization brought about by the high charge density of $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ . To be precise, the large polarization of $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ makes it difficult diffusion kinetic in the cathode hosts due to its strong electrostatic interactions with anion. Novel host structures and material regulation strategies are highly needed to further improve the Mg-ion storage capability and the Mg-ion transport kinetic of $\bar { \mathrm { M g } } ^ { 2 + }$ - storage cathodes. We have summarized multifarious material designs for intercalation-type cathodes in detail in another topic review, which will not be repeated here [15]. In view of the severe limitation of Mg-ion diffusion in high voltage intercalation-type cathodes, recent researchers also focused on conversion-type cathodes (such as sulfur, iodine, sulfides, and organic molecules), which went hand in hand with the development of Mg electrolytes regarded to be chemically unreactive toward conversion-type cathodes. However, these conversion-type cathodes (represented by sulfur) suffer from rapid performance degradation, caused by the shuttle effect of soluble cathode species, a thorny problem that also exists in the Li-analog battery systems. It should be noted that, in some organic cathodes and Mg–S batteries, electrolytecathode interactions govern the electrochemical performance through the storage of complex ions such as $\mathrm { M g C l } ^ { + }$ [194] or inadvertent parasitic reactions with the cathode current collector [196]. These metamorphic concepts should be strictly distinguished in future research works. In addition to in- trinsic material properties (i.e., Mg-ions diffusion in insertion cathodes or structural designs in conversion cathodes), key factors associated with high energy barriers resulting from strong coordination between $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ and anion or solvent, or electrolyte-induced cathode surface passivation are rarely addressed and remain mostly overlooked. Solvated Mg-ions need to be desolvated into bare $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ before entering the cathode hosts. Therefore, fully understanding the charge transfer process at the cathode interface is also a critical basic scientific issue for the development of high-performance Mg cathodes.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: With regard to Mg metal or alternative anodes, although Mg metal anode has unique advantages, the interface passivation of Mg metal anode and the morphology regulation of Mg metal deposits need to be paid more attention. The currently developed interfacial modification methods to Mg metal anode have greatly expanded the choice of Mg electrolyte components and significantly improved the electrolyte/electrode interface compatibility [197]. Also inspired by studies in Li batteries, the interfacial parasitic reactions that arose from the solvent or anion in various solvated structures should also be further investigated in Mg batteries. For example, varying concentrations of Mg salts or mixed solvents will form different solvated species, resulting in different interfacial parasitic reactions on Mg metal anode surface. In addition, diverse alloy anodes are also very potential alternatives by virtue of their lower reactivity with Mg electrolytes, but electrolyte/alloy anode interactions and the corresponding consequences remain a mystery [198]. We speculate the properties of the interphases on alloy anode surfaces also directly determine their performance stability during alloying/dealloying. After all, the successful use of alloy-based alternative anodes in Li batteries requires ensuring the forming interphases that support ${ \mathrm { L i } } ^ { + }$ diffusion and mitigate further electrolyte decomposition in the highly reductive anodic environment [199]. The interfacial modification of Mg metal or alloy anode must be considered comprehensively with the development of $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ -conducting electrolytes.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: As an integral device, the efficient operation of RMBs requires the combined action of electrolyte, cathode, and anode. In addition to the intrinsic properties of various key materials, a stable and friendly interface is the basis for the efficient synergy of various battery components. The discovery of $\mathrm { { \dot { M } g } } ^ { 2 + }$ -conducting solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that in-situ forms on $\mathrm { M g }$ metal surface has spurred the unprecedented knowledge of Mg metal anode [200]. Unfortunately, the detailed function, morphologies, chemistries, and evolution with $\mathrm { M g }$ cycling of those proposed SEIs remain mostly unknown. In addition, the function of cathode/ electrolyte interphase and the detailed desolvation process of solvated Mg-ions on the cathode side are also significant issues that need to be studied urgently.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The development of Mg batteries is still at the infant stage. More fundamental issues should be investigated to understand the basic mechanism of charge-storage and chargetransfer during charge-discharge process, which occurs at both the host materials and interfaces between electrolyte and electrodes. With the unremitting efforts, it is highly expected to practically commercialize the high energy-density and low-cost RMBs in the near future. We hope that this mini-review provides some clear research clues to investigate the scientific issues of RMBs, which boost the development of RMBs.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Since their commercial application, lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have been widely used in consumer electronics, electric vehicles, and other fields [201]. However, the present LIBs based on inorganic transition-metal oxide cathode materials are restricted by limited resources and specific capacity [202,203]. In recent years, organic electrode materials have received extensive attention as potential alternatives due to their high element abundance and structural designability, enabling the potentials to achieve cost-efficiency, high theoretical capacity, good reversibility, and fast redox kinetics [204]. Various types of organic compounds such as conjugated carbonyls, conductive polymers, organic radicals, organosulfur, imine, and azo have been applied as electrode materials in various rechargeable batteries [17,205–207]. Organic electrode materials can be divided into n-type (reaction between negatively charged and neutral states), p-type (reaction between positively charged and neutral states) and bipolar (reactions involving n-type and ptype) based on their redox reactions [207].

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In the past decade, the research on organic electrode materials has been focused on the molecular design of classical functional groups and expanding their application to various electrochemical systems. Unfortunately, disadvantages such as low electronic conductivity, high solubility, and low doping level restrict commercial applications of organic electrode materials in practical rechargeable batteries [17]. Many efforts have been made to conquer these challenges, such as building conductive networks to increase the conductivity, introducing physical adsorption and chemical polymerization to suppress the dissolution, using molecule engineering to increase the specific capacity [208,209]. Nevertheless, these strategies also reduce the ratio of active materials, blocking the electrochemically active sites, and elevating the cost of synthesis, reducing the overall energy density and low-cost merits of practical batteries. Therefore, how to realize the theoretical advantages of organic electrode materials in rechargeable batteries and simultaneously maintain the long lifespan are still urgent practical challenges for organic electrode materials. We suggest the future development for rechargeable batteries with organic electrode materials that should be focused on the following aspects (Figure 12).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: (1) Synthesis and application of lithiated organic cathodes. At present, most of organic electrode materials are used as the lithium-free cathode and need to match a lithium-containing anode such as metal lithium to provide lithium source, which inevitably bring the potential safety issues of batteries. Therefore, the development high-performance lithiated organic cathodes are of great significance to the construction of LIBs [210]. Lithiated organic cathodes are synthesized by chemical or electrochemical approaches. The oxidation and hydrolysis of lithiated organic cathode materials in air are the main factors that restrict them to be handled and processed in the same way as commercial inorganic cathode materials. In addition, the cyclability of lithium-organic electrode materials still needs to prolong due to the high dissolution in electrolytes especially in fully charged state.  (2) Development and utilization of biomass electrode materials. Many organic electrode materials are ubiquitous in nature or can be produced from biomass using green processes [211,212]. For example, electrochemically active dilithium rhodizonate $( \mathrm { L i } _ { 2 } \mathrm { C } _ { 6 } \mathrm { O } _ { 6 } )$ and anthraquinone derivatives can be derived or prepared from natural organic products in plants. The development of biomass electrode materials is conducive to achieving sustainable development, decreasing the consumption of non-renewable resources, and reducing the cost of electrode materials for rechargeable batteries. The search for electroactive organic molecules synthesized from biomass may pave the way for the next generation of rechargeable batteries.  (3) Application of organic electrode materials in solid-state batteries. The optimization of electrolyte can directly affect their dissolution behavior, which is an effective way to improve the cycling stability of organic electrode materials. In particular, the development of all-solid-state electrolytes may be an ultimate way to improve the lifespan of rechargeable batteries with organic electrode materials [213,214]. Issues such as low ionic conductivity and the interface failure caused by the volume change of organic electrodes during the cycling should be properly addressed before further applications of solid-state electrolytes in organic rechargeable batteries.  (4) Development of aqueous rechargeable batteries with organic electrode materials. Aqueous batteries have received extensive attention owing to the lost-cost, environmental friendliness, high ionic conductivity, non-flammability of aqueous solutions [215]. However, the narrow electrochemical window of aqueous electrolytes greatly restricts the choice of electrode materials. Organic electrode materials are more attractive in aqueous rechargeable batteries in view of their appreciate operation voltage and high capacity [216]. Unfortunately, many organic electrode materials still face the challenges of high solubility. Designing and developing polymer electrodes are one of the main choices for aqueous rechargeable batteries because they are almost insoluble in aqueous solutions [217]. Other optimization strategies in aprotic electrolytes such as composite electrode and electrolyte optimization can also provide references for aqueous batteries. In addition, aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) are also promising candidates for large-scale energy storage [218].

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Although some organic electrode materials have shown great potential for application, the development of organic electrode materials in rechargeable batteries is still in their infancy. In addition to the above directions, more efforts are still needed to engineer organic electrode materials from the aspects of commercial applications, such as thick cathode, low conductive additives, and high tap density. Through continuous progress on electrode and electrolyte design, material fabrication and engineering process, organic batteries will achieve their advantages of sustainability, high energy density, and low cost.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: To achieve the strategic goal of “carbon peak” and “carbon neutrality”, it is imminent to develop advanced grid-scale energy storage devices [219–221]. Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have dominated the market of portable electronic devices and electric vehicles [222]. However, the high cost and safety issues seriously restrict their application in stationary energy storage. Compared with LIBs, aqueous metalion batteries (AMBs) possess the merits of low cost, environmental benignity and high safety, which have been regarded as an ideal alternative to LIBs for large-scale energy storage.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Until now, various types of AMB systems have been successfully constructed. Aqueous alkali metal-ion batteries (i.e., aqueous LIBs, sodium-ion batteries and potassium-ion batteries) have been preferentially developed based on the background of conventional organic electrolytes [223–225]. Beyond these systems, multivalent metal ions as charge carriers can transfer multiple electrons and provide higher capacity under the condition of equivalent embedding sites, which is conducive to breaking through the limitation of energy density [189]. Among them, aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) are of special concern due to their high theoretical capacity and suitable redox potential of Zn metal anode since Kang et al. [226] first proposed the concept of neutral ZIBs in 2012. However, some common issues strongly restrict the development of AMBs. The water solvent in electrolytes leads to a narrow electrochemical window and limited energy density. On the cathode, the ambiguous carrier storage mechanism and structure collapse during the ion intercalation/de-intercalation process are intractable. Meanwhile, the corrosion and interfacial side reactions (e.g., hydrogen evolution reaction and/or dendrite formation) are inevitable on the anode. When assembling into full cell and battery packs, tailored manufacturing/integration techniques together with accurate life prediction and failure analysis are highly required. Up to now, how to realize the theoretical advantages of AMBs remains urgent practical challenges toward commercial applications. We suggest that the future development for aqueous AMBs should be focused on the following aspects (Figure 13).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: (1) Development of high-energy, electrochemically stable and cost-effective electrode materials. For cathode materials, intercalation compounds with short migration channels and robust structural integrity are promising to realize long-term and high-rate cycling, while well-proportioned pseudocapacitive behavior endows faster charge transfer compared with volume lattice diffusion and thereby improves the kinetics of AMBs. It is necessary to elaborately control the crystalline structure and composition of cathode materials to accommodate metal ions, especially multivalent metal ions. This can cause strong electrostatic interactions with host materials and realize high capacity and fast ion-insertion kinetics. Carbon coating and defect engineering are suggested to optimize the electrochemical stability of the cathode materials (e.g., manganese-based oxides for ZIBs) [227]. For anode materials, suppressing interfacial side reactions (e.g., hydrogen evolution reaction) and/or metal dendrite growth is highly required to achieve satisfactory electrochemical stability and highly active material utilization. Strategies of surface modification and structure/composition design on the anode should be further explored to stabilize the anode| electrolyte interface. Above performance enhancement relies on a fundamental understanding of the energy storage mechanism and structure degradation behavior via spatially resolved and/or non-destructive operando characterization techniques.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: (2) Design of aqueous electrolytes with wide electrochemical stability window and temperature adaptability. Despite the merits of lost-cost, environmental friendliness, high ionic conductivity and non-flammability, the narrow electrochemical window of aqueous electrolytes has greatly restricted the choice of high-energy electrode couples. Accordingly, highly concentrated electrolyte and passivation film-forming electrolyte additives could efficiently broaden the stability voltage and simultaneously stabilize the electrode|electrolyte interfaces [228,229]. Furthermore, the high freezing point of aqueous electrolytes leads to slow transport kinetics at low temperatures, while the Brownian motion of water molecules at high temperatures results in serious side reactions. Adjusting the hydrogen bond receptor in the electrolytes is an efficient strategy to reduce the freezing point and improve the ionic conductivity and charge transfer at low temperatures. Specifically, introducing $Z \mathfrak { n } ^ { \bar { 2 } + }$ or $\mathrm { M g } ^ { 2 + }$ to coordinate with oxygen on $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O }$ , adding high electronegative anions $\left( \mathrm { B F } _ { 4 } ^ { - } \right)$ , $\mathrm { C l O } _ { 4 } ^ { - }$ and so on) to coordinate with hydrogen on $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O }$ , incorporating organic co-solvents (e.g., alcohols) into the electrolytes, and gelling the aqueous electrolytes have been proven to be effective approaches [230–233]. Meanwhile, screening flame-retardant organic additives is promising to relieve the aggravated hydrogen evolution, side reactions, corrosion and self-discharge issues at high temperatures [234,235].

label: 概述
paragraph_context: (3) Design and assembly of high-performance AMB full Intelligent monitoring and lifeprediction  Figure 13 Prospects on aqueous metal-ion batteries (color online). cells. To realize high-performance AMB full cells, not only electrode materials and electrolytes but also key auxiliary materials (e.g., separators, current collectors, conductive additives and binders) should be well-designed. Developing ultrathin separators helps to enhance the energy density and fast charge/discharge capability of the AMB cells. Meanwhile, endowing the ultrathin separators with multi-functions (e.g., metal anode stabilization) is conducive to realizing compact and high-energy-density AMB full cells by maximizing the performance of each component [236]. Moreover, the long-term operation of practical AMB cells highly relies on corrosion-resistant current collectors, lowexpansion conductive additives and stable binders, although these components have been long overlooked in laboratory research [237]. Besides, more efforts are still needed to engineer the optimum combination of battery components during the configuration design of AMB full cells, e.g., thick cathode, high tap density, and low-content conductive additives. Establishing mathematical models involving momentum transport, energy transport, quality transport and electrochemical reaction facilitates a deeper understanding on the operation and failure mechanism of AMB cells, which helps to further optimize the cell configurations.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: (4) Integration design of AMB pack and battery management. AMBs are believed to be decent for grid-scale energy storage, while battery protection and management systems are of great importance for actual operation. Challenges such as the complexity of the capacity attenuation process and the difficulty in accurately evaluating the performance of the AMB module are rigorous. The self-discharge behavior of AMBs also needs to be carefully evaluated. To obtain battery modules with high safety, high efficiency and high adaptability, the characteristics of the AMBs under different operating and aging conditions, as well as extreme application environments need to be carefully evaluated. Life prediction and intelligent monitoring technologies are of high significance for realizing the application of AMB packs in smart grids.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Although significant progress in electrode material development and electrolyte design has been made, the practical viability of AMBs is still in the incipient stage. Through continuous progress on material updating and device engineering, more advances in this hot, attractive, and important area are expected; the AMBs will win safety, sustainability, and low cost in the near future.

label: 理化性质
paragraph_context: The growing demand for electrical energy storage has greatly stimulated the development of alternative advanced batteries [238]. In view of high safety, low cost, and environmental sustainability, zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) have become pro- mising candidates for future large-scale energy storage [239]. The unique advantages of metallic zinc, such as highcapacity density $( \sim 5 , 8 5 5 \mathrm { ~ m A h ~ c m } ^ { - 3 } )$ , low redox potential (−0.763 V vs. standard hydrogen electrode), and insensitivity to the atmosphere environment, have encouraged intensive interest in ZIBs [240]. The charge storage in ZIBs relies on migrating Zn ions between Zn metal anodes and cathode materials which are capable of reversible $Z \mathrm { n } ^ { 2 + }$ ion desertion/ insertion or reactions [241]. These components including the Zn anode, electrolytes, separators, and cathode materials directly affect the overall battery performance. In the past few years, the research on ZIBs has showed explosive growth, but there are still many challenges to their practical applications.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: For ZIB technology to be competitive on an industrial scale, cathode materials must possess large reversible charge/discharge capacities and maintain these capacities over extended cycle life. Although various cathode materials have been proposed, including manganese oxides, vanadium oxides, Prussian blue analogues, and organic materials [242], the development of ZIB cathode materials is still unsatisfactory due to their low capacity and/or low potential and/or poor stability. Developing cathode materials with high energy density and superior stability is the key to bringing ZIBs toward practical applications (Figure 14). Meanwhile, because of the narrow electrochemical window of aqueous electrolytes, it is equally important to extend the voltage window through electrolyte engineering to meet the needs of high-voltage ZIBs.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: On the other hand, the charge storage in the Zn anode depends on the reversible plating/stripping of $\mathrm { Z n / Z n } ^ { 2 + }$ , during which the Zn dendrite growth and parasitic reactions (e. g., hydrogen evolution and Zn anode corrosion) also hinder the applications of ZIBs and pose an obstinate threat to the operation stability of batteries [243]. Up to now, various efforts, including electrolyte engineering, surface modification, and novel Zn host design, have been devoted to improving reversibility (Coulombic efficiency of Zn plating/ stripping) and stability (uneven Zn deposition and dendritic) of Zn metal anodes. Some advanced strategies, such as lattice-match anode substrates [244], super-high concentration electrolytes [245], and the construction of robust fluorinated interphase on the anodes [246], have effectively overcome these issues. Despite these advances, utilizing Zn anodes still needs to be improved to further enhance the energy density of ZIBs.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: What is in our mind on the way to more practical ZIBs is as follows. (1) How we use the massive amount of data collected from button cells to evaluate the potential of materials for a practical ZIB or we should evaluate materials/strategies developed for a high-energy stable ZIB in a more practical way instead of button cell testing. (2) The Zn metal anode is annoying and considering the fact that no metal-based anode is utilized in rechargeable battery industry so far. Should we consider other types of anodes other than the metal ones for ZIBs? (3) Should we define ZIBs aqueous batteries, or we should try more with other safe electrolytes, even organic ones? (4) Considering the 2 V voltage of lead–acid batteries, what would be the target voltage of the advanced ZIBs?

label: 概述
paragraph_context: As an electricity-based society, the transition towards a climate-neutral electricity generated by clean energy requires transformative changes in the way by which we use electricity. Normally, the electricity produced by sustainable renewable energies is random and intermittent, which makes it quite challenging for its wide application and integration into the grid. Energy storage devices, especially battery technologies can store electricity, while, still can release it as needed, which has been identified as one of an irreversible technology for achieving carbon neutrality by realizing widespread application of renewables.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Flow batteries have been regarded as the key strategy to accelerate the shift toward sustainable and clean energy because of their advantages of flexibility, secure-safety and high performance. According to the types of redox couples in electrolytes, the flow battery can be divided into inorganicbased flow batteries, all organic-based flow batteries and inorganic-organic flow batteries. The vanadium flow battery is currently at the stage of commercial demonstration, and many vanadium flow battery demonstration projects have been contracted and installed recently (e.g., the construction of 200 MWh in South Africa announced by Bushveld Minerals in 2021, the successful grid-connected operation of 17 MW/51 MWh vanadium flow battery system developed by Sumitomo Electric Industries). In October 2022, the world’s largest 100 MW/400 MWh vanadium flow battery plant developed by Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences and Dalian Rongke Power was put into practice (http://www.dicp.cas.cn/xwdt/kyjz/202210/t20221- 031_6541871.html), which will accelerate the shift towards sustainable and clean energy. In addition to vanadium flow battery, the zinc-based flow batteries and iron–chromium flow batteries are currently at the demonstration stage after nearly fifty years of development [247]. Compared with traditional flow battery technologies, the next-generation flow batteries such as organic-based flow batteries have the advantages of diversity resources and adjustable properties [248], i.e., structure, redox potential and solubility, which makes the development of flow battery technologies more sustainable and affords new opportunities for energy storage applications (Figure 15).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Although many demonstrations with different scales have been successfully installed for vanadium flow batteries, the major bottleneck for its large-scale deployment is the use of relatively high cost of vanadium electrolytes. Thus, to achieve the goal of carbon neutrality, future gigawatt- or terawatt-scale deployment of vanadium flow battery requires the improvement in capital cost reduction as well as performance from the perspective of materials, stack structure and control system of a demo. Different from vanadium flow batteries, the zinc-based flow batteries using zinc as the anode possess the merits of high cell voltage, high energy density and low cost, showing promising prospects for distributed energy storage applications. Nevertheless, the major scientific challenges remain to be addressed, i.e., realizing a uniform plating–stripping process of the zinc couple on the anode to avoid the short-circuit caused by dendritic zinc, increasing the areal capacity of metallic zinc deposited on the anode as well as working current density to decrease the cell stack cost [22]. Since no single flow battery can satisfy all the needs of end-user, organic-based flow batteries have been sprouting up and attracted increasing attention. However, most of current reported organic-based redox couples were not stable in the atmosphere, which causes the organic-based flow batteries to work at an inert atmosphere. This intrinsic characteristic for organic-based flow batteries makes them developed at the proof-of-concept stage. Although the theoretical solubility of organic-based redox couples is usually, the solubility of organic-based redox couples in a real-battery test is still very low, which limited their energy density. Up to now, although many high quality-papers and reviews had been published and focused on the progress and challenges of flow batteries, the improvements in calendar life, efficiency, energy density, power density, capital cost reduction for practical applications remain urgently needed.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Driven by the requirements of practical applications, the enhancements in battery performance and capital cost reduction from the perspective of advanced materials (including electrode, membrane, electrolyte) and cell structure innovation become essential. For instance, developing electrode materials with high electrochemical activity toward redox couples or homogeneous property to reduce the battery polarization and realize the homogeneous redox reaction in the electrode, engineering membrane materials with high ionic conductivity and selectivity, long-term stability, ease of pilot scale to enable a high-performing devices, fresh chemistry in electrolytes to enable a longer service life in the wide temperature or current density range, are of the utmost importance. Additionally, more efforts should be devoted to the integration of commercial-scale flow battery stack, especially for those next-generation flow battery technologies.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In summary, flow battery technologies are cheaper, safer, and more flexible and adaptable, and have proven to be wellsuited for grid-scale long-duration energy storage needs. Although the past two decades have witnessed the significant progress of flow battery technologies, only vanadium flow battery technology has stepped into the stage of industrialized promotion. Zinc-based flow batteries and iron– chromium flow batteries have been in the demonstration stage, and challenges still need to be overcome to realize their commercialization and industrialization. Improvements in cycle life, efficiencies, energy density and power density remain urgently needed for new flow battery systems. Indeed, the development of flow battery technologies cannot be divorced from advanced materials and cell structure progress, which are necessary to push forward the progress of flow battery technologies, and further accelerating the shift toward sustainable and clean energy.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Recently, we have witnessed a growing number of successful examples where the computation and modeling provide fundamental understanding and practical design strategies for battery materials. By building models ranging from atomistic scale to continuum scale, the simulation and modeling plays an important role in establishing the multi-scale structure–property relationship for battery materials. Many macroscopic properties and phenomena of battery materials, such as ionic conductivity, voltage profile, cycling lifetime, chemical stability, are determined by material structures or the thermodynamic/kinetic interplay of these materials. Atomistic modelling, which falls on the microscopic side of the length scale, has demonstrated itself in fundamentally revealing these underlying mechanisms [249]. Besides, computation-driven, or data-driven approaches have been widely employed to screen or predict novel battery materials with desirable properties [250].

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: Despite the achieved success, computation-driven materials design also confronts multiple challenges. There is still a large gap in time and length scale between what compu- tation can achieve and experiments. For example, the typical system size in density functional theory (DFT) calculations contains only up to a few hundreds of atoms. While grain boundaries, microstructures, and interfaces can be of critical importance to battery performance, it is very difficult to model these complicated systems directly due to the size limit. Complicated processes, such as the charge transfer process at the interfaces, usually involves coupled chemical/ mechanical/electrochemical/thermodynamic/kinetic effects and are also quite challenging for modelling. Furthermore, batteries are a multi-component coupled system instead of a mere combination of a few battery materials. While battery material design usually focuses on improving a few target properties of a specific component, optimization at the full cell level is more challenging but lacking (Figure 16).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Machine learning (ML) has become an emerging tool in many interdisciplinary areas, including materials science. ML force field development has gained increasing attention in the past decade [251]. ML force fields are classical force fields that are trained on dataset generated from first principles calculations. Once successfully trained, they can achieve DFT-level accuracy but also maintain low computation cost like other classical force fields. In principle, they are generally applicable to any system that are of interests. ML force fields can be a powerful tool to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations and to extend the achievable temporal and spatial scale, which can potentially enable us to model and study complicated processes in batteries, such as electrode degradation, ionic diffusion, charge transfer, passivation [252]. Besides, ML has also been adopted to predict novel materials, or even to provide the optimization for batteries at the full cell level directly. We expect that datadriven approaches powered by machine learning would be an emerging paradigm for the battery development in the future [253].

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The performance of Li ion batteries (LIBs) such as fast charging, cycling stability, safety and energy density is intrinsically dependent on their components, chemicals and architectures inside, including the anode, cathode, electrolyte, current collector, separator and additives [204]. Many researchers have devoted efforts in seeking the best materials and architectures, in which advanced characterization techniques play an important role to discover the mechanism within [254].

label: 结构表征
paragraph_context: Among the characterization methods such as X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), secondary ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS), Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) has the unique ability to detect structure information with a resolution of sub-angstrom, which makes it suitable to observe the structure and the structural change of the LIB electrodes at atomic scale [255].

label: 结构表征
paragraph_context: The difficulty to imaging Li ions by TEM is that high energy electrons are less scattered by light atoms [256]. Also, Li species such as LiOH and LiF are easily damaged under the irradiation of high energy electron beam [257]. To solve the two important problems is the prerequisite for the Li detection by the TEM technique. Recently, advanced scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) techniques are developed to enhance the contrast of Li ions during imaging, including annular bright field (ABF), integrated differential phase contrast (iDPC), ptychography [258,259]. Besides, electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) provides “finger-print” information about Li distribution and chemical bonding [260]. To maintain the integrity of Li species during the beam radiation, cryo-TEM is applied to minimize the beam damage. Therefore, the composition of solid electrolyte interphase, which largely influences the stability of a battery, can be studied due to the ultra-cold environment [261].

label: 结构表征
paragraph_context: Exciting achievements have been made based on these advanced methods. Currently, most ex-situ TEM work has been focused on the element distribution, surface phase, defects and morphology of electrodes at different charged states [262]. On the other hand, it is vital to study Li ions’ transport behaviors inside a specimen including its site occupation and the changes of chemical environment during working [263]. This crucial transport and the evolution of electrode materials can only be studied by real-time in-situ TEM.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: TEM investigations on secondary batteries have provided profound insights about how the components of LIBs work during cycling. The roadmap in Figure 17 demonstrates the progress of analytical TEM and in-situ TEM for the LIB research. It is convinced that advances in TEM techniques could help guide the material design and structural modification, thus facilitating the improvement of LIBs. This review offers a feasible reference for researchers who are interested in understanding the fundamental material issues of LIBs.
