label: 概述
paragraph_context: The use of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs)-operated underground mining machinery has gained tremendous momentum as a result of their numerous advantages. This includes their high energy density, long cycle life, high voltage delivery, low heat release, stability, negligible memory efects, and low carbon footprint.  Battery  operated vehicles are also preferred in underground mines for their fexibility. They do not emit harmful pollutants during nominal operations, making the work environment safer for miners. However, thermal runaway (TR) incidents can occur which  presents risks to miners and underground infrastructure. Therefore, it is crucial to understand battery operations and their failure mechanisms. This article outlines the advantages of LIBs, the necessary precautions for their safe operations underground, the conditions and impact of  TR events, battery management systems, handling LIB fre emergencies, and the research opportunities to promote safer and widespread use.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Keywords Lithium-ion batteries $\cdot$ Thermal runaway $\cdot$ Fire suppression $\cdot$ Battery system management $\cdot$ Battery electric vehicles NIOSH National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health OSHA Occupational Safety and Health Administration Rechargeable lithium ion batteries (LIBs), also called secondary lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), are used widely as energy storage devices due to for their high energy densities, excellent Coulombic efciencies, low self-discharge, negligible memory efects, and long life-cycles (Kim et al. 2019; Deng 2015). They were first introduced by Sony Corporation in 1991 and have since revolutionized energy storage systems (Goodenough 2013). Contemporary LIB consists of a negatively charged electrode, called an anode, generally made of graphite, newer alloys, or transition metal compounds (Nzereogu et al. 2022; Goriparti et al. 2014). The cathode is, usually, made of a non-toxic lithium-oxide material (Yuan et al. 2011; Julien et al. 2014). A porous separator immersed in a non-aqueous electrolyte, made of lithium salts and organic solvents, allows restricted motion of the lithium ions from the anode to the cathode during the discharge cycle (Sheng 2007; Huang 2011; Lagadec et al. 2019). The ions move in the opposite direction during the charging cycle (Xie and Yi-Chun 2020). A schematic of the operations is shown in Fig. 1. The metal electrode in the electrolyte solution is covered with an insoluble thin flm, called the solid electrolyte interface (SEI), which acts as an insulator for electrons but conducts the lithium ions (Shreenag et al. 2022; Wang et al. 2018). The homogeneity and stability of the SEI layer afect the retention of battery capacity and its performance parameters, including self-discharge characteristics (An et al. 2016).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: LIBs were originally designed for low-power electronic devices, but are now being used in various high-power equipment as well. This is due to the scalability of the development of battery materials and the versatility of the packing arrangements (Ko et al. 2016; Ge et al. 2013). Largeformat LIBs consist of cylindrical, prismatic, and pouch cells. They have distinct advantages and disadvantages in terms of packaging, ease of connections, and monitoring (Saw et al. 2016). Many research works aim to improve electrode materials, electrolytes, and separator thinning for better voltage delivery, safety, and low-cost manufacturing and operations (Grey and Hall 2020). The rapid evolution of  LIB's rapid evolution is also supported by extensive research and development in their safe recycling procedures (Zubi et al. 2018; Fan et al. 2020; Heelan et al. 2016). They are already being used in large-format confgurations primarily for energy storage (Killer et al. 2020; Haruna et al. 2011). However, several critical problems must be addressed before the mining industry begins to implement them on a large scale (Meng et al. 2022). Some of the most important research areas are the development of battery management systems, better prediction methods, and an understanding of the evolution and suppression of LIB-related fre in thermal runaway events (Lan et al. 2022; Kamat 2019; Zhong et al. 2021; Panwar et al. 2021).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The safety of a battery is determined by its construction, confguration, operating conditions, electrochemical tolerance, and environmental conditions (Chen et al. 2021). Modern LIBs are safe under prescribed operating conditions, but a recent publication by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) reported approximately 25,000 LIB-related fre incidents spanning more than 400 diferent types of devices during 2012–2017 (Lee 2018). A thermal runaway (TR) is defned as a chain reaction in a cell with a rapid release of heat and smoke from a cell or a battery pack, that often transitions into a fre event (Finegan et al. 2015). This exothermic reaction occurs between the electrolyte and the electrodes (Wang et al. 2012; Chen et al. 2021; Wang et al. 2019). Usually, the reaction begins with a recombination of atomic hydrogen in the graphite anode that then leads to the destruction of the SEI layer (Galushkin et al. 2018). The degradation of the SEI layer could begin at a relatively low temperature of about $1 2 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Wen et al. 2012). It is often followed by cell rupture and explosive venting of combustion products. TR often occurs due to mechanical, thermal, or electrical abuse of the cell. Its propagation depends on the electrolyte properties, the power delivered by the battery, the charging rate, and the battery pack design. Large-format LIBs undergo TR with a complex, rapid, and violent exothermic reaction. Research on 50 Ah LIBs showed that their structural expansion is the frst step in a TR. This is then followed by several cycles of jet fames and stable combustion. The ignition was observed to occur at about $1 7 5 \mathrm { - } 1 8 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Ping et al. 2015). Since LIBs are designed to have a high energy density, controlling their dissipated heat is challenging (Balakrishnan et al. 2006). This paper summarizes the latest developments in battery technology that favor their implementation on underground mining equipment, TR thermal runaway events in underground mines, control systems, and the avenues of immediate research required for LIB safety.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Underground mining is an economical method of extracting deep-seated minerals and contributes to meeting the growing demands for renewable energy systems and other critical minerals for the sustainable energy transition (Nidhi and Atul 2022; Igogo et al. 2021; Laurence 2011). These mines are usually ventilated using artifcial systems that move a regulated volume of air to dilute the generated dust and reduce the miners’ exposure to particulates. Strategies to alleviate dust exposure-related diseases continue to be the major objectives for ventilation (Petsonk et al. 2013; Hoy and Chambers 2020; Entwistle et al. 2019). Often, diesel engine-powered or electrical equipment, including excavators and haulage systems using trailing cables, are used for several unit operations underground. These heavy highvoltage trailing cables are dangerous to the miners working around them and severely constrain the movement of the machinery. Moreover, underground operations are often not conducive to ‘human thermal comfort’ (Sunkpal et al. 2018; Roghanchi and Kocsis 2018). Heat stress in mines is a major occupational hazard (Lazaro and Momayez 2021). Therefore, removing miners from the active working face and protecting them from hazards is critical. One of the key steps in this direction is the feasibility studies of extensive automation and the application of battery technology underground. LIBs, which are high energy storage and low emissions systems, can be used to power several of these mining equipment. LIBs have distinct advantages, but any failure that leads to fre or explosions can have disastrous consequences in these operations (Wang et al. 2012). The following paragraphs describe the advantages of battery-operated vehicles underground.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: LIBs have high energy density required for long-duration operations, ofer operational fexibility, supply power consistently, and eliminate hazardous conditions for miners who work around trailing high-voltage cable-controlled machines. Since LIB-operated equipment also does not emit carcinogenic diesel particulates or excessive heat, it provides a favorable environment for miners. The following paragraphs explain the factors that support the implementation of LIBs in underground mines.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: High energy density is arguably the most important factor that has led to the rapid implementation of the LIBs in a wide range of small and large devices for energy storage (Aifantis Katerina et al. 2010). This, attributed to research on battery materials, has also enabled their rapid growth in transportation systems where weight is important for efcient long-distance travel (Bilgin et al. 2015; Turcheniuk et al. 2021). This will be critical for mining applications that will use large-format batteries, as the equipment is required to deliver high power for long hours. Transition metal oxides are usually used for their high energy density, notwithstanding some other drawbacks. For example, $\mathrm { L i C o O } _ { 2 }$ cathodes are now favored strongly in electronic devices despite their toxicity (Manthiram 2011). Research is now focused on the development of high energy-density electrode materials having a favorable operating voltage, and fast charging capabilities (Amine et al. 2010). For example, replacing $5 0 . 0 \%$ of graphite anode with $\mathrm { S i O } _ { x }$ increases the energy density from $5 1 3 \mathrm { W h / L }$ to $6 2 8 ~ \mathrm { W h / L }$ in the pouch-cell confguration (Choi and Aurbach 2016). Research has also focused on the development of new electrolytes to enable higher energy storage and faster charging (Park et al. 2021; Freire et al. 2016). The other important factor is the shape and packing of the cells within the battery modules. Conventional 18650 cells have volumetric energy densities of 600–650 Wh/L. This is about $2 0 \%$ higher than pouch or prismatic cells, which are often preferred for their fexibility in packing (Duduta et al. 2011). However, modern LIB designs continue to follow the original design where power evacuation components occupy a substantial volume; this provides several opportunities for optimization.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Battery systems will also provide signifcant fexibility to machines that are restricted by the reach of electrical power cables. The deployment of these cables is regulated, especially in the underground coal mines (MSHA 2021). They also pose a safety hazard when damaged or not handled properly (Tripathy and Ala 2018). According to a NIOSH study, the most common equipment involved in electrical accidents are switchgear and trailing cables. More accidents were reported in coal mines compared to non-coal operations (Homce and Cawley 2013). In addition, untethered battery-powered vehicles are faster which enhances mine productivity. Powering excavators and trucks using LIBs would allow signifcantly better maneuverability in an underground operation (Paraszczak et al. 2014). In addition, the expenditure on developed infrastructure is signifcantly reduced since transformers, power centers, and other devices are not required. The installation of battery charging station underground allows the improvement of the operation efciency of the equipment, as travel to the surface is minimized. Travel for charging does not contribute to actual production and lowers the machine productivity during the scheduled time (Raf et al. 2020).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Traditionally, diesel-powered machines are used in underground mining operations for their efcacy and fexibility. However, they emit diesel particulate matter (DPM) as combustion products from their engine exhausts, which are dangerous compared to gasoline engine emissions (Ristovski et al. 2012a, b). DPMs are complex mixtures of solid particulates, liquid aerosols, and vapors (Eric and Hart Jaime 2020). They are formed as a result of incomplete combustion of diesel fuel. Their diameter is predominantly less than $2 . 5 \mu \mathrm { m }$ , making them respirable. Studies in animals indicate that their mass median aerodynamic diameter after agglomeration is about $0 . 2 \mu \mathrm { m }$ (Cheng et al. 1984). The primary mode of their transportation into the body is through inhalation (Jiaen et al. 2010). Their size, mass, large surface area to mass ratios, mixing rate, and coagulation properties infuence their transportation ito the human respiratory system. They are hazardous and their toxicity is a factor of their physical and chemical characteristics (Mohankumar and Senthilkumar 2017). The surface  adsorption of organic compounds has been shown to initiate processes that can lead to respiratory diseases (Ristovski et al. 2012a). These airborne particles travel in the mine assisted by the ventilation air currents and could potentially impact miners working away from the source as well. This has necessitated several regulatory bodies to adopt measures to control their exposure (Chang and Guang 2017). This has further encouraged the battery electric vehicles’ usage.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The safe operations of the LIBs and the supporting infrastructure are crucial for their underground deployment.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Since LIBs have high energy densities, it must be ensured that they do not become a source of fre ir explosion. They must be intrinsically safe, and their enclosures must be fameproof. A large-format battery for mining applications impacts the surrounding environment and vice versa (Fig. 2). Therefore, as shown in the fgure, the battery management system (BMS) will process the weather elements (humidity, temperature, etc.) and the operating conditions (such as the mining terrain, speed constraints, etc.) so that the LIBs always operate within the prescribed parameters. The following paragraphs explain the challenges that need to be overcome before their deployment.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Intrinsically safe devices are incapable of igniting the surrounding fammable gases. This is done by restricting electrical or thermal energy that might escape the enclosure (Dubaniewicz Jr and DuCarme 2016). All equipment used in the mines must be unable to produce  a spark that could cause a fre (Magison 1972). Coal mines follow even more stringent regulations due to the presence of highly fammable methane and explosive coal dust mixture (Cashdollar 1996, 2000). Intrinsically safe devices are designed to quench the plausible onset of the worst-case fault scenario during operations. Several features are built into the LIB packaging to prevent a sudden energy release that could lead to ignition. A mechanical safety vent is the most common device that alleviates pressure build-up in a cell (Swart et al. 2006). Thermal fuses, despite their inability to be reused, are also used as a protection device and are usually set to operate at $3 0 { - } 5 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ above the nominal LIB operating temperature (Balakrishnan et al. 2006). The fammability characteristics of the electrolytes and the electrodes play a critical role. For example, contemporary carbonate-based and organic liquids electrolytes are volatile and break down to release $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ . Inorganic and other polymers are signifcantly safe and alleviate lithium-dendrite growth (Chen et al. 2018). For example, a non-fammable fuorinated phosphate electrolyte $( 0 . 8 \mathbf { M }$ LiPF6/tris(2,2,2-trifuoroethyl) phosphate (TFEP)) is one of several proposed chemicals that shows excellent stability on the electrodes by forming an inert interface (Zeng et al. 2020). Although separators do not participate in the reactions within a cell, they are critical to their intrinsic safety, especially during any TR events (Liu et al. 2021).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: In explosive environments, LIB can act as a source of electrical ignition. NIOSH research showed that an internal short circuit in the spiral-wound Saft FRIWO M52EX $\mathrm { L i M n O } _ { 2 }$ cell posed a methane ignition hazard (Dubaniewicz Jr and DuCarme 2014). Any such TR events could be disastrous for a coal mine with a high methane concentration. Since a TR event could lead to the development of high-pressure conditions followed by a rapid release of several fammable gases outside of the enclosure, they must be installed in special chambers called fame-proof enclosures (Lingyu Meng et al. 2022). These enclosures have small gaps between the fanges that prevent the transfer of the efects of internal explosions to the external fammable environment. Holes are not permissible and all joints and threads must be corrosion-free (Keane et al. 2014). Usually, a test defned in IEC 600079 is performed to examine the ability of the enclosure to withstand high pressure (Krause et al. 2017). NIOSH researchers also provided recommendations for improvements of the LIB safety assessment criteria based on plastic wedge crush tests (Dubaniewicz Jr and DuCarme 2016).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Although the structural integrity of the chamber is crucial for the fame-proof characteristics of the LIBs, the battery materials including the separators play important roles in fame suppression. Most of the separators with fame retarding capabilities use inorganic agents like metal hydroxides that inhibit the chain reaction. For example, the addition of $\mathrm { M g ( O H ) } _ { 2 }$ to a polymer composite electrolyte improves the fame retarding properties. However, it is recommended that its concentration in the electrolyte is kept below 40 $\mathrm { w t } \%$ to maintain the mechanical strength of the cell (Kim et al. 2017). Composite microfber and nanofber separators developed through the electrospinning process also show enhanced fame-retardant properties in LIBs in addition to enhancing electrochemical efcacy (Liu et al. 2017; Chen et al. 2020).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Underground mines are dynamic environments in which several high-power machines work systematically in a constrained layout. High capacity LIBs are expected to be deployed on several of these pieces of equipment. The latest research on the development of Nickel-based cathodic materials, including $\mathrm { L i N i _ { 0 \cdot 8 } C o _ { 0 \cdot 1 } M n _ { 0 \cdot 1 } O _ { 2 } }$ (NCM811), $\mathrm { L i N i _ { 0 \cdot 6 } C o _ { 0 \cdot 2 } M n _ { 0 \cdot 2 } O _ { 2 } }$ (NCM622), and several others that pack a much higher energy density required for these applications has been successful (Feng et al. 2018). However, these materials could be hazardous and will enhance the TR severity (Fig. 3). TR could result from mechanical damage, exposure to temperature and humidity, and overcharging, in addition to several other factors described in the following paragraphs.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: A collision of mobile equipment underground may cause mechanical damage that could  lead to an internal shortcircuit or failure of the casing failure. The diferent  components of a large-format battery, including the cells, modules, and packs, are most likely to be exposed to shocks and vibrations (Liu et al. 2020). This may lead to electrode damage and electrolyte leakage under hot conditions. Depending on its severity, this can quickly transition into TR events. They are incredibly difcult to reproduce in a laboratory setting. In a NIOSH research to investigate the failure of LIBs due to internal short circuit, cylindrical $\mathrm { L i C o O } _ { 2 }$ and ${ \mathrm { L i F e P O } } _ { 4 }$ cells were crushed using a plastic wedge in a 20.0 l methane chamber to mimic equipment collision. It was observed that ${ \mathrm { L i F e P O } } _ { 4 }$ cells were safer and did not ignite in a $6 . 5 \%$ methane concentration. Other cells failed through TR in the methane environment (Dubaniewicz and DuCarme 2013). Further crush tests on prismatic $\mathrm { L i C o O } _ { 2 }$ and primary spiral-wound $\mathrm { L i M n O } _ { 2 }$ cells led to their ignition due to an internal short circuit. This would be a very dangerous situation in an underground coal mine (Dubaniewicz Jr and DuCarme 2014).

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: The nail penetration test is the most widely accepted approach to study the impact of mechanical damage to a cell (Chiu et al. 2014). Several research projects have focused on the studying the likelihood of explosions when a LIB is mechanically damaged. A research group built a 3D TR propagation model using empirical equations and validated it with experiments. The research showed that TR could be delayed by modifying the separator, improving heat dissipation, and introducing insulators between the batteries (Feng et al. 2016). Nail penetration tests on large-format LIBs, likely to be used on mining machines, are even more difcult to conduct due to the large volume of heat and gases that are released violently within a short period. A research group investigated the impact of nail penetration on a 6-battery module (25.0 Ah) with 47 thermocouples installed at strategic locations. The onset of TR was observed to take place at lower temperatures and at a faster rate compared to the tests where batteries were heated uniformly (Feng et al. 2015). It was also observed barely $1 2 . 0 \%$ of the total heat released in a battery can  lead to a TR event in the adjacent battery. Torsion also has a signifcant impact on the mechanical damagerelated TR as was indicated in a study on the large-format battery (18 AHr LFP and 25 AHr NMC). Peripheral torsion led to a voltage drop but the battery recovered quickly without resulting in TR (Wang et al. 2017). Therefore, the extent of damage and transition into TR is complex and depends on several factors, many of which need signifcant research.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: Underground miners and machines are often exposed to various challenging environmental conditions including a wide temperature distribution due to the mines’ geographical locations and altitudes. These conditions are not only detrimental to LIB performance, but they also restrict their applications (Hou et al. 2020). The most accepted temperature range suitable to LIB operations is often regarded as $- 2 0$ to $6 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Ma et al. 2018). Their performance is severely restricted at low temperatures because the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte decreases, the kinetics of the interfacial reaction is sluggish  , ${ \mathrm { L i } } ^ { + }$ difusion is slowed, and Li is deposited on the anode causing a short circuit (Zhang et al. 2022). Research has established that there is no change in the charging characteristics in the $2 0 { - } 4 0 \ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ range, but they deteriorate at temperatures under $2 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Lu et al. 2019). At $- 2 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ , ionic conductivity diminishes, and the anode electrolyte resistance increases, severely reducing the power delivery (Ji et al. 2013). Another research showed that the state of charge of the LIBs also reduced to $7 \% - 2 3 \%$ of the initial value at low temperatures (Aris and Shabani 2017).

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: In contrast, even under nominal working conditions, it might not be possible to safely remove the heat generated in a large battery pack on a hot day. This results in a deterioration of LIB performance. The kinetics and exothermic nature of LIB chemical reactions favor the rapid increase in reaction rate with an increase in temperature. This increases the likelihood of TR (Hou et al. 2020). The collapse of SEI at high temperatures is followed by the short circuit of electrodes, melting of the separator, and other chemical reactions involving the electrodes and the electrolyte (Ping et al. 2014). The LIB electrolyte, $\mathrm { L I P F } _ { 6 }$ in organic carbonates, decomposes into carbon dioxide and other compounds at moderate $( 8 5 - 1 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } )$ temperatures; this was demonstrated in research using multinuclear magnetic spectroscopy and other tools (Campion et  al. 2005). Studies were carried out on a 25 Ah NCM battery by heating it and terminating the heat supply at a temperature that does not force it to undergo TR. The module was rendered unusable once its temperature reached $1 4 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ due to an exponential rise in its Ohmic resistance. Further, the battery capacity can degrade by up to $2 0 \%$ when exposed to temperatures near $1 2 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Feng et al. 2014). Similar research on 50 Ah $\mathrm { L i N i } _ { x }$ $\mathrm { C o } _ { y } \mathrm { M n } _ { 1 } - { } _ { x } - { } _ { y } \mathrm { O } _ { 2 } / \xi$ graphite batteries with a $1 0 0 \%$ state of charge shows that TR could be avoided if heat is dissipated quickly before $1 2 6 . 5 \mathrm { - } 1 3 2 . 5 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ temperature is reached. The research also showed that heating power strongly infuences heat release, gas emissions, and total mass loss (Wang et al. 2019). Another research on Sony 18650 cells showed a systematic decay in the capacity when subjected to temperatures beyond nominal room temperatures due to progressive flm formation on the anode surface. The capacity fade was observed to be about $7 0 \%$ after 490 cycles at $5 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Ramadass et al. 2002). LIBs are also observed to age rapidly at higher temperatures. High SOC encourages several undesirable reactions at the positive interface that lead to oxidation of the electrolyte components that afects the LIB capacity (Michel Broussely et al. 2005). This leads to increased cell impedance. Research on commercial 18650-type cells with $\mathrm { L i _ { \boldsymbol { x } } N i _ { \boldsymbol { 1 } } } _ { / \mathrm { \scriptsize ~ 3 } } \mathrm { O } _ { 2 } \mathrm { M n } _ { 1 / \mathrm { \scriptsize ~ 3 } } \mathrm { O } _ { 2 } \mathrm { C o } _ { 1 / \mathrm { \scriptsize ~ 3 } } \mathrm { O } _ { 2 } / \mathrm { L i } _ { \mathrm { \scriptsize , M n } _ { 2 } } \mathrm { O } _ { 4 }$ cathode and graphite anode showed them to rapidly age beyond $2 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ , dominated by SEI layer deposition on the anode (Waldmann et al. 2014). Therefore, battery deployment in both low and high temperatures leads to performance degradation.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: High humidity levels are unfavorable for the storage and operation of LIBs. Their electrochemical performance rapidly degrades and is attributed to the formation of surface impurity layers in the presence of moisture. This was demonstrated for $\mathrm { L i N i _ { 0 \cdot 8 } } \varsigma \mathrm { C o _ { 0 \cdot 1 } M n _ { 0 \cdot 0 } } \varsigma \mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$ cathode material stored at room temperature and $6 3 \%$ humidity for one year (Zhang et al. 2022). Structural deterioration of nickel-manganesecobalt (NMC), widely used as the cathode material, was observed. Nickel reacts with moisture to lower its oxidation state, signifcantly diminishing the specifc capacity. Carbonates and oxides are formed that have lower electronic conductivity and reduce the electrochemical efcacy of the LIBs (Busà et al. 2021). Impurity species are generated with $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ and $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O }$ afecting their storage and cycling. Research has also shown that even the newly developed cathode material with high energy density, such as ${ \mathrm { L i F e S O } } _ { 4 }$ , degrade rapidly in the presence of humidity (Zhang et al. 2015). Electrode decomposition is rapid when the humidity exceeds $6 2 \%$ ; this is not uncommon close to the active mining faces. Similar performance degradation was observed for $\mathrm { L i N i } _ { 0 \cdot 6 } \mathrm { C o } _ { 0 \cdot 2 }$ ${ \bf { M n } } _ { 0 } . _ { 2 } { \bf { O } } _ { 2 }$ cathodes when subjected to $8 0 \%$ humidity at $5 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Chen et al. 2017). Therefore, prolonged LIB operations in humid underground mine impact their performance.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: The state of charge (SoC) of the battery indicates the energy stored in it, which, in turn, also determines the availability of the LIB-driven equipment. Depleting SoC is a major drawback of battery-operated equipment. A charging station is analogous to a closed-loop inventory system where depleted batteries are replaced by fully-charged batteries (Cui et al. 2023).  Currently, the battery swapping technique is utilized to minimize the delays involved in charging. A properly designed battery swap architecture can reduce operational delays to a few minutes (Ahmad et al. 2020; Vallera et al. 2021). However, it requires certain considerations such as heterogeneity in batteries, electrifcation, voltage transformation infrastructure, and monitoring instrumentation to approximate the SoC (Hao 2021).

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: A healthy SoC is required for any task that requires substantial energy; however, overcharging a module could increase the internal cell temperature which could lead to a more violent TR (Ouyang et al. 2017). Overcharging research on commercial pouch LIB showed electrolyte decomposition on the cathode and dissolution of the transition metals. Failure of the pouch and separator melting resulted in TR (Ren et al. 2019). Overcharging a cell could also quickly lead to the solvated lithium ions penetrating the separator via the electro-conducting process. This results in its failure with the release of gaseous products that can quickly overwhelm the mine ventilation system (Belov and Yang 2008). Research on 32 Ah prismatic cells reveal signifcant gas generation when the cell is overcharged to $1 8 0 \%$ SoC. The inside temperature of the cell can reach $2 3 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ ; which could lead to the melting of the lithium electrode. The temperature diference between the inside and outside of the cell can reach $1 4 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Yuan et al. 2015). Another research on a 38.0 Ah battery with $\mathrm { L i N i _ { 1 } } _ { / 3 } \mathrm { C o } _ { 1 / 3 } \mathrm { M n } _ { 1 / 3 } \mathrm { O } _ { 2 } / \mathrm { . }$ graphite electrode showed much more smoke when a module with a $1 0 0 \%$ SoC was subjected to TR compared to a module with a $5 0 \%$ SoC. Lowering the SoC to $5 0 \%$ also increased the propagation time of TR between adjacent batteries to 307.0 s from 87.0 s (Li et al. 2019).

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: Larger battery packs dissipate significantly larger amounts of energy, depending on their capacity. Experiments on lithium-ion phosphate/graphite battery packs of 50 Ah capacity showed a sequence of events. Battery expansion was followed by two- stage jet fames and stable combustion. Combustion abatement and quenching were the last stages. While the ignition occurred at about $1 7 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ , the fame temperature was much higher (Ping et al. 2015). TR started when the separator melted. The heat release rate and mass loss also increase with an increase in the SoC. Therefore, proper installation of charging stations underground equipped with battery SoC monitoring terminals is critical.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: A thermal runaway event in a large-format battery, likely to be used on mining machinery, is characterized by an uncontrolled rapid reaction leading to short circuits, combustion, defagration, and explosion. This leads to a drop in the output voltage levels and often violent battery failure. Externally, the LIB becomes a source of intense heat and gas release in a short time. These are undesirable and can quickly lead to unsafe conditions in an underground mine. The following paragraphs describe the impacts of a TR event in a mine.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: While TR starts in the $1 5 0 { - } 2 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ range, the combustion of diferent components in a LIB produces very high temperatures (Tran et al. 2022; Feng et al. 2019). For example, the redox reaction between electrodes causes a substantial heat release within a battery with $\mathrm { L i } ( \mathrm { N i } _ { x } \mathrm { C o } _ { y } \mathrm { M n } _ { z } ) \mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$ cathode following an internal short circuit (Feng et al. 2019). This could lead to a fre that can rapidly spread and cause disasters in mines. Several LIB explosion events followed by combustion have been reported in the literature (Zalosh et al. 2021). The temperature distribution dependence inside and outside the LIB is complex and is infuenced by several factors. This is attributed to a high heat release rate, which is the most important parameter that describes the intensity of LIB’s impact on the surroundings. Research on TR of a pack of 32 units of $1 8 6 5 0 \mathrm { L i C o O } _ { 2 }$ type 2,600 mAh cells with $8 0 \%$ state of charge showed a peak heat release rate of $4 4 2 . 6 \mathrm { k W }$ and temperature exceeding $4 0 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ ; this can easily ignite fammable materials (Chen et al. 2019). The fame temperature strongly depends on the state of charge. Maximum temperatures exceeding $7 0 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ were observed across all states of charge (0, 50, and 100) (Huang et al. 2015). Research on 25 Ah large-format prismatic LIBs revealed a wide temperature distribution with a diference of $5 2 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ within the battery, with the internal temperature reaching $8 7 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Feng et al. 2014). Tests on lithium nickel manganese cobalt (NMC)/ lithium manganese oxide (LMO) cells in pouch confguration showed peak temperatures of $6 1 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ which is much (about $2 3 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ ) higher than lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells. Furthermore, the reactivity of transition metal oxide in NMC/LMO cells also led to higher vented gas temperatures compared to LFP cells (Sturk et al. 2019). Studies on LIBs using an accelerating rate calorimeter (ARC) at NIOSH showed that NMC batteries generate peak temperatures of up to approximately $8 0 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ , while LFP peak temperatures are around $4 0 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ .  Research showed that the intensity of LIB combustion is also a factor of the supplied power, with a larger incident heat fux resulting in more vigorous combustion. A maximum temperature of $7 9 7 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ was observed, which can ignite adjacent cells leading to TR (Yangyang et al. 2015). Therefore, there are substantial diferences in temperatures that in turn infuence their impact on the underground surroundings (Tang et al. 2020).

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Although the cathode could be made of lithium and transition metal oxides, the anode is predominantly made of graphite. Electrolytes are rich in salts. Most of these are fammable which can exacerbate the ambient working conditions in a mine in a TR event. Although gases, some of explosive nature, are released from the combustion of battery casings, electrolytes, electrodes, and other components (Baird et al. 2020; Jin et al. 2021). The characteristics of the LIBs determine both volume and types of gases (Jia et al. 2023; Huang et al. 2021). The gases emitted are studied qualitatively and quantitatively in laboratory experiments under controlled conditions. An inert atmosphere is used during these tests to prevent the ignition of vented gases. Gas chromatography, mass spectroscopy, and FTIR spectroscopy are often used to identify them. The detected gases include $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 }$ , $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ , CO, $\mathrm { C H } _ { 4 }$ , $\mathrm { C _ { 2 } H _ { 4 } }$ , and ${ \mathrm { C } } _ { 2 } { \mathrm { H } } _ { 6 }$ (Baird et al. 2020; Li et al. 2021). Gas emission is strongly infuenced by cell construction and type. LFP and NMC/ LMO cells produce $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ , CO, and volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Acid gases, Hydrogen Fluoride (HF) and $\mathrm { P O } _ { 3 }$ are also produced. NMC/ LMO cells produce signifcantly larger gas volume compared to the LFP cells (Sturk et al. 2019). HF is especially toxic; its concentration could be in the range of $2 0 { - } 2 0 0 \mathrm { m g / }$ Wh for the LIBs (Larsson et al. 2017). For reference, exposure to HF even at low concentrations of the order of 3 ppm is harmful to human health while 30 ppm could be deadly (Krebs et al. 2022).

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: Several cell eruption gases released during the TR sometimes react with air to generate other combustion products. The heat released during gaseous combustion could contribute to the severity of the TR (Mishra et al. 2022). The concentration of the gas components and their ignition temperature are some of the important factors that control the infammability of the mixture (Li et al. 2021). The gas composition is independent of the volume released during a heat plate-triggered TR event on cells with graphite anode and NMC cathode. However, the volume and concentration of the released gas strongly depend on the energy density and cell capacity (Koch et al. 2018). One of the research projects at the National Institute of Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) involved the heating of a Li-ion cell using an accelerating rate calorimeter. The experiments demonstrated that the NMC cell showed sharp exothermic peaks at $1 5 9 { - } 1 7 4 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ and the largest volume of gases compared to the LTO and LFP cells (Yuan et al. 2020). Ventilation of the battery pack signifcantly helps in the alleviation of TR conditions by diluting the gas concentration. This reduces the duration of their exposure.  This has been shown by lumped network and computational fuid dynamics (CFD) models (Wang et al. 2023). Experiments on NMC and LFP cells have revealed the emission of particles of 5.6–560.0 nm size; the size is a function of TR mechanism, battery chemistry, and several other factors (Premnath et al. 2022).

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: There have also been several attempts to quantify gas emissions during overcharging initiated TR. Gas chromatography (GC) and FTIR have indicated the presence of up to 14 gases. In one of such studies,  NCA cells were found to release a much larger volume of gases at $1 { , } 0 7 5 \ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ while LFP cells released lower gas volumes and attained a maximum temperature of $4 4 8 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Golubkov et al. 2015). This also includes a larger volume of CO and $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 }$ that increases the toxicity and fammability. The experiments also showed that the TR onset temperature of overcharged cells $\mathbf { \sigma } _ { \mathrm { { S o C } } } =$ $12 0 \%$ ) decreased drastically from $1 4 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ to $6 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ . Another research on LFP cells using $\mu$ -GC showed the presence of CO2 (47%), $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } ( 2 3 \% )$ , and $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { H } _ { 4 } ( 1 0 \% )$ gases predominantly in addition to other minor species; these form a fammable and toxic mixture. HF concentration was also found to increase towards the end of the TR event (Fernandes et al. 2018). Most of these gases are detrimental to human health and could signifcantly impact afected miners, especially in a confned underground environment.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: LIBs deliver their design voltage during their nominal operations. A change in their output voltage pattern is a strong indicator of battery instability. The voltage is rapidly reduced during failure and drops to $0 . 0 \mathrm { ~ V ~ }$ in a TR event. To study this, NIOSH researchers subjected fve commercially available LIBs to controlled heat in an accelerating rate calorimeter (ARC) in research. While LFP 18650 showed erratic changes in voltage patterns before failing, NMC and LTO batteries showed a sudden drop to $0 . 0 \mathrm { V }$ (Tang et al. 2020). Research on NCM622, NCM811, and LFP batteries showed that the output voltage rapidly drops to $0 . 0 \mathrm { V }$ about 2–8 s before the  quick temperature increase, indicating the TR event. TR onset could also be determined using the trend of the voltage change rate. The voltage reduction rate is low at the beginning which indicates the melting of the separator (Yang et al. 2022). Similar research on large-format LIB showed a sudden drop in voltage about 15–40 s before the occurrence of the TR (Feng et al. 2014). A recent TR research on hundreds of LIBs with various SoCs carried out using indentation tests showed rapid voltage changes indicating sudden energy release. The control NMC cell with $1 0 0 \%$ SoC showed the fastest voltage drop (Lin et al. 2023). Similar research on LFP batteries showed the temperature at which the voltage drop occurs at diferent SoCs is in the $1 6 2 . 3 \mathrm { - } 1 7 3 . 2 \ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ range. This was lower than the TR onset temperature. These research works show that battery failure and voltage drop occur before uncontrolled TR reactions begin (Liu et al. 2020). Therefore, voltage monitoring can be used to determine the general health of the LIB.

paragraph_context: Elevated pressures could impact the integrity of the battery enclosures resulting in cases of sudden failure. Explosion-proof equipment is defined in 30 CFR 18 and requires the enclosure to withstand high explosion pressures and must not allow any ignition of surrounding methane-air mixture in an underground mine. Elevated pressures could impact the integrity of the LIB enclosures resulting in cases of sudden failure. A rapid rise in pressure is observed during the TR event and is attributed to the release of venting gases and impact forces due to rapid oxidation (Jia et al. 2022). Experiments on 18650 batteries have shown this pressure to reach $4 0 \mathrm { M P a }$ when the material began to yield, although gas venting was observed at about $2 \ \mathrm { M P a }$ at a surface temperature of about $1 3 8 \mathrm { - } 1 5 1 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ (Mier et al. 2022). MSHA regulations require explosion-proof enclosures to have a pressurebearing capacity of 150 psig (10.3 barg). The external surface temperature must not exceed $1 5 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ $( 3 0 2 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { F } )$ . This is especially critical to any battery-operated vehicle deployment in an underground coal mine. However, in one of NIOSH’s research on a confined MH1 cell with $9 2 . 5 ~ \mathrm { m l } $ of free space, pressure  was observed to reach 232 bar. Inverse power relationships were observed between the free space and TR pressures. This will have significant implications for equipment safety underground (Dubaniewicz et al. 2022). Tests on lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) cells also showed an inverse relationship between TR pressures and free space. Resultant pressure values were close to 294 bar (4,260 psi) which could easily trigger methane-air ignition (Dubaniewicz et al. 2021). These results indicate that the battery housings need to be carefully engineered for their safety in a TR event.

paragraph_context: Mining Group recommends that the battery management system, thermal management, conditions and usage profle of the batteries, automatic shutdown, and several other critical factors must be considered while building battery-based operations due to the larger weight of the vehicles and their high power requirements (Group 2022). Battery management and control systems (BMCS) are a class of software-based algorithms that perform various tasks during real-time battery operation (Bergveld et al. 2002; Plett Gregory 2015; Rahn Christopher and Chao-Yang 2013; Xing et al. 2011; Zhang et al. 2022). The algorithms typically operate based on feedback signals from measured quantities: terminal voltage, surface temperature, and applied current. These tasks range from monitoring, such as limit checking, internal state estimation, and fault diagnostics, to control, such as charging/discharging control and thermal management. Limit checking typically refers to testing whether the measured voltage, temperature, and applied current exceed their predefned safety limits. Upon crossing the limits, alarms are raised–sometimes followed by cutting of battery operations. Limit checking is solely a signal-based operation; no mathematical models are required. Internal state estimation refers to the process of estimating internal battery variables that are not measured, for example, Stateof-Charge (SoC), State-of-Health (SoH), State-of-Power/ Energy (SOP/E), and internal temperature. Fault diagnostics refers to detecting, isolating, and sometimes estimating anomalies in battery operation. These anomalies can range from over-charge/over-discharge type faults to internal electrochemical, thermal, and mechanical faults. On the controls side, charge control refers to applying a charging current to charge the battery to a desired state. Discharge control typically works to provide power/current demand by the operation—with some exceptions of intelligent constraint satisfaction type control. Within the battery pack, thermal and/or charge balancing of the battery modules or cells is also part of the control features. The thermal management task is to control the battery temperature within desirable limits–typically in conjunction with certain cooling mechanisms. Oftentimes, these algorithms work together to maintain battery safety. Internal state estimation, fault diagnostics, and intelligent controls are typically performed either by using models or data or a combination of both. A battery management system schematic is shown in Fig. 4.

paragraph_context: Battery thermal management is a key functionality of battery management. A typical goal of thermal management is to monitor temperature across the battery pack, raise an alarm if temperature anomalies are detected, and actuate the cooling system to reduce temperature and/or its gradient. Such functionality is essential since battery performance and safety depend heavily  on temperature. Battery thermal management activities can be broadly categorized into two types. The frst category focuses on developing real-time algorithms to monitor battery temperature and detect battery thermal faults. Examples of such algorithms can be found in several research (Lin et al. 2019; Sattarzadeh et al. 2021a, b). The second category focuses on designing efcient cooling strategies. Examples of diferent types of cooling systems include phase change materials, and air and liquid cooling (Feng et al. 2018; Olabi et al. 2022; Kim et al. 2019). Active temperature control and reciprocating cooling fows have been studied and have demonstrated to have better uniformity in temperature distribution ( $1 . 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ instead of $4 . 2 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,$ ) in the battery module (He and Ma 2015).

paragraph_context: Thermal runaway events result in the emission of several gases. Along this line, another potential aspect of battery management is monitoring gas emissions from batteries under various anomalous scenarios. This is crucial for mining applications since such emitted gases can adversely afect the exposed personnel. Starting from thermal anomalies (which can be caused by electrochemical, mechanical, and thermal abuse conditions), overheating, and fre can potentially initiate the release of toxic gases, including carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide (Larsson et al. 2017; Lebedeva and Boon-Brett 2016; Sun et al. 2016; Nedjalkov et al. 2016). Furthermore, combustion of electrolyte and/or electrode binder contents can lead to gases like hydrogen and phosphoryl fuoride (Larsson et al. 2017). Such gas emissions can be monitored by embedding electrochemical, chemical, semiconductor, and optical-type gas sensors (Cai et al. 2021).

paragraph_context: Other than detecting emitted gases, monitoring the mechanical response such as pressure or force inside the battery can provide certain diagnostic capabilities. This internal mechanical pressure has strong efects on battery performance and safety (Chen et al. 2023). The fact that the battery contracts and expands during charge and discharge leads to the stress/strain-related characteristics in the LIBs.  Such stress/strain behavior can potentially help to detect abnormal behavior arising from internal anomalies. This can be accomplished by utilizing in-situ thin flm sensors or cell expansion sensors (Chen et al. 2023; Mohtat et al. 2019; Kwak et al. 2021).

paragraph_context: TRs are low-frequency but high-impact events. Therefore, battery safety and thermal stability are critical for any application in underground mines. Although uncommon, fres are extremely difcult to extinguish once the battery is in the TR phase. This is because the fuel, ignition temperature, and oxygen for combustion could be provided by the battery itself. This leads to a highly exothermic reaction and generation of a large amount of gases (Ren et al. 2017). Therefore, smothering and cooling of fre cannot be implemented efciently. Most research has focused on the development of battery materials for improvement in LIB performance and lowering of costs in commercial applications (Chombo and Laoonual 2020). The following paragraphs describe the inherent safety features in LIBs, fre suppression agents, and personnel protection to be used in cases of LIB fres in underground mines. Figure 5 shows a schematic of the built-in safety features of a LIB and the external chemical agents that can suppress the fre.

paragraph_context: The large-scale commercial application of the LIBs will be driven by high-energy density and safe battery materials. LFP LIBs re commonly used for many applications due to their superior thermal stability, low cost, environment friendliness, and long cycle life. For example, their capacities have been further enhanced by controlling the constituent particle sizes, and their surface modifcation by coating with carbon nanostructures (Ahsan et al. 2021). Three-dimensional thermal models show that ${ \mathrm { L i F e P O } } _ { 4 }$ cells have the best thermal stability when compared to other cathode materials (Peng and Jiang 2016). Graphite and silicon composites, thermally stable materials, are commonly used in anodes (Xiangkun et al. 2019). Polymer separators with good mechanical and thermal stability have been developed that prevent short-circuits between the electrodes, yet allow the ions to move efciently (Jiang et al. 2017; Mohanty et al. 2016). LIB electrolytes, with additives such as  lithium hexafuorophosphate $\mathrm { ( L i P F _ { 6 } ) }$ , are fammable. Therefore, electrolyte additives are used to improve the SEI layer, protect the cathode, and stabilize the $\mathrm { L i P F } _ { 6 }$ salt (Zhang 2006; Pushparaj et al. 2023). Stable lithium salts like lithium bis(oxalate) borate, fame retardants, overcharge protection additives, and several other chemicals are used to enhance its stability (Wang et al. 2019; Zhenrong et al. 2006; Yixuan et al. 2021). Additionally, there have been several eforts in the design and fabrication of the electrodes to improve the temperature distribution (Xiangkun et al. 2019). Reducing the risk of cell wall failure, efcient removal of heat through better heat sinks, protecting the adjacent cells from the failed cells, and restricting the fames within the battery enclosure are the most recommended to reduce hazards from a single-cell TR event (Darcy 2016).

paragraph_context: LIBs contain several devices and mechanisms like current interruption units, safety fuses, and positive temperature coefcient (PTC) thermistors to regulate the current (Balakrishnan et al. 2006; Tobishima and Yamaki 1999). Unwanted charging, which can lead to TR, could be prevented using diodes (Doughty Daniel and Peter Roth 2012). Safety vents are also provided to release excessive internal pressure while minimizing the rapid ejection of gases (Kim et al. 2017). The protection circuits integrated with the LIBs safeguard them against overcharge, over-discharge, and excessive currents and temperatures (Wang et al. 2014; Bin et al. 2021). In addition, passive fre suppression systems that work as barriers between the adjacent cells of the module have also been proposed. They dissipate heat and restrict the transfer of combustion products to limit the TR propagation. These will be critical in large-format batteries that will be used underground. A study has shown that a properly sized aluminum plate installed between two pouch cells in a battery module could prevent TR. While a $0 . 8 \mathrm { m m }$ thick passive plate failed to prevent the TR propagation in the adjacent cells, a $3 . 2 \mathrm { m m }$ thick plate did not result in TR (Li et al. 2019). Large-format LIBs in underground mines will require several of these safety features to alleviate TR occurrences.

paragraph_context: The noxious products of combustion resulting from a thermal runaway event dangerous underground. Therefore, an external agent must be applied to rapidly quench the fre. The most desirable suppression agent must have excellent fre extinguishing capacity and cooling performance to prevent re-ignition, low cost, good insulation properties, and should leave little or no residue (Zhang et al. 2022). The disappearance of the fames does not confrm the quenching of the fre since re-ignition can occur due to internal chemical reactions owing to higher temperatures (Park 2013). Therefore, the suppression agent must lower the battery’s internal temperature; this is usually extremely difcult since the LIBs are sealed and can explode violently during the TR. The suppression agents can be classifed into solid (such as, dry powders), liquid (such as, water, liquid nitrogen, and several others), and gaseous ( $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ , etc.) forms based on their states at nominal temperature. They are described in the following paragraphs.

Agents in the form of dry powder are the most widely accepted. Recently, a dry powder, $\mathrm { N H } _ { 4 } \mathrm { A l } ( \mathrm { S O } _ { 4 } ) _ { 2 } \mathrm { i } \dot { \mathrm { H } } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O }$ , in the form of an inorganic phase change material, was introduced. The powder decomposes as the temperature increases. The catalytic reaction of the active species suppresses the propagation of the LIB TR (Xiutao et al. 2023). ABC-type dry powder extinguisher is usually preferred (Wang et al. 2018). Its main constituents are $\mathrm { N H } _ { 4 } \mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { P O } _ { 4 }$ and $\mathrm { ( N H 4 ) } _ { 2 } \mathrm { S O } _ { 4 }$ (Zhao et al. 2021). The complexity of LIB fres in confned underground space increases manifolds despite the heat release rate being similar to that of a fossil fuel powered vehicle (Sun et al. 2020). The resulting toxic products of combustion and the tendency of re-ignition will impact the miners (Colella 2016). Research has shown that internal combustion engines and battery-operated vehicles release similar noxious gases such as $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ , $\mathrm { N O } _ { \mathrm { x } }$ , HCN, CO, and HF (Lecocq et al. 2012). Peak heat-release rates of up to 6.51–7.25 MW have been observed in BEV fres with the LIB pack generating approximately 1.54 MW (Sungwook et al. 2023). paragraph_context: The literature lacks information on LIB-related frefghting techniques in underground mines due to their minimal deployment; most of the information is currently obtained from case studies of battery fres in passenger car battery fres. Firefghters responding to electric vehicle fres usually immobilize and disable the vehicle and extricate the persons before attempting to extinguish the fre (Park 2013). Since LIBs could have stranded energy, frefghters, while approaching them, must exercise the highest levels of caution and preparedness (Bisschop et al. 2020). Water, in a large continuous supply, or other agents, are required as discussed earlier. High-voltage batteries require more water. EV manufacturers also recommend continuous monitoring of battery temperature using thermal imaging cameras for at least an hour after the active fre is quenched (Välisalo 2019; NTSB 2020). Also, damaged LIBs are required to be moved away from any combustible material. Firefghters must be equipped with appropriate personal protective equipment, including boots, electrically insulated gloves, helmets, face shields, and self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) (Park 2013). Their exposure to high concentrations of LIB fre products in underground operations increases the importance of SCBAs manifolds (Dorsz and Lewandowski 2022; Said and Stoliarov 2021; Fent Kenneth and Evans 2011). PPEs must be able to ofer protection from respiratory-related and electrical shock hazards. PPEs that can protect against water vapor to prevent the fumes from entering the skin are preferred (lisalo 2019). paragraph_context: Lithium-ion battery (LIB)-operated equipment shows immense potential for underground mining operations. LIB systems would make the equipment operation more fexible in constricted spaces. LIBs are also safer because they do not use acidic electrolytes that could harm human operators and the environment. They use several conventional safety devices and controls such as vents, thermal fuses, and safety casings. Several non-infammable electrolytes and electrode materials have been developed to prevent TR incidents. Cathode materials such as $\mathrm { L i C o O } _ { 2 }$ , $\mathrm { L i N i O } _ { 2 }$ , $\mathrm { L i M n } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } _ { 4 }$ , ${ \mathrm { L i F e P O } } _ { 4 }$ , and others have been developed; they are often coated with metal oxides like MgO, ${ \bf A l } _ { 2 } { \bf O } _ { 3 }$ , and others to lower the phase transition phenomena and improve their stability. Similarly, several processes have been developed to treat conventional graphite-based electrodes to improve their surface structures. This prevents the thermal decomposition of Solid Electrolyte Interphase (SEI) layers. However, rapid exothermic reaction with the release of toxic gases, in a process called thermal runaway, is a threat to their safe operations underground. These events are detrimental to miners working in confned spaces supplied with a regulated airfow. Several fre suppression agents have been proposed, with diferent levels of efciency. However, these might not be efective on a large-format battery that is expected to be used on large mining machines. Standard procedures to approaching and handling the damaged LIBs underground need to be developed. Furthermore, the impact of a large TR event on the strengths of surrounding natural and artifcial supports needs to be investigated for preparedness in an active mine, should an event like this occur.

paragraph_context: • A critical assessment of cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) for high-voltage cathode electrodes in Li-ion cells.  • Fundamental understanding of why interfacial interphase is important to electrochemical performance and further elaboration on how to design robust CEI interphase.  • Emerging theoretical simulations and advanced in situ characterizations helps to unveil the mystery of CEI are summarized.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: ABSTRACT The thermal stability window of current commercial carbonatebased electrolytes is no longer sufcient to meet the ever-increasing cathode working voltage requirements of high energy density lithium-ion batteries. It is crucial to construct a robust cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) for highvoltage cathode electrodes to separate the electrolytes from the active cathode materials and thereby suppress the side reactions. Herein, this review presents a brief historic evolution of the mechanism of CEI formation and compositions, the state-of-art characterizations and modeling associated with CEI, and how to construct robust CEI from a practical electrolyte design perspective. The focus on electrolyte design is categorized into three parts: CEI-forming additives, antioxidation solvents, and lithium salts. Moreover, practical considerations for electrolyte design applications are proposed. This review will shed light on the future electrolyte design which enables aggressive high-voltage cathodes.

paragraph_context: KEYWORDS Cathode–electrolyte interphase; High-voltage cathodes; Interfacial chemistry; Electrolyte design; Batteries.

label: 电化学性能
paragraph_context: Along with the transition to a net-zero emissions future, there is a consistently growing demand for high energy density lithium-ion batteries with high voltage and high specifc capacity [1, 2]. The simplest method to further improve the energy density of lithium-ion batteries is to increase the upper cutof voltages. Taking the representative $\mathrm { L i C o O } _ { 2 }$ as an example, the discharge capacity increases from 170 to 220 mAh $\mathbf { g } ^ { - 1 }$ by changing the upper cutof voltages from 4.3 to $4 . 6 \mathrm { V }$ [3]. However, creating a battery that can withstand high upper cutof voltages while maintaining low side efects is no small feat. Cutof voltage fuctuations accelerate interfacial reactions between the cathodes and electrolytes which will inevitably lead to serious consequences such as rapid capacity decay or even battery breakdown.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Since 2011, extensive works on cathode modifcation and electrolyte design have emerged in the hope of suppressing or even eliminating such interfacial reactions. There are multiple efective cathode modifcation strategies such as heteroatom doping and surface coating [4, 5]. Heteroatom doping was applied to stabilize the crystal structure of primary particles and inhibit the undesired electrode–electrolyte interfacial reactions [6–9]. Likewise, surface coating strategies including oxides, fuorides, and phosphates have been put forward to prevent electrolyte penetration and transition metal dissolution [10–14]. Atomic layer deposition and molecular layer deposition outperform various surface coating techniques, enabling controllable coating with atomic-level precision, excellent uniformity, and conformity [15, 16]. Conformal surface coating can be efective even under a high temperature of $5 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ : exhibiting capacity retention of $8 9 . 4 \%$ for Ni-rich cathode [17]. Another promising strategy aims to enhance electrolyte stability by modulating electrode/electrolyte interfacial reactions directly through electrolyte design. In the history of Li-ion batteries, the electrolyte-derived interphase on the anode was observed and defned as “solid electrolyte interphase (SEI),” which is a milestone [18]. In parallel, the interphase formed on the cathode is named “cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI).” The role of CEI was once overlooked because there is no thermodynamic driving force for electrolyte oxidation for commercial batteries operating within $4 . 3 \mathrm { ~ V ~ }$ [19]. The understanding of CEI becomes increasingly important due to the requirement of high voltage operation [20–23]. In situ formation of robust CEI via rational electrolyte design is the most promising strategy to separate the electrolyte from active cathodes and prolong the cycle life under high-voltage operation due to its ease of regulation by various components and self-healing ability. A review of CEI from the perspective of electrolyte design could provide fundamental guidance for further research.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: This review aims to recount the history of CEI from its concept evolution to practice, including the cumulative cognition of CEI compositions and formation, the latest knowledge about CEI brought by advanced characterizations and modeling efects, and the design principles of CEI especially from the perspective of practical electrolyte design, and future research needs on this topic. All the electrolytes in our review are liquid unless noted; otherwise, the discussion of solid-state electrolytes is not included in the scope of this paper.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Unlike SEI on the anode side, the important role of CEI was not realized until attempts were made to increase the cutof voltage beyond the oxidation stability of electrolytes [24]. It is academically accepted that there is virtually no thermodynamic driving force for electrolyte oxidation on most conventional positive electrode materials. However, this law only applies to thermal stability windows below $4 . 3 \mathrm { ~ V ~ }$ and fails when the cutof voltage increases.

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: In addition, the view that CEI is not present on the cathode surface below $4 . 3 \mathrm { ~ V ~ }$ was also found to be misleading. A lot of studies linked oxidation stability with the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy [5]. In general, molecules with higher HOMO energy are more vulnerable to oxidation, from which researchers derive oxidation stability higher than the actual value, leading to the conclusion that CEI is nonexistent under $4 . 3 \mathrm { ~ V } .$ . The new study, however, shows that the oxidation potential strongly depends on the local environment, meaning that there is no direct correlation between HOMO energies and experimentally observed oxidation stability [25, 26]. Therefore, it is more reasonable to use HOMO energy as a qualitative assessment of possible oxidation stability. In contrast, quantum chemistry (QC) calculation which takes the local solvents and anion environments into consideration is a promising direction for predicting oxidation stability [26].

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Analogous to the case of graphite anodes, when high voltage operation exceeds the oxidation stability limits of organic electrolytes, a robust CEI is required to suppress side reactions. Before discussing how to design a powerful CEI, a comprehensive understanding of CEI is necessary, which is a challenge due to its sensitive chemical nature, complex formation process entangled with both electrolyte composition as well as surface chemistries of cathodes, and the lack of reliable characterization tools.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: Pioneering works have been carried out to study the CEI even though the validity of the CEI concept was still doubted in the early 1990s [27, 28]. Selected studies show a brief historic evolution of the mechanism of CEI compositions and formation is presented in Fig. 1. A surface layer on $\mathrm { L i C o O } _ { 2 }$ was frstly suggested by Goodenough et al. through the analysis of impedance spectra in conjunction with electron microscopy observation (Fig. 1a) [29]. The composition of the surface layer was later investigated using an in situ Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and Fig. 1b demonstrates the presence of carboxylate groups on the surface of cycled $\mathrm { L i C o O } _ { 2 }$ thin flm electrode [30]. A bi-layer CEI model consisting of an inner layer of polymer/ polycarbonate and outer layer of LiF as well as precipitated species like $\mathrm { L i _ { x } P O _ { y } F _ { z } }$ , phosphorus oxides was proposed according to the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis of cycled $\mathrm { L i M n } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } _ { 4 }$ electrodes (Fig. 1d) [31]. Figure 1h illustrates that artifcial CEI of conductive polymer on Ni-rich cathodes can efectively suppress the undesired layered to spinel/rock-salt phase transformation and enhance the capacity under high-voltage operation [32]. Meanwhile, a LiF-rich CEI formed in the concentrated electrolyte can also stabilize the cathode structure and improve the electrochemical performance of lithium-rich cathode (Fig. 1i) [33]. One vital but debatable issue in CEI chemistry is the role of fuorinated species, such as LiF. On the one hand, less LiF was reported to result in a thin CEI flm with low impedance to enhance high-voltage performance [34, 35]. On the other hand, LiF-rich CEI layers have been well reported with superior cycling performance, especially with concentrated electrolytes [33, 36, 37]. label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: It is extremely challenging to fully understand the CEI formation mechanism due to the complicated CEI compositions which are still not completely identifed so far. However, a number of meaningful explorations have been conducted in recent years. Based on spectroscopic measurements and structural analysis, exchange reactions and nucleophilic reaction mechanisms were proposed for diferent cathode materials [28]. In the case of nucleophilic cathodes such as $\mathrm { L i N i O } _ { 2 }$ , the electrode is covered by ${ \mathrm { R O C O } } _ { 2 } { \mathrm { L i } }$ originating from direct reactions between the active materials and the electrolyte solutions (Fig. 1c). However, the existence of all CEI components cannot be explained by this mechanism alone, and more CEI formation mechanisms have been proposed later. As shown in Fig. 1e, Yabuuchi et al. raised a surface reaction mechanism where oxygen can be reduced to superoxide to attack carbonate solvents to form $\mathrm { L i } _ { 2 } \mathrm { C O } _ { 3 }$ [39]. It is worth mentioning that the cathode materials undergo surface reconstruction or reduction of transition metal oxidation state in contact with the electrolytes [40, 41], indicating the charge transfer between cathodes and electrolytes. CEI was found to be dominated by ethylene carbonate open-ring reaction activated by $\mathrm { P F } _ { 5 }$ derived from $\mathrm { L i P F } _ { 6 }$ decomposition (Fig. 1f) [42]. Other ethylene carbonate open-ring reactions initiated by electron-abstraction, proton-abstraction, and Lewis base were also discussed [43]. Shao-horn and co-workers found that the ethylene carbonate dissociation leads to hydroxylation of the cathode surface, namely the dehydrogenation reaction mechanism [44]. Importantly, the tendency of ethylene carbonate dissociation is strongly cathode material dependent. Proton transfer, also known as H-transfer reaction, between solvents on the cathode surface followed by solvent oxidation has recently been found to be universal [45]. The oxidation stability of common solvents including carbonates, sulfones, phosphates as well as ether signifcantly drops when coupled with H-transfer [46, 47]. Such a mechanism understanding shed light on manipulating the CEI chemistry by bringing specifc components closer to the cathode surface to facilitate desired redox reactions.

label: 概述
paragraph_context: CEI and SEI were usually studied independently as separate components on the cathode side and anode side. More attention should be paid to the correlation between the two, given that both are important components in the Li-ion battery system. Recently, it was revealed that the SEI transforms from a thick “three-layer” to a thin “two-layer” architecture by tuning the CEI surface chemistry via the amount of lithium bis-(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) additive, demonstrating obvious CEI and SEI interaction (Fig. 2a and b) [48]. The modifed CEI layer is composed of $\mathbf { B } _ { \mathrm { x } } \mathbf { O } _ { \mathrm { y } }$ species with extreme robustness against electrochemical abuse which can efectively prevent the transition-metal crossover, benefting the formation of a thin (O-enriched exterior layer and Li-dominating interior layer) SEI. Li et al. highlighted the strong interaction between CEI on high voltage $\mathrm { L i C o O } _ { 2 }$ cathode and SEI by quantitative XPS analysis of CEI/SEI components and evolution [49]. The CEI components only slightly changed with fresh Li metal or graphite anode replaced at the charge state, while the CEI thickness increased rapidly with the original charged Li metal during the discharge process, as presented in Fig. 2c. In another example, the generated gas species at a cutof potential above $4 . 2 \mathrm { ~ V ~ }$ was migrated to, and then interacted with the SEI layer, as verifed by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry measurement [50]. With the ongoing research eforts, increasing evidence has indicated the interaction between CEI and SEI [51, 52]. In parallel with Li-ion batteries, synergistically strengthening the SEI and CEI leads to ultra-stable cycle life of dual-ion batteries [53–55].

paragraph_context: CEI is dynamic during the charge/discharge cycling, and therefore, advanced operando characterizations are crucial to understanding the CEI evolution [56]. Changes in structure and composition of the CEI layer can be monitored by in situ neutron refectometry [57]. As shown in Fig. 3a and b, the CEI thickness increased to $4 8 . 8 \ \mathrm { n m }$ at $4 . 2 \mathrm { V }$ for sample (iii) and decreased to $3 5 . 6 \mathrm { n m }$ at $3 . 3 \mathrm { ~ V ~ }$ for sample (iV), suggesting a growth/dissociation of the CEI layer during $\mathrm { L i ^ { + } }$ Fig. 2 Schematic illustration of the interaction between CEI and SEI caused by transition metal crossover with a baseline electrolyte and b LiBOB-added electrolyte. In situ atomic force microscopy (AFM) visualized the morphological changes of the CEI layer up to a high voltage of $4 . 5 \mathrm { V } .$ , revealing that the CEI flms are only formed at the edge plane of $\mathrm { L i C o O } _ { 2 }$ crystal and decomposed at the discharge state (Fig. 3c) [58]. An operando-attenuated total refection—Fourier transform infrared (ATR—FTIR) technique was developed to study the dynamic mechanism of CEI formation in real time [59]. It was found that the addition of tris(trimethylsilyl)-borate additive can prevent the continuous decomposition of ethylene carbonate at high voltage and promote the stability of the CEI flm. Raman bands of CEI exhibited substantial dynamics in strong correlation with the state-of-charge of the $\mathrm { L i N i } _ { 0 . 3 3 } \mathrm { C o } _ { 0 . 3 3 } \mathrm { M n } _ { 0 . 3 3 } \mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$ electrode by a monolayer of deposited Au nanocubes [60]. Ideally, the in situ characterization techniques should bring minimum interruption to the operating cells and be under real operating conditions [61]. Learning from the anode side, in situ mass spectrometry and Cryo-TEM [62, 63], which dynamically investigate the SEI formation, can also be applied to monitor and visualize CEI formation. Emerging nanoscale X-ray tomography combined with artifcial intelligence and machine learning might be able to develop predictive models to analysis the impact of CEI on cell performance [64, 65]. All these techniques have helped us understand the cell failure mechanism. More importantly, we should try to guide the optimization of better electrolytes based on observations from various characterizations.

label: 机理/模拟
paragraph_context: Nowadays, MD simulations play an important role in investigating electrolyte solvation structure, the formation of CEI and its evolution. MD simulation applied in batteries can trace back to the late 1990s [66, 67]. Oleg and co-works investigated the interfacial chemistry on the cathode side using classic MD simulation with applied electrode potentials [45, 68]. On the cathode electrode surface, highly concentrated electrolytes were found to exclude the solvent molecules away and selected anions could be preferentially absorbed for decomposition (Fig. 4a). Density functional theory (DFT) in combination with ab-initio molecular dynamics was conducted to understand the electrolyte role in CEI formation, showing that an electrolyte with high fuorine content can induce a robust fuorinated CEI [69].
